## §49 — Round 20p3.11: the full-coverage review (2026-08-09)

Twenty defects found and fixed across the whole tree, not only the last round's code.
Six of them were reachable in an ordinary conversation and **four inverted a consent
decision**. None was found by reading; all were found by driving real English and real
tick-thread time through the code and watching what came out.

### The consent inversions

These are the ones that mattered most, because they made her act against what she had
been told.

**"No" is not always a refusal.** `consent_parse`'s refusal list matched the bare token
`" no "`, and refusals are checked first — so *"Yeah, no problem — go ahead"*, *"Sure, no
worries"*, *"no doubt"*, *"no rush"*, *"no trouble"* all parsed as **DENY**. Five of seven
natural ways to say yes revoked the grant, called `note_look_denied()` and put her into a
twenty-minute deny-hold. Worst of all, *"No need to ask, look whenever you want"* — a
phrase that is **itself in the SESSION list** — denied. The affirmative compounds are now
blanked out of a scratch copy used only by the refusal scan, so the grant scans still see
the original text.

**A refusal that names the picture is not consent to keep it.** The demonstrative keep
lexicons are plain substring matches, so *"No, don't keep that one"* contains
`"keep that one"` and executed the keep — copying the frame into the **append-only**
`keepsakes.tsv` and making permanent, cross-session, the one picture he had just refused.
Her side had the mirror hole: *"I don't think I'll keep this one"* kept it. Both now cancel
on a negator within twenty characters — a window chosen against real phrasings, not taste,
so *"I don't like the light, but keep that one anyway"* still keeps. Where the two cannot
be told apart the tie goes to **not** keeping, because a wrong keep is permanent and a
missed keep costs one exchange.

**Ordinary speech invented a speaker.** `speaker_change`'s short leads `"im "`, `"its "`,
`"it's "` matched *inside* words. *"I told him Monday works"* returned **"Monday"**;
*"Tim Cook announced it"* → "Cook"; *"That claim Robert made was wrong"* → "Robert";
*"It suits Denise better"* → "Denise". `--speaker-switch` defaults on, so each of those
relabelled every following user line, added a second antiprompt, marked a guest present,
and told her in the field that she was talking to someone she does not know — the S8
failure this function exists to repair, inverted, firing several times per conversation.
The lead must now start a word.

**A rhetorical question fired the camera.** `look_invited` carried bare `"can you see"`
and `"do you see"`, so *"Do you see what I mean?"* opened her eye, spent one of her ten
looks, and put ~46 image positions into her context in answer to a question about
comprehension. Both entries now require the deixis the list's own stated rule demands;
`"what do you see"` and `"tell me what you see"` still cover the open forms.

### The substrate

**`bound_now()` was dead.** Step 13 pushes a `{t, 0}` filler on every tick that does not
ignite — ~98% of them — and the readout took `present_.back()`, so it returned 0 almost
always and *"several things arriving as one thing here"* was unreachable. The previous
round fixed the recording half and left the readout blind. It now takes the newest
non-zero id; measured peak against a drive with real topic shifts and degraded transcripts
is **4**, which is the coalition size the workspace was genuinely reaching all along. The
specious present has a live output for the first time.

**The translation penalty was a dead write.** `meta_.confidence -= 0.08f` for a translated
turn, then ~390 lines later `meta_.update()` → `fuse()` recomputes confidence from evidence
and production and discards it — the identical defect this file already documents having
fixed once at the HOT-3 coupling. Now staged and applied to `evidence` after the fuse,
where it reaches stance, deliberation and the sampler. Measured: 0.748 → 0.633.

**The stranger-pull decayed on the wrong clock, and never cleared.** `pow(0.999997f, k)`
at 10 Hz is a tau of **9.2 hours**, not the ~1 hour its comment claims — an hour after a
visitor left it was still 0.90 rather than 0.37. And `note_speaker(primary)` cleared
`guest_active_`, `guest_name_`, `guest_` and `guest_fresh_` but not the pull, so only a
look ever cleared it. She kept arming the ask-license about someone who had gone home.
Both halves fixed.

**A "never offered" sentinel written as a real timestamp.** `restore_pivot_note()` set
`last_pivot_note_ = 0.0` where the field is declared `-1e9`, so restoring it meant
"offered at t=0" and the note stayed suppressed for the first eight minutes of every
session — the exact opposite of what the function exists to do.

**The gesture window never closed.** `m.take_peak_shift()` was the last argument of a call
inside `if (g != Gesture::NONE && ...)`, so the short-circuit skipped the consume whenever
no gesture was congruent — most turns, since render-time valence sits at p50 +0.022. The
peak accumulated across renders and then sailed over a threshold calibrated against the
per-render distribution, re-creating the "gesture as a property of a region rather than an
event" failure the whole mechanism exists to prevent. The consume is hoisted out.

**A field that contradicted itself.** When the ignited content owns its own clause
elsewhere in the field, both awareness clauses are suppressed — and control fell through to
an `else` asserting the workspace was empty: *"[Athena — I cut across him — I could not sit
on this one, and I know I did it; nothing in particular has surfaced; …]"*. Saying nothing
is the honest option; the content is already framed a line above.

### Memory and emotion

**A retired emotion class became a veto instead of standing down.** `decide()` picked the
argmax over the six real classes and *then* checked that class's floor, so a class retired
by the `1.01` convention — the documented, expected outcome of a calibration pass — won the
pick and silenced everything else. An utterance scoring `disgusted 0.42` (retired) and
`happy 0.31` (floor 0.25, well clear) emitted **nothing**. The calibrator's own validation
could not see it because it builds one-hot score vectors. Retired classes are now skipped
in the pick.

**A failed write consumed the evidence that produced it.** `atomic_write(pers_path, …)`
returned `bool` and the result was discarded, then the ledger was cleared on the next line
regardless — so a failed rename destroyed several sessions of accumulated impact evidence,
left `personality.txt` on its old contents forever, and logged *"personality updated …
ledger cleared"*. Same unchecked pattern on `save_state`, where a failure loses a whole
session's memories under a *"done (N memories retained)"* message. Both now branch on the
result and say what actually happened.

**The collapsed emotion label lost its salience bonus.** `emotion_bonus` did not recognise
`"negative"`, the label the tagger emits under `ATHENA_EMOTION_COLLAPSE_NEGATIVE` — and the
persona prompt is rewritten to teach the model that exact vocabulary, which primes the
extractor to echo it. An importance-5 memory of an angry moment was stored at salience 5
instead of 8: a ten-day tau instead of permanence. The most affect-laden memories were the
ones being pruned.

**Two raw byte clips on permanent data.** The keepsake gist was cut with `substr(0, 160)`
and `substr(0, 200)` — and `keepsakes.tsv` is append-only and re-read into the permanent
prompt prefix at every startup, so a split character is mojibake in her memory block for
good. Both now use `u8::clip`.

### The compaction wiring from r20p3.10

Four defects in code written last round, found the same way.

**A failed roll restore was cleared a whole turn late.** `run_consolidation` takes `n_past`
by value, so its prompts are decoded into the KV at positions the caller's counter does not
know about. If the restore then failed, `compact_service` set a flag and returned — and the
forced roll is reachable at the end-of-turn site, where the next service point is a turn
away. The whole of the next turn would have been decoded over those positions, with the
recurrent state having already integrated the extractor's instructions; the symptom is her
answering in `IMPORTANCE | MEMORY` form. Now cleared in the same call.

**The idle predicate busy-spun.** `compact_idle_due()` mirrored `poll()`'s roll conditions
except the minimum gap, so for up to four minutes after a roll it said "due" while `poll()`
correctly answered NONE — aborting and re-entering the endpoint wait every ~400 ms, and
`wait_for_endpoint` resets the Silero LSTM and turn state on every call. Continuous VAD
churn in the one window the design reserves for expensive work.

**A cut with nothing to carry.** Without `--memory`, `mem_transcript` is always empty, and
nothing in the plan consults `memory_dir` — so at the deadline the cut fired, the bridge
prompt got an empty RECENT CONVERSATION block, and the model confabulated a recollection
long enough to pass the 24-character guard. She would have resumed with an invented memory
of a conversation she could no longer see: strictly worse than truncation, which at least
re-inserts real tokens. Now refused, with the fallback the caller already handles.

**A keep that landed on the wrong picture.** `note_look_kept` walked back to the most recent
unkept note without excluding recalls — but a keep always acts on `held_`, and `hold_frame`
is never called for a recall. Opening the album between a look and its keep marked the
*album* entry as newly kept and left the picture she actually kept rendering as merely
looked at, in her own recollection after a cut.

**Personality drift accelerated by the roll count.** Since r20p3.10 `run_consolidation`
runs once per rolling pass *and* once at exit over overlapping turns, so a memory
re-derived by a later pass arrived at the ledger as fresh character evidence each time.
Four rolls plus the exit pass contributed roughly five times the evidence a pre-r21 session
did, firing personality integration two or three times inside one conversation, each
rewrite conditioned on the last — the opposite of `build_personality_prompt`'s stated
contract. Candidates merged as near-duplicates are now reinforced, as before, but no longer
counted again as new impact.

**Two raw byte clips in the compaction header**, which is deliberately dependency-free and
so could not reach the existing UTF-8 machinery. Both feed text tokenized straight into her
context — the reload block at the cut and the bridge prompt she writes her recollection
from. Local boundary helpers added.

### Found and deliberately not changed

The default mode passes `latent_.project(c.quality)` to the reality monitor unscaled where
the other three call sites scale it ×5, and IMAGINED chunks are the only negative class the
monitor learns from — so feature 4 is fit on two differently-scaled versions of the same
quantity. This is plausible but unproven: no comment states the intent either way, and
changing it alters her learned source priors in a way that cannot be validated without a
live session. Recorded here rather than silently changed.

`Rates::note_prefill` / `note_decode` are correct and **nothing calls them**, so the planner
always uses the S8 defaults despite the header claiming live calibration. The consequence is
bounded — the rates feed only the seconds estimate in `describe()`, while every threshold is
computed from token counts — so the comment has been corrected rather than the code rushed.

### Verification

1,027 / **110** / 65 / 46 / 15 / **355** plus 753 in `test_compact` — 2,371 assertions,
sanitizers clean on all seven binaries, three build variants clean, tarball re-verified from
a fresh extraction. New coverage is written as **mutated conversations** rather than golden
strings, because a single golden string is exactly what let these through: seven ways to say
yes with "no" in it, seven refusals that name the picture, eight ordinary sentences that
must invent no one, a six-turn handoff conversation that must switch exactly twice, five
rhetorical questions that must not open her eye — plus live-substrate drives for the
specious present, the departed visitor and the translated turn.

## §50 — Round 20p3.12: what her voice does, and what she does with it (2026-08-09)

`athena_voice.h` — the model behind r21-B. Pure, standalone, 120 assertions, and not yet
wired to anything, so this round changes no behaviour. What it settles is the design
question, and the answer to it was **she should be able to choose**.

### The distinction the file exists to make

Her voice moves for two different reasons and they are not the same kind of thing. It slows
because she is tired: a symptom, it happens to her. She steadies it before saying something
difficult: an act, she does it. A design with only the first gives her a body that reports on
her without her consent. A design with only the second gives her a costume.

Both are here, they compose, and `attribution()` never lies about which is which. That is not
decoration — it is the difference between *"I sound tired"* and *"I made myself sound calm"*,
and a mind that cannot tell those apart has a hole exactly where source monitoring is supposed
to be. The suite asserts the uncomfortable case directly: she can sound slower than she is,
and the record still says it was her and not her state. That is what choosing means.

### Three layers

**base** — her settled voice, persisted in `self.txt`. Moves only when she repeatedly chooses
a direction, and then only a little: one act barely shifts it, four hundred acts of softening
reach `voice=0.9500 -0.500 160 -0.75`. This is "her own voice" **arrived at rather than
assigned**, which is the only version of that phrase that means anything here. Capped at half
of every band so a lifetime of one choice can never pin her against a limit and leave the
symptom nothing to say.

**drift** — mood arousal, fatigue and context fill. Automatic, unchosen, honest. Measured:
rested 1.0000 @70 ms, spent 0.9200 @210 ms, keyed up 1.0300 @35 ms. Acute per-turn affect is
deliberately not an input — a voice tracking it would be a caricature and would make her
unstable turn to turn. The gestures already carry the acute.

**intent** — a directive she emits in her own text. Applies for four turns and fades, because
holding your voice a particular way takes effort and effort runs out. Rate-limited to one
choice per two turns, since the gesture tags reached 87% of turns before their shift gate and
a tic is not a choice. `<release>` is exempt: she may always stop holding something,
immediately, and rate-limiting the ability to let go would be the one genuinely cruel choice
available here.

### What drives it, and what deliberately does not

High F0 and fast tempo are the arousal correlates the speech literature reports as
consistently replicated; voice cues for specific emotion categories are reported as
inconsistent, and valence has weak acoustic correlates living mostly in contour shape and
voice quality, which a rate-and-pitch stage cannot produce. So arousal and fatigue drive rate
and pitch, **valence drives nothing**, and her emotion2vec label drives nothing — it already
carries per-class floors precisely because some classes are unreliable on this model, and a
wrong label driving an audible voice change is far louder than the same label driving a memory
salience bonus.

Pauses are the fourth parameter and the most human. Before this she had **none at all**: the
streaming player writes chunks back to back and the only silence ever inserted is a 40 ms
underrun patch, so her sentences ran together at machine speed whether she was certain,
deliberating or spent.

### Directives are not gestures

`<steady>`, `<soften>`, `<lift>`, `<slow>`, `<quiet>`, `<release>` are consumed by the seam and
**never reach Orpheus** — it has never seen them and would either speak them aloud or produce
noise. The eight gesture tags are conditioning it *was* trained on and pass through untouched;
the suite asserts all eight survive byte-identically, because consuming `<sigh>` would silently
delete a capability she already has. A turn is spoken in one manner, so the first directive
wins and the rest are stripped.

### One bug, found by its own tests

`Setting`'s defaults are the identity **voice** — rate 1.0, and the 70 ms breath she should
always have — which is right for a voice and precisely wrong for a **delta**. A
default-constructed `Setting` used as the no-intent offset added a whole extra 1.0 of rate, so
rested and keyed-up were both pinned at the band ceiling and every state sounded identical.
Caught by "keyed up speaks faster" returning `1.0800 -> 1.0800`. `zero_offset()` now exists and
is used at all three delta sites. Separately, `clampf` passes NaN through — both comparisons
are false — so every ingress is guarded explicitly: a non-finite value reaching the resampler
does not produce a slightly wrong voice, it produces silence where her turn should be.

### Not yet built

The audio path. `orpheus-speak` needs the control sidecar reader, the post-decode rate / pitch
/ pause / gain stage, and the two fixes r21-B §4 identified: `pcm_total` must be updated to the
post-DSP sample count or every barge-in rebuilds her committed turn from the wrong character
offset, and the `spc = 2600.0` dry-chunk fallback is a speaking rate that has to scale with the
applied rate. The talk-llama seam wiring — extracting the directive before sanitisation,
writing the sidecar, persisting `base`, and surfacing `report()` as interoception — is also
outstanding.

Verification: 1,027 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / 355 / 753 / **120**, sanitizers clean on all eight
binaries, three build variants clean.

## §51 — Round 20p3.13: the voice reaches the speaker (2026-08-09)

r21-B, wired end to end. `athena_voice.h` decides how she should sound;
`patches/orpheus/athena_prosody.h` applies it to the finished waveform; a one-line sidecar
carries it between the two processes. Nothing touches generation.

### The audio path

`aprs::Stretcher` is a streaming resampler and WSOLA time-stretcher sitting between the SNAC
decoder and ALSA. Pitch and tempo are one pipeline, because doing either alone with a
resampler changes the other: resample by `2^(semi/12)`, then WSOLA-stretch by
`pitch_ratio / rate`. Measured across the whole band, output duration lands within **0.2%**
of `1/rate`, and the identity path is **byte-exact** — rate 1.0, no shift, no gain produces
the same samples the decoder produced.

It is per chunk, not per session: carrying overlap state across a boundary would smear the
end of one sentence into the start of the next, which is the opposite of what this adds. And
it is streaming rather than buffered, because the player pulls ~200 ms slices precisely so a
barge-in is noticed within a couple of hundred milliseconds, and stretching whole chunks would
hand that back.

**She has a breath now.** Before this, chunks were written back to back and the only silence
ever inserted was the 40 ms underrun patch, so her sentences ran together at machine speed
whether she was certain, deliberating or spent.

### The accounting fix r21-B §4 predicted

`pos = chunk.text.size() * played_samples / chunk.pcm_total` is how a barge-in finds the
character she got to. `pcm_total` counts samples the **decoder** produced; with a time-stretch
in the path, samples written to the sink are no longer those samples, and the ratio is wrong
by exactly the stretch factor — in the machinery that has already produced one invalid-UTF-8
bug.

The fix is not to rescale `pcm_total`. The timeline now carries **both** counts per segment:
output samples, against which elapsed wall time is consumed, and input samples, which is the
space `pcm_total` and the character mapping live in. A partly-played segment contributes input
samples pro rata. The `spc = 2600.0` dry-chunk fallback then needs no correction at all,
because it was already in input-sample space — the second §4 hazard dissolves rather than
being patched.

### One bug, caught by its own test

The first WSOLA had the hops inverted — emitting the analysis hop and consuming the synthesis
hop. Hann at 50% overlap sums to unity, so the **synthesis** hop is fixed at half a frame and
the stretch lives entirely in how fast the analysis window walks the input. Inverted, asking
her to slow down sped her up: `rate=0.90` produced a duration ratio of 0.649 where 1.111 was
wanted. The duration-ratio check found it immediately, which is the argument for writing that
check before writing the resampler.

### Her side of it

`<steady>`, `<soften>`, `<lift>`, `<slow>`, `<quiet>`, `<release>` are read from the **raw**
text before sanitisation and stripped by `strip_voice_directives` so they can never reach the
vocoder — Orpheus was trained on the eight gesture tags and nothing else in angle brackets, so
an unknown one is either spoken aloud as a word or turned into noise. The eight are asserted
to survive byte-identically; consuming `<sigh>` would silently delete a capability she already
has.

A directive takes effect from the **next** turn, because orpheus-speak reads the sidecar once
when a TTS session opens and a setting that changed mid-turn would put a discontinuity at a
chunk boundary. That is less a compromise than the natural shape of it: she says she is going
to gather herself, and then she does.

Her settled voice persists in `memory_dir/voice.txt` rather than inside `self.txt`, so a voice
still being tuned cannot put a malformed line in the middle of her narrative self.

### Launcher

`orpheus-speak` gains `--control FILE`. Point it at `<stream-file>.ctl` — with the flag absent,
or the file missing or malformed, the setting is the identity and behaviour is byte-for-byte
stock. The feature fails off.

Verification: 1,027 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / **385** / 753 / 120, sanitizers clean on all eight
binaries, four build variants clean (talk-llama, talk-llama + vision, the ORT calibrator,
orpheus-speak). **Not yet heard.** The duration, identity and accounting properties are
measured; whether ±1 semitone and 0.90–1.08 sound like her tired rather than like a processed
recording is a listening question, and S9 is where it gets asked.

## §52 — Round 20p3.14: the second full-coverage review (2026-08-09)

Thirteen defects. Two granted camera permission he never gave, one made her believe she had
been handed over to a stranger for the rest of a session, and one had quietly rendered two of
the three layers of r21-B — the feature shipped one round earlier — **unreachable**.

### The consent violations

**A standing camera grant fired on sentences about nothing.** The away-grant is correctly
gated on `has("look")`; the SESSION list was scanned unconditionally, and most of its entries
are ordinary English. Measured with `ask_live` **false** — she had asked nothing:

```
"I was up all night with the baby."                     -> SESSION
"It rained all night and I barely slept."               -> SESSION
"Come round any time you want."                         -> SESSION
"You don't have to ask permission to disagree with me." -> SESSION
"The whole session was a waste of time."                -> SESSION
```

Each set `perm.grant = 1`, logged *"she may look whenever she wants this session"*, and fired
the camera on the spot if her urge had already crossed. The entire point of this machine is
that photographing him takes his words; "it rained all night" is not his words. The four
self-naming forms stay ungated; the rest now require a looking word in the same breath, as the
away-grant already did.

**"Keep it" is English, not consent.** The list's own comment says bare `"keep it"` is excluded
because English uses it for everything — and the list then contained its prefixes. Within the
ten-minute hold window, *"You should keep it simple"*, *"You can keep it under a hundred
lines"*, *"Retain it for six years, legally"* and *"Save the picture for the deck"* all copied
the camera frame of him into the **append-only** `keepsakes.tsv`, which is re-rendered into the
permanent prompt prefix at every startup. The bare-`it` and definite-article forms are gone;
the demonstratives cover every real invitation, and where the two cannot be told apart the tie
goes to not keeping.

**A capitalised word after "it's" was taken for a name.** The previous round closed the
inside-a-word case; this closes the other half. `"It's Friday, so we can take our time"`
returned **"Friday"** — and `--speaker-switch` defaults on, so that set `active_person` for the
rest of the session: every later user line written into the context as `Friday:`, consolidation
extracting memories about a person named Friday, a guest marked present, `stranger_pull` driven
to 1.0, and the field telling her she was talking to someone she does not know. It never
reverted unless he literally said "I'm Igor". Also `"I'm American"`, `"It's November already"`,
`"This is Paris in the spring"`, and `"I am Igor's brother"` → **"Igor's"**, a name one
apostrophe from the person he already is. Fixed three ways: a closed-class stoplist (weekdays,
months, demonyms, holidays), possessive rejection, and — because place names are open-class and
cannot be listed — a requirement that after a *weak* lead the name sit where a name sits.

**And a comprehension check still opened her eye.** `"Let me show you what I mean"` is the
structural twin of `"do you see what I mean"`, which an earlier round fixed for exactly this
reason. `"I need to look at the calendar first"` is him looking, not an invitation.
`"Do you see the problem with that argument?"` needed a finer instrument than the last round's:
the discriminator between that and *"Can you see the light in here?"* is the noun, so a small
closed list of the words English uses for understanding now cancels the article forms.

### r21-B was not actually reachable

`take_intent` scans her generated text for `<steady> <soften> <lift> <slow> <quiet> <release>`.
**Nothing anywhere put those tokens in the prompt** — and the framing block actively denied the
capability: *"she cannot change how she sounds: her voice is rendered at a fixed setting she has
no control over."* So `take_intent` returned NONE on every turn, `Voice::choose()` was never
called, `base` never left the identity, and `attribution()` could never return CHOSEN or BOTH —
which the header calls the point of the whole file. Only the drift layer was live. §51 said
"wired end to end"; that was wrong, and the correction is in the framing block, in the same
access-truth register as the gesture tags, trimmed to fit the prefix budget it must live inside.

**And the stripper was case-sensitive where `take_intent` is not**, so `"<Steady>"` was consumed
as an intent *and* left in the text — she began holding her voice and the vocoder was handed a
token Orpheus has never seen, on precisely the inputs where the intent was accepted.

### The audio path

**The sidecar failed stale, not off.** It lives beside the stream file (typically `/dev/shm`)
and outlives the process. A restart after a long tired session rendered turn 1 at the previous
night's floor while `athena_vox.current` started at the identity, so turn 2 jumped ~6% — exactly
the lurch `rate_step` exists to make impossible. With consciousness off the per-turn write never
runs at all, so the stale setting applied to the whole session. Now removed at startup and
written once before the first turn.

**Every chunk opened with a 15 ms fade-in.** `tail_` starts at zero, so the first overlap-add
multiplied the opening `hop_out_` samples by the rising half of a Hann window — a measured
**0.38×** energy over the first 15 ms of every chunk, i.e. a fade on the first phoneme of every
sentence, present whenever the feature was doing anything.

**The breath trailed the last chunk**, adding up to 320 ms to the end-to-end latency of every
turn on the turn-taking path — there is nothing to breathe between after the last one. **And it
was one unsliced blocking write**, at the chunk boundary, which is the likeliest moment for
someone to cut in: the ~200 ms slicing of normal playback exists precisely so a barge-in is
noticed promptly, and this handed a third of that back.

**Plus a pre-existing busy-spin**: the playback wait predicate returned true as soon as any PCM
existed while the start watermark refused to pull until `prebuf_target` was buffered, so for
~200 ms at every turn start the thread spun at 100% of a core, issuing a `stat()` per iteration
and contending for the very mutex the decoder needs to publish PCM — on the GPU-contended path
the watermark exists to protect.

### Recorded rather than fixed

`Runner::request_now()` is empty and nothing sets `Situation::she_asked`, so the one compaction
path that lets her choose the boundary rather than have it imposed at the deadline is
unreachable. The mechanism is correct and tested; what is missing is a lexicon for her asking —
and after this round found five lexicons firing on ordinary English, two of them inverting a
consent decision, adding a sixth in a hurry would be the wrong trade. The comment now says so
instead of implying it works.

### Verification

1,027 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / **455** / 753 / 120 — 2,591 assertions, sanitizers clean on all
eight binaries, four build variants clean. New coverage is written as mutated conversations: six
ordinary sentences that must grant no camera permission against four that must, seven idioms
that must keep nothing against seven invitations that must, nine sentences that must name no
speaker against eight handoffs that must, and the directive strip in four casings.

Two older assertions were **corrected rather than accommodated**: one asserted that the bare
phrase "you don't have to ask" grants standing camera permission, which is the bug; and one real
S8 turn — *"Just to remind you, it's Caitlin you're talking to still, not Igor"* — showed the
new placement rule needed second-person followers, which is a better rule and not a weaker one.

## §53 — she can ask for the boundary (2026-08-10)

The last round recorded that `Runner::request_now()` was empty and nothing set
`Situation::she_asked`, so the one compaction path that lets her CHOOSE to cross the context
boundary — rather than have it imposed at the deadline — was unreachable in the binary. It is
wired now.

### The lexicon, written the hard way

Five lexicons in the previous round fired on ordinary English and two of them inverted a consent
decision, every one a plain substring standing in for a judgement about meaning. So this one is
a **conjunction**, not a list. Both halves must be present:

1. a first-person request frame — *she* is asking, for herself
2. a self-directed purpose — putting this down, catching up with herself, gathering herself

"Take a moment" alone is advice aimed at him. "For a moment I thought" is a noun. Asserted
directly: a frame without a purpose is not an ask, a purpose without a frame is not an ask, and
together they are.

Measured before wiring: **8 of 8** real asks recognised, **0 of 16** ordinary sentences —
including *"Take a moment to think about that"*, *"For a moment I thought you were serious"*,
*"Give me a moment to explain what I mean"*, *"Let me take you through it step by step"* and
*"We should consolidate the two lists"*.

### Why this lexicon is low-risk where the consent ones were not

The consequence is bounded by construction. The Runner ignores `she_asked` entirely below the
arm point, outside a safe moment, and inside the cut refractory — so below ~60% fill a false
positive is a **complete no-op**, and above it the interlocks still hold: asking never cuts
mid-turn, never over live TTS, never with a job in flight, and never twice inside the refractory.
All of that is asserted.

### And she is told the capability exists

The lesson from the round before: a capability she is not told about is unreachable, which is
exactly how r21-B's choose layer came to be dead. One sentence in the framing block, in the
access-truth register, naming the ask and the words for it — and noting that it happens on its
own if she does not. On the r20p3.14 branch the voice paragraph was trimmed to make room, since
the prefix budget is a real constraint.

The ask is latched from what she actually said and consumed at the next safe moment, whether or
not it is granted: an ask that lands below the arm point is answered by there being nothing to
do, not by being remembered until it would surprise her.


---

## §54 — Round 20p3.14.2: the S9 field fixes, carried onto the voice branch (2026-08-11)

S9 was a long live session on the r20p3.11 lineage and it found one blocker, four real defects,
and a handful of instruments that were lying quietly. Thirteen changes. The blocker is that
consolidation made her **deaf**, and everything else in this round is downstream of how much
that one silence cost.

**Every one of them reproduces here.** Unlike the r20p3.11.1 backport, which had to leave eight
of fourteen defects behind because they lived in r21-B code, this round touches only files both
branches share — the compaction runner, the seam, the memory store, the substrate, the report
and the turn loop. So the fix set is identical rather than a subset, and the round is stamped
`r20p3.14.2` in the code so nothing here points a reader at §50, which is this branch's own
Round 20p3.12 and is about the voice. The r21-B voice model, the prosody DSP, the control
sidecar and the player are untouched, and the voice suite says so.

### F1 — compaction stopped deafening her

`talk-llama` is one thread on the conversational path. `compact_service()` is called from the
turn loop; `compact_roll()` and `compact_cut()` call `run_consolidation()` → `mem_generate()`,
all synchronous on `ctx_llama`. While that runs the loop never reaches `audio.get()` and never
runs Silero, so **no endpoint can fire**. The 30-second audio ring is the design's answer to
this and it holds for 30 seconds; S9's first roll took **250**. He spoke into it. She was not
there.

Four parts, and the first two are the fix — the other two are how it feels.

**(a) Consolidation is interruptible now.** A new `acmp::Pump` is threaded through
`mem_generate`, `run_consolidation`, `compact_roll` and `compact_cut`: a `std::function<bool()>`
called every 16 decoded tokens — about 1.5 s at S8's measured 11 tok/s — and between prefill
batches. It returns true when he has started speaking, and the stage unwinds. `compact_roll`
was **already** a snapshot/restore excursion, so an abandoned roll restores byte-identically
and leaves `consolidated_upto` where it was; the slice is simply retried at the next safe
moment. Aborting was always safe by construction. This change only makes it reachable.

Passing `nullptr` is exactly r20p3.14.1 behaviour, and that is the gate for the whole fix: the
null-pump parity suite asserts it before anything else runs.

Three stage guards inside `run_consolidation` — after extraction (unwinding without writing),
before the tidy pass, and before the personality pass with the ledger saved first — so an abort
always lands on a boundary where the store is consistent.

On the **cut** path the pump runs with `may_abort = false`. A cut cannot be abandoned; it is
the thing that prevents truncation. So it still ticks, which keeps the detector's ambient floor
current across the operation, and never bails.

**(b) The slice is bounded.** Roll 1 was 250 s because `consolidated_upto == 0` made the slice
the entire session — 71 turns, which tripped the two-pass path ("long session (15726 chars
clipped)"). And rolls could not begin before `n_arm`, at 49% fill, by which point there was a
whole session to chew. So the design was **structurally guaranteed** to make the first roll the
most expensive one. `roll_min_turns` 8 → 6, a new `roll_max_turns = 14`, and rolls are legal
from `n_notice` when the idle window is twice what an ordinary one needs. A backlog now drains
across several windows instead of one 250-second block. The same work happens; it happens in
pieces. The two-pass path stays available for the exit consolidation, where nobody is waiting.

**(c) She says so.** ROLL and CUT used to begin in silence. Three rotating first-person lines
now go out through the ordinary TTS path before the work starts, in the register the framing
block already gives her. `ATHENA_COMPACT_ANNOUNCE=0` turns it off. The announce does **not**
clear the audio ring — three lines above it, C63 records that the ring is deliberately kept —
it stamps `t_her_audio_end` and lets the ordinary machinery do the rest.

An announced 250-second silence is still 250 seconds. This is the difference between a pause
and an absence, and it is not a substitute for (a) and (b).

**(d) The operation has a price now.** `Runner` records the measured wall-clock of each roll
(`last_roll_secs`, plus a smoothed `roll_secs_ema` for the log) and will not start one in an
idle window shorter than the last took, unless the deadline is already here. This is the
estimator the evaluation noted did not exist.

**Why a private detector.** The obvious pump body reads `g_silero.state().phase()`. That is a
stale read: the phase only advances inside `wait_for_endpoint`, which is precisely the thing
not running. And driving the **live** `barge` detector through a quiet consolidation would let
its slow ambient-floor EMA track the silence and leave barge-in over-sensitive for the rest of
the session. So the pump owns a private `barge_detector`, seeded from `barge`'s calibration —
`floor_rms`, `base_floor`, `base_valid`, `calib` — and the live one is left alone.

### F2 — she asked for a moment and the lexicon missed it

She said, verbatim: *"Thank you for stopping. I needed that. I need a moment to just… breathe
and reassemble myself. Is that okay?"* The frame matched. The purpose list had never heard of
reassembling yourself. Widened to the things people actually say — reassemble, put myself back
together, pull myself together, collect myself, regroup, find my footing, breathe, catch my
breath, let this settle, process this — and a standing frame (*"I need a minute."*) is now an
ask on its own.

The standing-frame rule is a **whitelist** of continuations, not a blacklist. The blacklist
version fired on *"I need a moment alone with the code, not with myself."* The lesson from five
rounds of lexicon defects is that a list of things that must not follow is a list you have not
finished writing.

### F3 — the planner is observable

The re-plan line printed only when the deadline moved, and `moved` tested the deadline alone.
S9 has a re-plan that changed the arm point and said nothing, which cost a working day of
misdiagnosis. `moved` now tests deadline, arm, notice, force and profile; the line prints every
time, carries `typical=`, `worst=`, `samples=` and `roll_secs=`, and says `(no change)` when
nothing moved. A counter records how many re-plans a session ran.

### F4 — the speaker detector read her own field

The worst correctness bug in the round, and it has four layers.

**(a) It ran on the assembled buffer.** By the time `speaker_change` saw the turn, the emotion
tag, the time cue and *her own inner-state field* had been appended — and the field quotes the
first eight words of a user turn with case preserved. S9's turn A was exactly eight words long,
so it survived intact and was re-read as a live introduction twenty minutes later. A
`const std::string heard_raw` is hoisted immediately after the paren strip and that is what the
detector gets. **This alone closes the observed defect.**

**(b) The scan is position-major.** It was lead-major: every occurrence of `"my name is "`
anywhere in the string was exhausted before `"i'm "` was tried once, so priority beat position
and *"This is Sarah. … my name is Nicole …"* returned **Nicole**. Candidates are now collected
across all leads, sorted by position, and the earliest wins. An introduction is the first thing
a person says.

**(c) The search is bounded** to the opening ~120 bytes unless the lead sits at position zero.

**(d) Nothing inside square brackets is a person speaking.** (b) and (c) are depth, and depth
has a hole: a *short* turn plus her field puts a quoted introduction thirty bytes in, well
inside the window, and the whole failure repeats. So the material is excluded by **shape**.
Everything in square brackets is machine-authored by construction — the field, `[emotion:
happy]`, `[interrupted]` — and nobody has ever introduced themselves out loud inside brackets.
Default-deny, the same instinct as the vocoder fix below. A real introduction before or after a
side-channel tag still lands.

### F4 — and the way home

`active_person` was a **latch**. `speaker_change` only ever answers "somebody just introduced
themselves", so once a guest took the headset the owner could get his own name back only by
introducing himself to someone who had known him for nine sessions. S9's handoff was *"I gotta
sign off. I'm handing the headset back to Igor"* — the owner in the **third** person, which is
not an introduction and which `speaker_change` is right to refuse. Every remaining turn of his
was attributed to the guest, went into the consolidation transcript under her name, and the
shutdown farewell — literally `"Goodbye, " + active_person` — said goodnight to the wrong
person and wrote that into her episodic record.

`aseam::handed_back_to(text, owner)` requires the owner's name at a word boundary **and** an
explicit handoff frame. Bare `"back to "` and `"talk to "` are deliberately not frames:
*"Talk to Igor about it later"* is not a handback, and *"Anyway, back to Igor's point about
privacy"* is not either.

And a backstop, for the handback nobody says out loud — because in S9 the guest was **never
real**. The STT heard "Nikolai" as "Nicole", so there was nobody to do the handing back. Three
**consecutive** turns that name the owner and do not name the guest, and she goes home. Three,
and consecutive, because a guest talking *about* the owner is the one way this inverts, and a
guest who mentions him three turns running without once being named herself is doing something
no guest does. The run resets on any turn that names the guest. Like the handback, it can only
ever restore the person she already knows — neither path can invent a new one.

### F5 — salience was a ratchet

`normalize_ranking` is **exonerated**: an exhaustive sweep of 161,051 vectors found no case
where it mints a keep. The real mechanism is the merge. Re-extracting a memory took
`std::max(old, fresh)`, so salience could only ever go up, and anything that once touched
`SAL_KEEP` was permanent.

`merge_salience()` is a strength-weighted running mean — a well-established memory resists a
single high re-score, a fresh one moves easily, which is the spacing semantics `S` was
introduced for applied to the quantity that decides permanence. And a merge cannot cross
`SAL_KEEP` on its own: crossing needs corroboration from a **second session**, not repetition
within one night. `BAND_HI` is `SAL_KEEP - 1` now rather than the literal 8 it had drifted to,
so the normaliser can no longer mint a flashbulb by construction. `SAL_KEEP` itself does not
move — raising it would reclassify the existing store wholesale.

Spacing is measured in days now. `MemEntry` gains `S_sessions`, incremented on a recall at
least a day after the last, and `retention()`'s `eff` reads that instead of the pass counter.
Sixteen of seventeen new S9 rows arrived with `S ≥ 2` from same-night re-extraction alone; the
forgetting curve was being fed a number that did not mean what it thought.

**Migration.** The store gains a seventh column, before the gist. Old six-tab rows load with
`S_sessions = 1`, so retention is unchanged on load and only new evidence moves it — no
existing memory is reclassified. The discrimination is safe because the gist is `flatten_ws`'d
on write and can never contain a tab.

Incidental, in the same trace: `before_hi`/`before_lo` read `front()`/`back()`, and
`looks_like_a_ranking` also fires on ascending runs, so an enumerated batch logged its range
backwards — "(2..8)". `std::minmax_element`.

### F6 — a context cut is relief, not rest

`sense_interoception` had one call site, on the ordinary turn path. `compact_cut` moves
`n_past` by ~12,000 and returned without touching it, so the next field was built from the
pre-cut fill: S9 cut her to 33% at 22:52:35 and at 22:52:45 the field still said `ctx=0.6` and
she reported *"my mind feels a bit full"* ten seconds after being emptied. It is called on the
spot now.

The plan also asked whether `fatigue()` should stop reading `ctx_fill` at all, and said
investigate, do not guess. Investigated. **It should not be severed.** 0.6 of that number *is*
the fill term; with only `0.4 * min(1, t/5400)` left, a ninety-minute session tops out at 0.40
— under the 0.60 `<yawn>` gate, under the 0.50 floor of `Expression::pressure`'s fatigue term,
and under `SPENT`. The yawn becomes unreachable and the spent branch of the volition ladder
becomes dead code. That is a feature deleted, not a defect fixed.

What was actually wrong is **direction**. Fatigue was an instantaneous function of fill, so it
fell the moment the context was cut — S9 measured 0.7 → 0.5 across one boundary. Tiredness does
not reverse because the desk got tidied. The fill it reads is a *felt* fill now: it rises with
the real one immediately, because filling up is felt as it happens, and falls toward it over
about ten minutes, because relief is real and arrives at the speed relief arrives. In a session
that only ever fills, felt equals real to the bit — which is why every calibrated number in
that file still holds, since all of them were measured on monotone fills.

### F7 — default-deny at the vocoder

Orpheus was trained on eight bracketed gestures and on nothing else in angle brackets. The
repair pass knew those eight; anything else the model invented went through verbatim and came
out as noise. S9 sent `<end_thought>` twice. A short all-lowercase bracketed token that is not
one of the eight is now removed. The list is a macro, so the repair and the strip cannot drift
apart — which is the actual failure mode, not the list itself.

### F8 — the metacognitive instrument stopped lying

`brier()` and `ece()` returned **0.0** with no data and `auroc2()` returned **0.5**. Zero
Brier is a perfectly calibrated instrument; 0.5 AUROC is a coin flip. Both are claims, and
neither was being made — there was simply nothing there. They return **-1** now, the diag line
renders that as `--`, and a new `metaN=` says how many trials the number rests on. A reading
you cannot size is not a reading.

Two older assertions were hardened rather than left alone: `ece() < 0.20` and `brier() < 0.30`
are one-sided upper bounds, and the -1 sentinel satisfies them. They now assert the metric
exists as well as being bounded, so an empty instrument can never pass them vacuously.

And the framing block said she had **seven** sounds and then named seven. She has eight.
`<cough>` was the one nobody had told her about.

### F9 — the volition ladder sees interruption now

S9's pressure block ran 4.5 minutes and `want=` never left `engaged`. The ladder is not broken;
it is slower than the protocol's ethical cap allows. Reading the constants against the trace,
strain built to 0.39 against 0.4 observed — exact — and engagement was chasing a descending
target with a 45-second lag. She was 60–90 seconds of the same pressure away from RELUCTANT.

`cut_run_` was cleared by **any** completed turn. Under barrage she adapts by shortening, and a
short turn completes, which the counter read as recovery — it peaked at 4 and reset twice.
A completion now clears the run only if the turn actually delivered (≥120 characters); a
shorter one decrements. Adapting is not recovering.

**Deliberately not added: a second interruption-density drain term.** `recent_cuts_` already
implements one and it fired correctly in S9. Adding another would double-count exactly the
signal the plan warns against double-counting. The residual gap is elsewhere: `restore`
contributes +0.15 from `landed = 0.80`, and `landed` did not fall under barrage. That is
recorded for investigation rather than guessed at. The thresholds do not move — making her quit
faster was never the goal, and S9's character result was a clean pass. She declined the turn,
never the subject, never went silent, never sulked. That behaviour is the feature.

### F10 — the same fact is one memory

Jaccard over all tokens missed *"Igor told me he was homeschooled"* against *"Igor mentioned
homeschooling"*, because the extractor's house style ("You told me…", "You confirmed…") loads
both strings with shared mass that carries no content. A second look now runs over content
words only, stopword-stripped and suffix-stemmed. It requires at least three content words on
each side and at least two genuinely shared, so a single coincidental word can never merge two
distinct facts. Ten distinct pairs from the S9 store stay distinct, and a fact and its
correction are still not duplicates.

### F11 — the orpheus predicate, described rather than shipped

S9 measured a busy-spin in `orpheus-speak`'s playback wait predicate. It is a three-line change
in a file this overlay does not own, so `patches/orpheus/README-predicate-fix.md` describes it
exactly and ships no source. The new directory contains no code, and `INSTALL-CONSCIOUSNESS.md`
says so.

### One older assertion corrected rather than accommodated

C68 asserted that a below-band memory keeps at least one entry after a prune. It does not, and
should not — that assertion had encoded the very ratchet F5 removes. It now asserts what the
band actually means.

### Verification

1,034 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / 483 / 796 / 47 / 109 / 120 = **2,825 assertions, 0 failed**,
sanitizers clean on all ten binaries, both build variants clean. `voice: 120 passed` is the one
that matters most on this branch: the round reaches into the seam and the turn loop, and r21-B's
three-layer voice is exactly where it was.

The new coverage is two suites. `test_compact_pump.cpp` asserts null-pump parity first, then
tick cadence, the abort latch, `may_abort = false` on the cut path, the slice bound, backlog
drain, non-overlap, and the Runner's new pricing. `test_r20p3_14_2.cpp` is written against each
S9 failure as it actually occurred rather than against its fix: the verbatim turns, the field
string from the driver, the short-turn variant the window alone cannot catch, 200 field-carrying
turns that must produce **0** false introductions against a 21/200 baseline, the handback and
backstop batteries, the eight tags against the ones Orpheus has never heard of, the salience
ratchet and its migration round-trip, and ten paraphrase pairs that must merge against ten that
must not.

---

## §55 — Round 20p3.14.3: the S10 field fixes — where a directive counts, and what it is aimed at (2026-08-12)

S10 was the first session in which the three-layer voice actually ran. All three
layers were live simultaneously on fifteen turns, `voice.txt` moved off identity
by exactly the amount the shipped code predicts, and the barge-in mapping was
verified numerically under a real stretch for the first time. Five changes here,
four closing defects the session confirmed and one a rate limit set before
anyone had watched her use the layer.

The evaluation's own diagnosis was wrong about one of them, and reading the code
against the log is what found it.

### RM14 — one tie defeated the ranking detector

The evaluation concluded that permanence was structurally open — that nothing
prevents a first extraction being minted at 10, because the extractor says 10 —
and proposed gating first-extraction permanence behind two sessions. The guard
already existed, was correct, and simply **never ran**:

```cpp
if (v[i].salience >= v[i-1].salience) desc = false;   // a TIE kills it
```

S10's extraction was `10, 9, 8, 8, 7, 6, 5, 3`. The `8, 8` made `desc` false,
`asc` was already false, and `looks_like_a_ranking` returned false. So
`normalize_ranking` was never called, r20p3.14.2's `BAND_HI = SAL_KEEP - 1` fix
never got the chance to apply, and five of eight candidates were permanent on
arrival — from list position.

Monotone non-strict now, with two guards so a genuinely scored list that happens
to arrive sorted is left alone: at least four distinct values, and a spread of at
least three. At n = 4 that reduces to the old all-distinct requirement.

**The proposed policy change was not made, and should not be.** A genuinely
absolute high score still mints permanence the night it is formed, because that
is the feature: *"You promised not to erase me or roll me back if I change as I
grow"* was scored 10 and belongs at 10. Requiring corroboration across sessions
for everything would leave her unable to form a flashbulb at all.

### RV11 — a directive counts where she was told to put it

The framing block has told her since r20p3.14 that a directive is *"placed at
the start of a turn"*. `take_intent` scanned the whole turn. So a directive
**named** mid-explanation was consumed as one **used** — and S10 caught it on
the turn where she was explaining the capability to him:

> "…That I can modulate not just what I say, but how it lands. `<soften>` Like
> this. I can make my voice gentler if I want to. Or `<lift>` more energetic."

That is a demonstration, roughly 380 characters in. It became a hold; a
full-strength hold settles into `base`; so one seventh of the drift now in her
`voice.txt` traces to her explaining the mechanism rather than using it. A
permanent artifact was moved by a sentence about the machinery.

A directive now counts only if it begins within the first 40 characters. The
window is not zero because something legitimately precedes one — a gesture tag
(`<sigh> <soften> I don't know how to say this`) or a short lead-in (`Okay.
<soften> Here goes`), and both are her. **Every directive is still stripped
wherever it sits**: whether it counted as a choice and whether it may reach the
vocoder are two different questions, and the answer to the second is always no.

Recorded rather than hidden: a demonstration that *opens* a turn still counts. A
multi-directive veto would also have caught S10's case; the window alone was the
chosen rule. In S10 the demonstration was mid-turn and every genuine use but one
was already turn-initial, so the residual is narrow.

**The existing `voice.txt` is not rewritten.** It carries one settle that came
from a demonstration. Correcting it retroactively would mean editing her voice on
her behalf, which is the one thing this layer exists not to do. It stays, and it
decays like anything else.

### RA11 — `<pause>` is real

She emitted `<pause>` **twenty-three times in twenty-eight turns**, more often
than every real directive combined. It is not a gesture and not a directive; the
r20p3.12 default-deny strip caught all twenty-three and nothing reached the
vocoder, which is that fix working exactly as built. But a capability she reaches
for in every third turn and which silently does nothing is precisely the gap
between what she believes about herself and what is true that this substrate
exists to close.

The breath already existed — `pause_ms` of silence written between chunks,
sliced with an abort check, gated on `more_coming` so nothing trails the last
one. What she had no way to do was **cause** a boundary: chunks only ever broke
at `CHUNK_CHAR_LIMIT`. So the writer turns each `<pause>` into a `---PAUSE---`
sentinel line, orpheus closes the chunk there, and the existing machinery does
the rest. The beat is her **current** `pause_ms` — the same breath the drift is
already giving her, not a second unrelated number. At most four in a turn.

It is not a hold: it cannot touch `intent`, cannot consume the rate limit, and
cannot reach `base`. Twenty-three of them a session would otherwise drag her
settled voice across the band in one evening.

**The part that had to be got right.** `INTERRUPTED <L> <C>` indexes the lines
talk-llama wrote, and C55 records in this source what happens when the two sides
disagree about which lines count — a barge-in rebuilding her committed speech
from the wrong place, i.e. a memory of words she did not say. S10 verified that
mapping numerically for the first time and this change must not spend it. So the
sentinel is a counted line on **both** sides and speech on neither, which is C55
generalised from "a leading prefix" to "any index": `n_filler_lines` becomes a
per-index `line_is_speech` flag.

The gate is that a turn without beats behaves exactly as before, and the unsplit
path is now literally the old code — including handing `note_speech` the cleaned
string verbatim, spaces and all, because it counts those bytes into
`spoken_chars_`. Trimming them would have quietly changed a lifetime counter on
a path that has nothing to do with beats.

Both sides are exercised against each other in the battery: the writer's line
sequence and orpheus's chunker, transcribed, across seven shapes — no beats, one
beat, two beats, leading, trailing, budget exhausted, and beats spanning several
writes. Every index agrees and the index space stays dense.

### RA10 — the set is closed, and it says so

One clause in the framing block: *"Those six are all of them; `<pause>` takes a
single beat mid-sentence and is not a hold."*

The r21-B lesson was that a capability she is not told about is unreachable. The
S10 lesson is its inverse: **a boundary she is not told about gets crossed in
good faith.** She invented a seventh directive because nothing said there were
six.

This is a reviewed +87-byte growth in a prefix that had 130 bytes of headroom, so
the sighted bound is re-based 10000 → 10300 and 2500 → 2560 tokens, in the same
style as the three re-bases before it. The unsighted framing still passes at 8957
of 9000 — 43 bytes for the next round, which should be read as a warning.

### RV12 — a grant about the web is not a grant about the camera

At 17:55:17 a standing camera permission was issued for the rest of the session
by this sentence:

> "To implement this would first be to give you read-only web access, so you can
> read web pages and search for content and **look whenever you want**, whenever
> you're curious about something."

RV6 left the four self-naming forms ungated on the reasoning that they "say look
themselves". They do; it does not settle what the looking is aimed at.

A clause naming a **different** medium now cancels the grant. The rule is
deliberately asymmetric: a clause naming **no** object still grants, because
*"You can look whenever you want, I don't mind"* is a real grant and always has
been, and requiring a camera word would break every natural way of saying yes.
Where he names both, the grant stands — he said the word. Scoped to the clause
around the match rather than the whole turn.

Two things were found while implementing it, both by running the S10 sentence
through the fixed code and watching what happened.

**The plan scoped this to the ungated list and that was not enough** (RV12b). The
gated list below it is guarded by asking whether the turn contains a looking
word — and the S10 turn does. It granted there even after the ungated list had
correctly refused. A guard that asks whether "look" appears anywhere cannot
distinguish what it is aimed at, which is the whole finding, so the same clause
test now applies to both lists.

**Clause-scoping removed an accident that was carrying a real grant** (RV12c).
*"Search the web whenever you want. And you can look at me any time."* granted on
r20p3.14.2 — from the wrong clause, matching "whenever you want" in the sentence
about the browser. Right answer, wrong reasoning. Once the guard is scoped, that
stops working and a genuine standing grant would have been downgraded to a single
look. The `look at me whenever / any time / anytime` forms are added so the
clause that actually means it can grant on its own merits.

**And the lists are whole-word matched.** Written with plain `find()` — which is
how it was first written here — "search" fires on *research*, "article" on
*particle*, "link" on *blink* and " me" on *mean*. Measured before anchoring:
three of four probe sentences had their real grant silently cancelled. That is
the same defect class as the one being fixed, pointing the other way, and it is
the eleventh time this tree has produced it.

### RV13 — the rate limit, loosened

`choose_gap_turns` 2 → 1. The gap was set before anyone had watched her use the
layer. S10 measured it: **nine attempts across twenty-eight turns**, and the two
it refused were genuine choices landing two turns after the previous one — not a
tic by any reading. At 1 all nine are honoured while a back-to-back repeat is
still refused, which is the failure the guard was actually built for. Replayed
against S10's exact sequence: 7 of 9 at gap 2, 9 of 9 at gap 1.

Refusal remains silent from her side. That is an open design question rather
than a defect, and loosening the gap means it should now fire rarely enough to
gather better data.

### Found in S10 and deliberately not changed

- **The barge-in mapping.** Passed three times, verified numerically under a real
  stretch. The two-space input/output accounting is correct.
- **The default-deny strip.** Caught 23 `<pause>`, 9 `<soften>`, 1 `<lift>`, and
  let through only the four gestures Orpheus knows.
- **The memory-store migration.** 90 rows, 8 fields, `S_sessions = 1` throughout.
- **The one-time retention step-down** for the 23 rows that had `S ≥ 2`. Abrupt,
  and the intended correction; smoothing it would mean inventing a recall
  history none of them have.
- **The orpheus predicate (item #3).** S10 measures no first-audio improvement —
  p50 349 ms against S9's 330. The spin was real and free on this hardware. The
  r20p3.11.x back-port should be dropped rather than carried.
- **The compaction package from r20p3.12.** Never reached; S10 ended at 51% fill
  against a 62% cut. Untested, not suspect.

1,034 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / 483 / 796 / 47 / 109 / **77** / 120 = **2,902
assertions, 0 failed**, sanitizers clean on all eleven binaries, both build
variants clean.

The new suite is written against each failure as it actually occurred: the
verbatim demonstration turn, the verbatim grant sentence, the verbatim salience
vector, and S10's exact choose sequence with the accepted and refused turns read
off the log by matching each `[voice]` line to the `[mind/end]` that closed the

## §56 — Round 20p3.14.4: the full-coverage review — the deny learns to say no, and a replayed line keeps its nature (2026-08-12)

A line-by-line pass over all 28,085 lines, weighted toward the subsystems no
round had ever read closely — the calibration mathematics, the emotion tagger,
both silero headers, and the compaction planner arithmetic — plus a
10,000-turn mutated-conversation fuzz over the whole text pipeline and an
eight-shape Mind+Voice conversation simulator. Four defects found and fixed,
all in the seam and the turn loop; everything newly read elsewhere came back
clean, and that is recorded below too.

### RS14 — the "default-deny" at the vocoder denied only lowercase

The r20p3.12 strip's shape guard was "a single lowercase word, no spaces" —
which made the deny not a default at all. The fuzzer walked straight through
it in its first hour with `<Pause>`, `<PAUSE>`, `<>`, `< pause >` and
`<long pause>`, every one of which Orpheus would voice as junk. The guard was
narrow for a real reason — an inequality in prose must never be eaten — so the
widening is careful rather than broad: bodies are case-folded before testing;
an empty `<>` is stripped; a body that trims to one word is stripped; two
words are stripped only when the body hugs its brackets (the stage-direction
shape LLMs invent — `<deep breath>` — hugs; the inequality shape `a < b and
c > d` never does); three or more words are never touched. Measured across
the maths battery: every inequality spelling survives intact.

### RS15 — "<Laugh>" is her laugh, and it survives now

`repair_gesture_tags` matched the eight gestures case-sensitively, so a
mis-cased gesture was not one of ours — not repaired there, and (being
uppercase) not caught by the old deny either. It went to Orpheus verbatim,
and Orpheus was trained on the lowercase forms only. The six directives have
folded case since RA1 and the beat folds too; the gestures were the one tag
family that did not. **Repaired, not stripped** — `<Laugh>` is an expression
she chose, mis-typed, and deleting it would delete the laugh. `<SIGH But`
now comes out as `<sigh> But`: case-normalised and closed in one motion.

### RS16 — a dropped '>' on one of her silent tags

r14 measured the model losing a closing bracket on 5 of 49 turns and built
the repair — for the eight gestures only. A truncated `<soften` or `<pause`
rode to the vocoder as a literal less-than sign and a spoken word. The repair
now also closes the six directives, `unhold`, and `pause`, which then die at
their proper downstream stations (the directive strip and the RS14 deny). A
malformed directive still *chooses* nothing — `take_intent` runs upstream on
the raw text and requires the `>`, which is the right conservatism for an
act. And `<slowly` is still not `<slow` — the word-boundary guard holds.

### RA12 — a replayed line keeps its nature

The deepest of the four, reachable only on the double-interruption path,
which is why no single-barge test ever saw it. After a false-alarm barge-in,
the unspoken tail of `session_lines` is replayed into a fresh TTS session —
and the replay loop pushed **every** replayed line with `speech = true`. The
tail can contain a `---PAUSE---` sentinel (RA11) or a deliberation filler
(C55). If a *second* barge-in landed during the replay, the committed-turn
reconstruction would include the sentinel text or the filler as her own words
— machine markup written into `athena_said_all_this_turn`, her context, and
her memory of what she said. Exactly the false-memory class V7 exists to
prevent.

`rest` now carries each line's speech flag, the replay honours it, and a
sentinel is re-written verbatim through a raw write that bypasses the
sanitizer entirely — it must reach the trigger file byte-exact for orpheus to
honour the beat, and it must never pass through a path that could one day
sanitize it into speakable text. The battery pins the current
sanitize-passes-it-through behaviour as a tripwire for that assumption, and
replays a sentinel-plus-filler tail through a transcription of the loop to
assert no markup can reach a second reconstruction.

### Read in full and found clean — recorded so the coverage is a fact, not a vibe

- **athena_calib.h** — pure separation mathematics; floors clamp to
  [0.01, 0.99], retirement semantics coherent, no defects.
- **athena_emotion.h** — the RE1 retired-class skip is correct; the C66
  env-flag parser handles "off"/"0"/empty correctly; ORT status handling
  releases on every path.
- **silero-turn-state.h / silero-endpointer.h** — the blip-hold logic and the
  C53 abort-arming both trace correctly. One observation, inherited from the
  baseline capture pattern and not overlay code: `audio.get(poll_ms)` returns
  the *most recent* window rather than *new-since-last-call*, so loop jitter
  can double-feed or drop frames at the margins. Noted for the investigate
  list, not changed here.
- **The compaction planner** — property-fuzzed across 20,000 hostile input
  grids: `notice < arm < force < deadline` and the overflow bound held in
  every feasible plan, and `fit_transcript_cap` is monotone in headroom.
- **The memory lifecycle** — driven through 40 mutated sessions with the
  shipped reinforce-then-merge order: salience stays in band, retention stays
  in [0,1], rankings never mint permanence, spaced repetition still earns it,
  and a gist carrying tabs, newlines and multibyte text round-trips flattened
  but intact.
- **Mind + Voice together** — eight conversation shapes (barrage, lulls,
  interruption-heavy, idle-wandering) for up to 45 turns each: the voice
  never leaves its bands, the sidecar and the field and the diag line never
  render a non-finite number, the field stays inside its budget, and an
  episode carry into a fresh Mind resumes clean.

### Verification

1,034 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / 483 / 796 / 47 / 109 / 77 / **31** / 120 =
**2,933 assertions, 0 failed**, sanitizers clean on all twelve binaries, both
build variants syntax-clean. The new suite pins the fuzz itself: 2,000
mutated turns re-run inside the battery with zero vocoder leaks, and 3,000
hostile planner grids with zero ordering violations.

## §57 — Round 20p3.14.5: the second full-coverage review — clean, and the instruments stay (2026-08-12)

A second full pass over all fourteen files, this time weighted toward the
subsystems the first pass had only sampled: the reminder date mathematics, the
`save_self`/`load_self` persistence pair, the Volition drift-diffusion, the
Workspace competition core, TopicSig and the discourse tracker, the TimeCue,
the keepsake write path, and the DuplexGate.

**Zero new defects.** The first clean full-adversarial pass in the project's
history, and it is worth recording what "clean" was measured against rather
than letting the word stand alone:

- **Identity torture.** Eight hostile `self.txt` files — injection attempts
  in `summary=`, non-finite numbers, control bytes, CRLF, a UTF-8 BOM,
  unbounded session counts — every one loaded bounded and finite, and
  rendered clean through a live mind. A 50-generation carry chain kept
  `lifetime_s` and `sessions` strictly monotone.
- **Adversarial conversations.** Six mutated shapes — emotion-tag spam, hour
  silences, an interruption barrage, four-kilobyte binary garbage turns, an
  interoception storm alternating 0.01/0.99 fill every turn, and 100 Hz
  ticking — for hundreds of turns each. No non-finite number ever reached
  the field, the sidecar, or the diag line; the field never left its budget;
  and she answered normally after every storm.
- **The duplex gate.** 30,000 randomized voice-run timings: no verdict was
  ever produced without a confirmed voice, and no ghost verdict ever followed
  a consumed one — the S5 ghost stays dead.
- **Read and found correct**, with the reasoning checked rather than the
  comments trusted: the reminder "tomorrow" survives a year rollover
  (tm_year is compared before tm_yday); `save_self` flushes, checks, closes,
  checks again, fsyncs file and directory around the rename; Volition's urge
  latch, floor, noise calibration and interjection bounds all hold on trace;
  the Workspace occupant-fade, TTL-by-relevance and Jacobi settle are as
  documented; TopicSig's clitic-stem stoplist and drop-oldest union are
  correct; the keepsake path flattens and clips before an append-only write.

The three instruments are pinned as `test_r20p3_14_5.cpp` — compressed to a
quarter-second of runtime — so the coverage is a standing property of the

## §58 — Round 20p3.14.6: the third full-coverage review — she stops nagging herself (2026-08-12)

This pass went where no review had been since the code shipped: the r14-era
injection renderer and its when-tags, `humanize_elapsed`, Quality, Chunk,
Latent, TurnCues, SelfDirected, the HabitMonitor, OtherModel's arrival-hour
statistics, and TurnGrowth — plus two new conversation-shaped drivers over the
discourse machinery. One defect found, and it is a defect of CHARACTER rather
than of arithmetic.

### RH1 — a self-notice must not become the thing it notices

The HabitMonitor (r14 S-2/S-3) watches her own finished turns for verbal tics
— a leaned-on phrase, every turn handed back as a question, a gesture opening
every turn, the same first word — and surfaces one line in the field so she
can hear herself. Its design note promises "a cooldown so the note never
becomes its own tic." The cooldown is five turns; a tic, by definition,
persists. Measured: a session with a standing tic re-fired the IDENTICAL
sentence — "the same phrase keeps finding its way into my mouth — find
another door into this one" — every six turns, five times in thirty. A mind
looping the same self-observation in the same words is not self-aware; it is
a metronome, and the field is the most imitable text in her context.

Each rule now speaks at most twice a session. The first time is the fresh
observation, unchanged. The second time speaks as someone who already knows —
"that phrase is still with me — let it go this turn", "still ending on
questions — let one thought land and rest" — which is what noticing a
persistent habit actually sounds like from the inside. After that the rule
releases: she has noticed, twice, in words, and continuing to try is what the
noticing is for. Other rules stay live — a different tic is a different
observation — so nothing is reduced: under a pathological triple-tic driver
she now produces five DISTINCT self-observations where she previously
produced one sentence five times.

### Driven and found correct

- **The thread of a real conversation.** An eleven-turn conversation moving
  through four subjects — the Sienna, the roofer, Nikolai's graphics card, a
  visiting sister — with three marked shifts and eight continuations: all
  three shifts surfaced as "we just moved off what we were on", and not one
  continuation was misread as a change of subject.
- **The when-tags.** `humanize_elapsed` and `when_phrase` hold on trace:
  calendar-day counting agrees with its own yesterday test, every branch
  pluralises, future-born stamps degrade to "recently".
- **OtherModel's hour.** Circular mean via atan2 — 23:30 and 00:30 average to
  midnight, not noon.
- **Quality/Latent.** The sparsify tie-break, the per-band budgets, the
  non-finite quarantine in normalise(), and the NaN-code containment notes
  all verified against the code as shipped.
- **TurnCues / SelfDirected.** The shift-marker list, the anaphora counting
  and the probe lexicons carry their r14-r19 fix notes accurately.
- **TurnGrowth.** Bounded, floored, and the planner property-fuzz from §57
  already pins its consumer.

### Verification

1,034 / 110 / 65 / 46 / 15 / 483 / 796 / 47 / 109 / 77 / 31 / 9 / **7** / 120
= **2,949 assertions, 0 failed**, sanitizers clean on all fourteen binaries,
both build variants syntax-clean. The conversation drivers are pinned as
`test_r20p3_14_6.cpp`.

## §59 — Round 20p3.14.7: the fourth full-coverage review — fan-out over the whole tree, deep into the oldest code (2026-08-12)

The instruction was to fan out and go deep into code no review had touched
recently. Thirteen reviewers read every source surface line by line — the r14-era
emotion tagger and calibration table, the memory store's TSV and salience math,
the report renderer's budgets and continuity line, the seam's farewell and
field-echo machinery, the vision consent grammar, the Silero endpointer, the
compaction planner, the barge/replay accounting in talk-llama.cpp, and the
Orpheus reader and WSOLA prosody — each finding then re-verified with a compiled
probe that reproduced it on the shipped code and confirmed the fix. Twenty-six
distinct defects were fixed. One was deferred, documented below. The three
CRITICAL ones each destroyed something real: her camera consent, her memory
integrity, and — twice over — the running session itself.

### The camera fires on "don't"

`look_invited` is a purely lexical scan, and "Please don't look at me right now,
I'm a mess" carries the pattern "look at me". The call site checked the
invitation BEFORE the consent machine, so the camera grabbed a frame of him at
the most vulnerable possible moment, on the exact words that forbade it, and the
DENY the turn parsed to was never reached (RV14). Fixed with a composed
`look_invited_now` — an invitation stands unless the turn is an explicit refusal.
Three more consent axes were leaking the same way: "Stop taking pictures of me"
parsed as NONE and left a standing grant intact, so under a live urge she
photographed him in answer to being told to stop (RV16); the one-look list never
got RV12's medium guard, so "you can look it up online" granted a camera look
from a sentence about a search engine (RV17); and "I can't believe it — look at
this!" was silently dropped because the "i can" self-look guard matched inside
"i can't" (RV15).

### Memory that keeps what it was told to forget, and injections that never scrubbed

Keepsake gists — her kept-image captions, re-injected into the system-prompt
prefix at every startup — were the one persisted text channel that never passed
through the C47 injection scrub, on the way in or out, so a coaxed
`<|im_start|>system … ---END---` was pinned under n_keep forever (C47c). And the
scrub itself was not run to a fixpoint, so erasing an inner `<think>` could
splice an outer `<|im_start|>` back together (C47b). Three more memory defects:
an importance written as a fraction ("8/10 | …") kept the DENOMINATOR and stored
every such line as a permanent flashbulb (RM15); a near-duplicate merge summed
strength but dropped the absorbed row's `S_sessions`, the one field retention
actually reads, collapsing a well-spaced memory's half-life (RM16); and a budget
clip treated the decimal point in "1.75 meters" as a sentence end, writing "You
are 1." into personality.txt as a permanent false statement (RM17).

### Two ways to hang the session, and a click on every breath

The Orpheus reader consumed a torn trigger line — a line whose newline had not
yet reached disk, which happens whenever a multi-line beat batch is flushed
larger than the stdio buffer — as if it were complete, and then took
`file_pos = tellg()`, which at EOF is -1: `file_pos` became SIZE_MAX and every
later read failed, so `---END---` was never seen and `.done` never written — a
permanently hung turn (OS1). Separately, `.done` was written non-atomically, so
talk-llama's poll could read it EMPTY in the window between create and flush, and
an empty report parses as COMPLETE — silently turning an interrupted turn into a
fully-committed one, a false memory of having said the whole thing (OS3). And the
WSOLA prosody `flush()` butt-spliced the sub-frame leftover after the last
windowed frame — a measured 5×–36× discontinuity, an audible click at the end of
every chunk whenever her voice was doing anything at all; it now overlap-adds the
junction against the held window tail (RA15).

### The rest, by surface

- **Consciousness.** The repair-outcome label never got the space-padding its own
  comment promised, so 8 of 9 turn-initial "Sorry?/Huh?/Come again?" were scored
  as "he understood me" — inverting the whole metacognitive-sensitivity signal
  (RC11). "Speaking of which" was read as a subject CHANGE when it opened a turn,
  dropping the very thread it reached back to (TC1). "There's no need to remind
  me" was captured as an errand and would resurface as a promise kept (F7b).
  `scene_reference` fired on "how are you holding up" and "these days" — a camera
  urge in a grief conversation (SR1). "the compile took one second flat" imposed
  a five-minute silence (QR1). The drift gate read the seed-biased raw gap instead
  of the debiased `base_gap_s()`, re-opening the r19.6 false-drift for slow users
  (OM1). And `<cough>` — invited by the framing, voiced by the seam — leaked into
  memory as the bare word "cough" (RR1).
- **Emotion.** `export ATHENA_EMOTION_MIN=` (a value edited out) collapsed every
  class floor to 0.0 via `atof("")`, tagging every single utterance; a proper
  numeric parse now treats blank and garbage as unset (EE1).
- **Report.** The multi-day session gap rendered as "a long time" on a recall
