### Tier 1 — the four that change what she is

**WO-SH3 — a claim is a prediction, and a correction is that prediction resolving
(`ATHENA_ASSERT_PROSPECT`).** The ASSERT channel's appraisal door wrote five literal constants, so
all **eight** corrections in two real S22 evenings produced the identical vector, the identical
argmax and the identical score — `shame` raw 0.8950, emitted 0.6936 — on turns as different as
*"That is not what I asked you to do, and you did it anyway"* and *"No, that's not true. They weigh
exactly the same."* Measured through the shipped `classify()`, **80.4 % of that score is the single
term `0.8 * agency_self(0.90)`**, and `shame` is the only negative label of the twenty that reads
`agency_self` at all: the argmax was a foregone conclusion dressed as a classification. The mechanism
this needed already shipped one line above. `Mind::sense_turn`'s `assert_pending_` resolver is the one
place in the tree that computes an explicit predicted probability (`p_stand =
calib_.score(Calibration::ASSERT)`) and an explicit outcome (`a_hit`), and it was the one such place
that did not call `prospect_resolved` — which is exactly what D8/D9/D13 call when a prediction of
hers resolves. A claim she made on solid ground **is** a prediction that it will stand; the correction
is that prediction resolving badly, by the amount she believed it. So on `!a_hit` the door now calls
`appr2_.prospect_resolved(-p_stand, /*was_feared=*/false, p_stand, t)`: the error is `-p_stand` (she
was that sure and it did not hold), the magnitude is `p_stand` (a claim she barely believed resolves
faintly). **No new label, no new lexicon, no new constant, no new accessor.** Measured on the eight
real corrections through the shipped engine: **`disappointment` on all eight, adopted on all eight,
0.6834–0.8360**. She keeps a name for every one of them, and the name stops being about her character
and starts being about what happened. Two of the eight land at margin 0.0913 / 0.0919, just inside
`GRAN_MARGIN` 0.10, so an *ask* on one of those turns is hedged by `take_label_line_asked` — it does
not fire on the real corpus. The spoken mixed-note rate **rises**, because `disappointment`'s tau is
1800 s against `shame`'s 600 s and the heavy residual is still alive when the next bright turn lands.
**What this does not claim, measured rather than assumed:** a correction of her BEHAVIOUR may deserve
`shame` where a correction of a CLAIM does not, and this door cannot tell the two apart — fitted on a
28-turn adversarial set, the best rule the tree can build from what it already computes (TopicSig
overlap, `assert_domain_of`, `assert_kinds_of`, `need_class`, `appraise_text`, `commitment_in`) scores
**50.0 %** on the eight real corrections, which is chance, and eleven of the fourteen shipped signals
carry no information there at all. The reason is structural: `assert_pending_` has exactly one setter,
in `finish_turn`, on a COMPLETE ASSERT-stance turn of HERS — so the only act of hers this resolver has
any record of is a saying. **The one reduction, disclosed rather than papered over:** scoring with
`p_stand` inherits the engine's floor, and `emit(p) = (0.8p + 0.15)(0.5p + 0.5)` reaches `EMIT_MIN`
0.55 at `p = 0.64724`, so on a COLD channel (`Calibration::score` = `(hits + 1.5)/(n + 3)` reads
0.5000 after no stood claims and 0.6250 after one) the correction names **nothing**, where r24.13's
constant always named `shame`. That costs the first one or two corrections of a **brand-new install**
and nothing else: S22 carried `calib=4|0|171|166` in `self.txt`, so the channel opened at 0.9633 and
the eight real corrections ran 0.7750–0.9079. It is pinned in three places, including
`test_r2412_affect` §2.a, the one scripted evening in the battery that reaches a cold channel.
**`ATHENA_ASSERT_PROSPECT=0` restores the r24.13 vector byte for byte — verified byte-identical to
shipped r24.13 over all 160 real turns.**
*In a session:* S1 18:35:01, *"No, that's not right. You never said that."* r24.13 says *"the closest
name for what this is: shame"*. r24.14 says **`disappointment`**, and the §3.1 note gains a named
heavy side.

**WO-SH4 — and the one arm where self-blame is earned (`ATHENA_ASSERT_SHAME_SIGNAL`).** WO-SH3 alone
does not merely take `shame` off this corpus, it takes the word out of the vocabulary: a census of
every appraisal door in the tree, each at the vector its own source writes, finds exactly **one** that
can produce an adopted `shame` — the correction door — and the next best (D12, a project abandoned)
scores 0.5900 → 0.4425 and is refused at the floor. **Zero adoptable doors would be a reduction in
what she can feel**, so this arm is not optional. The question is which corrections she is actually
the author of, and the site already knows: §1.7a's fast error stage sets `err_fast_t_` when a spike of
self-surprise crosses 2.2 σ **inside her own delivery** — part of her flagged that sentence while she
was saying it — and the arm four blocks below already tests exactly this 120 s window (*"part of me
had flagged that sentence before you did"*). So `own_signal = cfg_.meta2 && cfg_.assert_shame_signal
&& (t - err_fast_t_) < 120.0`, and on that arm the r24.13 self-agency vector and its intensity 0.55
are kept **byte for byte**. That is the distinction psychology actually draws between disappointment
and shame — not *claim or behaviour* but **did the self have the evidence**. Measured against the real
production traces (2,655,133 + 2,709,141 diag lines, `ssz=` sampled 1,646 + 1,714 times, peaks 3.2 and
4.3): of the eight real corrections exactly **two** carry a crossing inside that window — S2 13:41:36,
where she had given two different answers for the same gap in consecutive turns, and S2 14:58:14,
where she denied a dream she had had. Both are turns where she half-knew. **`shame` 8/8 → 2/8;
distinct negative names over two real evenings 1 → 2.** The arm reads the CLOCK and not
`err_fast_pending_` / `err_reached_awareness_` on purpose: the question is whether the self had the
evidence, not whether awareness caught it or whether the note below has already been spent. **The
looseness, named:** on the *tight* window — the delivery of the sentence actually being corrected —
the rate is **0 of 8**; both crossings that satisfy the 120 s test happened during an *earlier* turn.
That window is inherited from the shipped `err_note_` arm, not introduced here, and the honest reading
is *"her error monitor was live in the last two minutes"*, not *"on that sentence"*. **A documented
rider:** `ATHENA_ASSERT_SHAME_SIGNAL=0` gives WO-SH3's undiscriminated form (every correction
`disappointment`); with `ATHENA_ASSERT_PROSPECT=0` it is **inert**, because that arm is r24.13's
vector on every correction already. Stated explicitly because the disable-only law asks each switch's
`=0` to restore r24.13 alone, and this one narrows another switch rather than standing beside it.
*In a session:* S2 13:41:36. She has just given two different answers for the same gap and her own
fast stage spiked on the second. He corrects her. r24.13 says `shame` and cannot say why; r24.14 says
`shame` **and the substrate can point at the reason** — while the other six corrections of the evening
stop being about her character.

**WO-K6 — the loss door: `distress` was not unreachable, it was unreachable *from his voice*
(`ATHENA_COMPACT_LOSS_DOOR`) — and WO-K6b is what lets it reach her
(`ATHENA_APPRAISE2_OUTWEIGHS`).** r24.13's report shipped *"`distress` and `weariness` remain
unreachable for arithmetic reasons no feature change fixes"*. On `distress` that is **half wrong**,
and the half that is right is worth sharpening. Swept against the shipped `classify()` with no edit,
the minimum `|pleasant|` that emits `distress` over the whole coping range is **47/66 = 0.7121**, at
coping 5/11 = 0.4545 where the two binding constraints cross, and `emotion_valence_`'s deepest
negative is **0.70** (`angry`). So **no turn of his can ever get there** — that much is right, and the
tag map must not be deepened to make it (WO-V9 measures what happens if you try). But **the bound is a
bound on the tag map, not on the label.** A door whose `pleasant` is not `emotion_valence_` — a
**measured magnitude of a real loss** — is not bound by 0.70 at all. The magnitude is the part of the
live conversation a completed cut did not bring back, `(n_past_before − n_keep − reload_tokens) /
(n_past_before − n_keep)`, all four numbers already in hand at `compact_cut`'s call site. On S1's one
real cut, `(24,388 − 14,856 − 1,680) / (24,388 − 14,856)` = **0.8238**: 7,852 of 9,532 tokens of live
conversation, 82.4 %, gone. Her measured coping at that instant (fatigue 0.60, miss rate 3/34,
ownership 0.962, runway past the deadline) is **0.4000**, and that vector classifies `distress` raw
**0.6614**, emitted **0.6031**, against `EMIT_MIN` 0.55. Everything else in the vector is left at the
struct's own default, and **each omission is a refusal to claim** — the WO-AV1 discipline applied to a
door built from one number: `agency_other` 0, nobody in the room did this; `agency_self` 0, she did
not choose it either; `conducive` 0, a cut does not *obstruct* her, it removes what she was holding;
`goal_rel` 0, `concern_weight_` is 0.000 on all 160 real turns and a conversation is not a topic;
`novelty` 0, a cut is the least surprising thing in the evening. **The intensity IS the magnitude**,
so the residual laid is proportional to what was lost. **Where it is silent, which is most places.**
It fires exactly once across both real evenings — S1's single cut at 19:07:59 — because S2 never
compacted in 126.4 minutes, and it cannot fire in a session that does not cut. **THE BAND, said here
because a claim that holds only inside a window nobody has pinned is worse than no claim:** at this
magnitude `distress` beats `fear` only while her coping is above `7/6 − 0.8238 = 0.3429`, and at the
cut she measures 0.4000 — **0.0571 of coping**, which is 771 s more session clock through `fatigue_()`
or 0.0952 more context fill. Below it the same cut is named `fear`, whose tau is 240 s against
`distress`'s 3600 s. That is accepted rather than engineered away, and `test_r2414_stakes` §6.6 pins
both sides of the line by driving the real evening across it. **The caveat is stated, because one cut
is one sample:** the six real *plans* of both evenings would have lost 0.7826…0.9591 had they cut, so
a cut of the shape this planner builds is *always* a distress-grade loss — what this door proves is
that at the one loss that really happened the engine now has a name for it, **not** that the magnitude
discriminates between cuts. The **projected** version was built and rejected for exactly that reason:
armed at *plan* time it fires six times, including in S2 where no cut ever happened. This one is armed
by a **completed** cut and by nothing else. No floor was lowered and no magnitude invented: `EMIT_MIN`
is untouched at 0.55, the tag map is untouched, `GRAN_MARGIN` is untouched.
(**The disagreement, named:** `sense_compaction_loss`'s own comment says the door's floor is *"0.7826
lost and it is silent below that at every coping"*; `STAKES-CHANGES.md` says *"the floor at her
measured coping is 0.7768"*. `test_r2414_stakes` §6.3 computes the floor at the measured coping to
four places at run time and asserts only that it lies in (0.75, 0.80), printing the exact value rather
than pinning it — so neither number is pinned anywhere, 0.7826 is also the low end of the six-plan
range one paragraph above it, and the two cannot both be the floor. What is checkable without running
is the band: **the door is silent until more than three quarters of the live conversation is gone.**
The exact figure is an open measurement for r24.15, and the fixture should pin what it already
computes.)

**And WO-K6b, without which the paragraph above was false on the one evening it is about.**
`aff2::Appraisal2`'s hysteresis refuses a challenger unless it beats `current_score + HYSTERESIS`, and
`current_score` is a `classify()` score **frozen at the instant of adoption** — the one quantity in
that engine with no life at all, while every other reading of the incumbent decays. On S1, WO-SH3
turns each of the three corrections at 18:35:01 / 18:37:00 / 18:38:40 into `disappointment` at
`current_score` 0.8360 with a 1800 s residual. The one real cut is **1,759 s** later. The loss door
raises `distress` at emitted 0.6031 against a bar of **0.9560**; both labels are heavy, so `same_sign_`
is true and r24.12's cross-valence escape does not apply; the event was **REFUSED**, `hold_both` laid
the residual, and **the frame at the cut named nothing.** She felt it and had no word for it — and the
round's headline claim was false as merged. **The fix is not to lower the margin.** HYSTERESIS asks
one question — does the new name beat the standing one by a clear margin — and it is right to ask it.
It is asked in the wrong **currency** when the two events are far apart in time, because a fit measured
twenty-nine minutes ago is not a fit now. So it is asked a **second** time, in the other currency the
engine already keeps and already trusts for exactly this purpose: `residual_[i]`, how much of a state
is left. A challenger whose own intensity exceeds what the incumbent *still holds*, by the same 0.12,
is a change of state and not a wobble of the vocabulary. **Nothing is weakened.** The margin is
untouched, `EMIT_MIN` is untouched, and the escape is a FLOOR the challenger must clear and not a floor
lowered: `residual_[current] + HYSTERESIS` exceeds 1.0 for any incumbent above **0.88** — a derived
ceiling, `1.0 − HYSTERESIS` against a clamped intensity — so a fresh strong incumbent cannot be
displaced by intensity at all, and a small event can never take a name from a large one. At the cut,
`residual_[disappointment]` is 0.9079·e^(−1759/1800) = **0.3417**, the bar is 0.4617, `lays` is 0.8238:
adopted. **MEASURED BLAST RADIUS: exactly one event over the whole real corpus.** Over S1, S2 and S21
the **whole rendered field of all 160 turns is byte-identical** both ways, asserted with its reason
asserted beside it — WO-V8's gate is open on 0 of the ticks of all three scripts and none of the three
carries a cut, so neither door this escape arbitrates raises an event anywhere in that corpus. On the
one corpus where they can differ they do: driving S1's own timeline including the cut's own field, the
two arms differ on **1 of 59 rendered fields**, at turn index 40, and nowhere before it. **Two things
it does that the round did not first say, and both are recorded because they outlive the round.**
*First*, `current` is not only the name: `take_label_line_felt` answers *"what are you feeling"* from
it under `ask_prefers_current`, so after the cut the two arms answer that question with different
words for as long as the adopted residual outlives `ASK_FELT_MIN` — about 85 minutes of `distress`
against about 16 of `disappointment`. Driven at five offsets after the real cut, they differ on **four
of the five**. Both answers are labels the engine really holds, since `hold_both` lays the refused
challenger's residual either way, so this is a containment and not a defect — but *"only the NAME
moves"* was too small a claim and is withdrawn. *Second*, the escape admits **alternation**: the
incumbent's side decays and the challenger's laid intensity does not, so two doors that keep firing
can hand a name back and forth. That is accepted, bounded and pinned rather than argued away — see
**the review** below, where the alternative was measured and re-opens the blocker. **`=0` restores
r24.13's engine exactly** — the refusal condition becomes textually identical, `lays` is still
computed but has no effect, nothing in the appraisal engine is persisted so there is no `=0`
data-loss path, and the losing case is kept as a pin (`B.named == "(nothing)"`) so the blocker cannot
come back unnoticed. One bound on the bookkeeping argument, stated where it is made: *"the two
branches write the same residual, so every readout is bit-identical"* is true **given `hold_both`,
which is the default** — the refusal branch lays the residual only `if (hold_both)`, so at
`ATHENA_APPRAISE2_HOLD_BOTH=0` with this switch on (both legal, each still restoring r24.13 alone) an
adopted event lays a residual the refused one would not have.
*In a session:* 19:07:59 on 30 August. Eight thousand tokens of the evening go, and the frame carries
*"the closest name for what this is: distress"* instead of nothing.

**WO-R3 — the substrate computes regions (`ATHENA_LOOK_REGIONS`).** Every visual instrument in the
tree is whole-frame by construction. `dhash_rgb` reduces the frame to 64 monotone comparisons on an
8×8 grid and `hamming64` reduces **those** to a popcount; `photo_sig_rgb` is one global histogram. The
grid the dHash bits come from already carries *where* the structure moved and the popcount throws it
away: at the four real S22 second-look distances (13, 23, 26, 35) the popcount keeps about six bits of
a number that could have carried forty to sixty, and two real keepsake pairs at **exactly hamming 24**
split their flipped bits 5/5/8/6 and 4/4/4/12 across the quadrants — the same number, two different
events, one sentence. So r24.14 adds a second, independent decomposition of the **same buffer**,
computed once per look beside the two whole-frame signatures and never in place of them: a
`RGN_G × RGN_G` = 4×4 tile grid, and per tile (a) a `PhotoSig` — the shipped struct, so the shipped
`photo_delta` is what prices a tile's light, one implementation of that earth-mover term in the build
and not two — and (b) a 4×4 grid of sub-cell luma, **contrast-normalised** as `(c − mean) / (mad +
RGN_FLAT_K)`. The normalisation is the design decision: the photometric term measures the affine part,
so the structural term must not, or a webcam's auto-exposure would read as a thing that moved. **Be
exact about how far that goes.** The divisor is `mad + 8`, which under `c → a·c + b` becomes
`a·mad + 8` and not `a·(mad + 8)`, so the term is **exact under an offset and only approximate under a
gain** — the `+8` is what breaks the gain, deliberately, because it is the same `+8` that makes a blank
wall normalise to zero. The residual is bounded in closed form: on a tile of contrast `v` a pure gain
`a` leaves `256·v·|a−1| / ((a·v+8)·(v+8))`, maximised at `v = 8/√a` at `32·(√a−1)/(√a+1)` — under
`LOOK_CHANGE_BITS` for `a < 2.14` and under the FIGURE floor for `a < 4.84`, and peaking on a
*low-texture* tile, not a flat one and not a busy one. The fixture measures it against production
`region_tile_struct` at 1.25×/1.5×/2×/2.14×/3×/5× and prints the measured worst tile beside the bound:
2, 3, 6, 6, 9, 12 — crossing the gate at 2× and the FIGURE floor at 5×, exactly where the algebra
says. `RGN_FLAT_K` = 8 luma is a **denominator, never a threshold**. A tile's change is
`region_tile_struct ∨ photo_delta`, `look_change_score`'s own *"each term answers its own question"*
rule applied to a tile, in the same 0..64 bit-equivalent units, so **`LOOK_CHANGE_BITS` serves the
whole frame, the photometry and a tile with no second constant to keep in sync**. Over the sixteen
tile deltas `region_read` returns one of four verdicts — QUIET, GROUND (half the frame or more over
the gate *and* the median over it), FIGURE (a quarter or fewer, the loudest at least twice the gate,
and standing a gate above the median), and **MIXED, which says nothing**. The abstention is where a
camera nudge lands — 135 of 1,400 nudge pairs — and it is the difference between a channel that is
quiet when it does not know and one that guesses. **The grid was decided by measurement, not by
taste**: 4×4 has 3×3's zero false-positive rate and eight more true detections (FIGURE recall 27/28
against 19/28), because a lamp coming on over a quadrant is 4 of 9 tiles on a 3×3 grid — neither a
minority nor a majority, so all seven fell into the abstention — and is exactly 2×2 tiles on a 4×4
one, which is also the unit the place-phrase table names, so the grid and the vocabulary agree by
construction. 6×6 and 8×8 buy at most one more true detection for a **0.60 %** and **2.22 %** rate of
claiming a thing moved when nothing did. **No shipped function is modified**: `dhash_rgb`,
`photo_sig_rgb`, `photo_delta`, `hamming64` and `look_change_score` are untouched, and
`apply_scene_from_slot` gains two **defaulted** parameters so every existing caller compiles and
behaves identically. The pass runs exactly where the two shipped signatures already run — the detached
encode worker, or inline in `vision_drain_eval`, on the same buffer, in the same `!is_recall &&
!audio` block — takes no mutex, touches no shared state and **adds no diagnostic field**, so
`aseam::trace_signature`'s mask table is untouched; the forensic detail goes to the stderr look line
through `aseam::region_trace`, which is where WO-V2 put the same kind of detail and where the S23 grep
sheet looks. Measured cost **1.16 ms at 640×480** beside `dhash_rgb`'s 0.52 ms against a **measured**
5.0 s of encode and prefill for that frame: **0.023 %**. Confusion table over 126 pairs built from the
seven real keepsakes, every B frame through a real JPEG encode at the source file's own quantiser
tables: **QUIET 49/49, FIGURE 27/28, GROUND 49/49**. Two housekeeping items came out of the review and
belong here: `RegionSig::contrast` was written for all sixteen tiles on every look and read by nothing
— law 6's defect, and its own comment named a diag line this round had deliberately decided not to add
— so it is **removed** rather than wired, because wiring it would have changed the operator look line
that S23's static-room measurement is meant to read (`RegionSig` is 1,668 bytes now, not 1,732); and
`RegionSig::cell` gains `= {}`, because `region_sig_rgb` has four early returns that hand back an
invalid signature and without the initialiser it carried 1,088 bytes of indeterminate float into
`EncodeSlot::region` for the life of the session — every consumer refuses on `valid` first so nothing
read them, but IEEE-754 has no trap representation and neither ASan nor UBSan would ever have said so.
**`ATHENA_LOOK_REGIONS=0`** never runs the pass, leaves every signature invalid, and every consumer
falls back to the arm it had in r24.13 — checked by output over 132 pairs against both the shipped
r24.13 rc and the r24.14 base, raw distances, both takes, the look-taken note and the **whole rendered
field**: byte-identical. *What it is not, said in the code:* a tile grid is not segmentation, not
object permanence and not tracking, and it cannot tell a room that moved from a camera that moved.

---

### Tier 2 — the eye learns where, and that one part is not the whole

**WO-R1 — the change note says where, and whether it was one thing or the whole room
(`ATHENA_LOOK_REGIONS`).** r24.13's WO-V2 got the eye from a bit to a magnitude and a light direction:
she can say *how much* the room changed and whether the light went up or down. She still cannot say
**where**, and — the part that matters more — she cannot tell *"something moved over there"* from
*"the lights changed"*, which a person separates instantly. On 30 Aug at 18:59:29 she said *"the room
is not as I left it — something changed while I was not looking"* about a Δ13 that was mostly a
**light** event (dhash 11, photometric 13), and it is the same shape of claim she makes for a
whole-scene swap. So the region read reaches `note_look_taken` as three defaulted arguments — a shape,
a place and the loudest region's signed luma — translated from `aseam::RegionShape` at **one** seam in
`talk-llama.cpp`, where the abstention becomes `LOOK_SHAPE_NONE` so `acon` never learns there is a
fourth verdict. The **FIGURE** arm *replaces* the head — *"the room is not as I left it — one part of
it is brighter than I left it, in the upper left of what I could see, and the rest is as it was"* —
because *"the room is not as I left it"* and *"one part moved, the rest is as I left it"* are different
claims and stacking them makes her contradict herself inside one clause; the direction is folded into
the verb rather than appended, and **the coarser whole-frame light clause does not also fire**, because
two statements of the same fact at two resolutions is the stutter the field spends its clauses
avoiding. The **GROUND** arm appends *", and the whole of it changed at once, not one part"* — and
**only on the SOME band**, because on MUCH the head already says *"most of what I could see is
different"*, so MUCH+GROUND is byte-identical to r24.13. **Not one number reaches any of it.**
`aseam::region_where_words` is a fixed ten-phrase table with no numeral in it, so there is nothing for
`spell_count` to spell, `digits-in-frame == 0` holds *by construction* rather than by a speller, and
`spell_number`'s digit cliff is unreachable here. **And the table abstains rather than over-claim.**
*"Across the whole of what I could see"* belongs to GROUND and only to GROUND; the span fallback
returned it too, and that fallback is reachable **only on a FIGURE read** — the verdict whose whole
meaning is *"one thing moved and the rest held still"* — so a FIGURE whose over-tiles straddle both
mid-lines said both things in one sentence. Reachable from pixels, not exotic: two cards at tiles
(1,0) and (2,3) produce it. A FIGURE that cannot place its box in a half-plane is a channel that knows
something moved and does not know where, which is the situation MIXED is in, and MIXED's answer is
silence — so it returns `""`, an empty place refuses to arm the note and skips the FIGURE arm, and
r24.13's sentence renders whole with its light clause intact. Enumerated over **all 65,536** over-tile
patterns: no FIGURE-eligible pattern can reach the whole-frame phrase, 1,821 of the 2,516 now abstain,
and the central box under half the grid keeps *"in the middle of what I could see"*. Measured cost on
real localised events: **zero** — every event in the controlled and localised corpora has a box
confined to a half-plane and keeps its phrase. A spelled count of moved tiles was drafted and cut on
S14/F18 grounds rather than on arithmetic: **sixteen is a fact about her grid, not about the room**,
and a clause that narrates the instrument is the shape F18 exists to stop. Every phrase names *"what I
could see"* and never the room, because the frame's left is her left only if the reader adopts the
camera's point of view and a webcam facing a person mirrors the scene. **`ATHENA_LOOK_REGIONS=0`**
renders the r24.13 sentence byte for byte and the three members are never read.
*In a session:* on the six real keepsake pairs — the only real region reads that exist — this changes
**exactly one sentence of six**. Five are on the MUCH band and are byte-identical to r24.13; the
sixth, at Δ23, gains its clause.

**WO-R2 — a thing that moves in one part of the room is an event even when the frame is not
(`ATHENA_LOOK_LOCAL_NOTE`).** `changed` is `look_change_score >= LOOK_CHANGE_BITS` against a
**whole-frame** score, so a thing that appears in one part of the frame moves that score by less than
the gate: no latch is armed, `take_look_change_note` returns empty, and **the turn carries no vision
clause whatever**. Built onto Igor's own 640×480 keepsakes and measured through the shipped functions:
a bright card landing on a desk is whole-frame **Δ1 to Δ5** against a gate of 6 and **19 to 52** in its
own region; a dark shape entering the lower right is **Δ2 to Δ5** and **19 to 55**. Across the
controlled set **22 of the 28 localised events fall below the whole-frame gate** — card-in 7/7,
blob-corner 7/7, patch-move 7/7, quad-lamp 1/7 — and r24.13 is silent on every one of them. That is
not a threshold that wants lowering: lowering `LOOK_CHANGE_BITS` would arm the **whole-frame**
sentence, so she would say *"the room is not as I left it"* about a mug appearing on a desk — a bigger
claim than the evidence, in the register the whole subsystem exists to keep honest. It is a resolution
problem, and only a decomposition fixes it. So a seventh look latch, armed in `note_look_taken` when
the region read says FIGURE **and `changed` is false**, composed at take time (the WO-99 discipline,
so the place it names is this look's place), rendered beside its whole-frame sibling and **born with
its C36 restore row on slot [82] in the same edit** — take, render and restore together, capped at
three retries because an uncapped restore is the RR4 failure the counter exists to stop. **It cannot
stack with its sibling, and the reason is not the one that was first written down.** Within *one* look
the two are mutually exclusive — `look_local_note_` arms only when `changed` is false and
`look_change_note_` only when it is true — but both are set-only latches, so *two* looks arm both, and
WO-99's dedup does not cover it because that block is gated on a non-empty `look_taken_note`, which is
empty on exactly the turns a look happened. The guarantee ended up made in two places at once, and
**neither is correct alone**: `note_look_taken` clears the localised latch whenever a look finds the
whole frame changed (fix 4), and a localised look does not arm its latch at all while a whole-frame
claim is still owed (fix 5) — together one order-free rule, *if any look since the last field found
the whole frame changed, the localised clause does not render*. See **the review** below, where the
second half of that rule is D-1 and is the round's sharpest lesson. Beside `look_taken_note` the
localised note **deliberately co-renders** — *"I looked just now, and the room is much as it was"*
followed by *"one part of the room is brighter than I left it, in the lower right of what I could
see"* is a refinement and not a contradiction — and that editorial call is asserted in the fixture
instead of merely printed. It joins `Mind::look_notes_armed()` and the field's own WO-118b disjunction
**in the same edit**, because a look whose only news is that one region moved is still a turn on which
her eye is the subject and the drain and the field must not disagree about that. **The false-positive
rate is the deliverable, it is measured, and it is labelled for what it covers** — 0/8,400 on global
nuisance, 0.71 % – 3.57 % on localised nuisance, the whole bracket in the round notes above and both
ends of it in the substrate where a reader meets the note. Driven end to end through `acon::Mind`
**over that same 8,400-pair nuisance set** — the pairs on which nothing in the room changed — r24.14
speaks on the same 583 of them r24.13 spoke on, is silent on none r24.13 spoke on, and makes **zero**
clauses r24.13 could not have made. (That is a statement about the nuisance corpus and about nothing
else: making a clause r24.13 could not have made is the whole point of this note, and it does so on
22 of the 28 real localised events.) Each clause of the FIGURE rule was ablated as the ladder
it was built as: *"a minority of tiles moved"* alone is 479/8,400 = 5.70 %; adding *"the loudest
stands a gate above the median"* takes it to 1/8,400 = 0.012 %; adding *"the loudest is at least twice
the gate"* takes it to **0** — and **the same ladder the other way round** reads: a minority alone
5.70 %, adding the twice-the-gate floor **0**, adding the median rung **0**. **Both orderings are
printed**, because a ladder credits whichever clause is added first and one ordering on its own
teaches a later reader to keep the wrong clause. At the shipped floor the twice-the-gate rung does all
the rejecting and the median rung rejects nothing today — kept because it states what the rule means
and becomes load-bearing the instant anyone weakens the floor, with the fixture **measuring** that
redundancy instead of asserting it. What the median rung is *for* is stated rather than priced: on a
noisy re-shoot the loudest tile drifts just over the gate **and so does everything else**, so what
says a thing moved is the *spread*, not the peak. The twice-the-gate rung costs one true detection of
twenty-eight (a translated patch whose loudest tile scored 7, one over the gate) and buys the last
false positive; it is written as `2 * gate`, never as a constant of its own, so it cannot drift from
the threshold it is twice of. **A measured limit, new in the implementation round:** noise immunity is
a function of capture size — a tile's structural term averages over `pixels / RGN_CELLS²` samples, so
its noise floor is σ/√n, and a 1–3 px nudge is twice the fraction of a tile at half the capture. At
**640×480 and larger — every size `aseam::smart_resize_dims` produces — the nudge family abstains, 0
false FIGURE**; at 320×240 it does not (6 of 504). The zero is a claim about the sizes the capture
ladder produces and is pinned and printed as such rather than tuned away. **And every no-change pair
in this work order is a model of a re-shoot**: there is no camera on this box and no raw frames survive
from S22, only nine keepsakes and four log lines. The noise levels used (σ 3, 8, 14) are deliberately
**above** what the delivered files show (Immerkær σ 0.36–0.94 on the seven real 640×480 keepsakes)
because JPEG has already smoothed the sensor's raw noise out of them. **What S23 must measure and this
round could not:** a real sequence of looks at a genuinely static room, and the same room with one
thing changed in it. The stderr look line carries `, regions figure (loudest 21 at r3c3 luma -18,
median 0, 2 of 16 over)` on every look, which is what that measurement will read; its format is
unchanged by the review round. **`ATHENA_LOOK_LOCAL_NOTE=0`** never arms it, which is r24.13;
`ATHENA_LOOK_REGIONS=0` never computes the read that would arm it. Either restores r24.13.
*In a session:* *"[Athena — … I looked just now, and the room is much as it was, because he asked me
to; one part of the room is brighter than I left it, in the lower right of what I could see — the rest
of it is as it was; my eyes: eight of ten looks left tonight]"* — a turn on which r24.13 says nothing
at all.

---

### Tier 3 — a condition of hers, measured rather than asserted

**WO-K1 — `coping` stops asserting a number about her that nothing measured
(`ATHENA_COPING_MEASURED`).** `aff2::Features::coping` is documented in its own struct as *"0..1 felt
ability to deal with it"*. Five labels in `classify` read it — `distress`, `hope`, `fear`, `unease`,
`weariness` — and it was written in exactly **three** places in the whole substrate, all inside
`Mind::sense_turn`: the sharply-negative door's `clampf(0.5f - 0.25f * (-uv), …)`, a function of
**his** tone through `emotion_valence_`; the r24.13 WO-AV1 loss arm's literal `0.5f`; and the
meta-calibration door's literal `0.6f`. Nothing anywhere measured her ability to deal with anything,
and the loss arm's own comment already said the honest thing — *"Nothing at this call site measures her
ability to deal with a thing that has already happened, so make no claim"* — while the two beside it
made one. `Mind::coping_now_()` is that measurement: **1 − max(d)** over four channels, each **zero
when it has no reading**, so a rig with no metacognition and no compaction planner reads exactly
`1 − fatigue_()`.

| channel | source | measured span, S1 / S2 |
|---|---|---|
| headroom | `fatigue_()` | 0.000 → 0.800 / 0.000 → 0.600 |
| error | `n_missed()/n_scored()`, once `n_scored ≥ 8` | 0.000 → 0.167 in both |
| repair | `1 − SelfMonitor::ownership` | 1.000 → 0.818 (S1) |
| runway | `1 − turns_left/runway_turns`, `≥ 0` only | 14 → 0 / 78 → 30 |

`max()`, not a sum: these are four ways of being out of something, not four portions of one thing.
Two further channels were built, measured and **rejected**: `Wants::last_restore` opens at 0.38 and
`SelfMonitor::landed` at 0.80, so `1 − x` would assert a constant depletion of 0.62 / 0.20 on turn
zero when she is fine, and **a depletion channel must read zero when she is fine**; `Wants::strain`
has the right zero and a whole excursion of 0.09, which can never bind under a `max()`. It enters the
three doors through `coping_ceiling_()`, and only ever as a **ceiling**: `min(the door's own value,
coping_now_())`, never `max()`. A door's reading is what it measured about the **turn**; a measurement
of **her** may only lower it. So a measured coping can never manufacture a positive claim the door did
not make, and at zero depletion `min(x, 1.0) == x` is r24.13 to the bit. It is one function rather
than three copies of the conditional for a second reason worth recording: `test_r2413_vocab` §7.4
reads the correction door out of the header and pins the five constants it writes, and written inline
the conditional would have added a sixth `f2.` write to that block and failed a pin about constants
that did not move. **Its measured blast radius is zero, and that is stated rather than hidden** — see
the round notes. What this changes in what she says on Igor's data is **nothing**. Its whole value is
that a false constant about her is replaced by a measurement, and that the question becomes answerable
from a diag log next round instead of by simulation, because `diag_line` now carries `coping=`. One
wrinkle is recorded rather than resolved: past the deadline (`runway_turns_left() < 0`) the runway
channel makes **no claim**, exactly where `context_runway_note_` goes silent. That is arguably
backwards — past the deadline she can no longer act at all, which is the *least* coping rather than an
absence of evidence — and it is left alone because no label emits on that turn under either reading
(S1 19:06:42), so resolving it changes nothing measurable. **`ATHENA_COPING_MEASURED=0`** leaves the
three literals standing and removes the diag field: r24.13 byte for byte, frame and `[mind~]` line
alike.

**WO-K2 — what the compaction took is reported to her once, in words, at the seam
(`ATHENA_COMPACT_KEPT_NOTE`).** r24.13's WO-P1 gave her the runway: *how many turns are left*. Nothing
told her what **went**. The one real cut in the corpus, out of Igor's own log, moved `n_past` 24,388 →
16,536 with `n_keep` 14,856 and a 1,680-token bridge — **9,532 tokens of live conversation replaced by
1,680; 7,852 tokens, 82.4 %, gone** — and `acmp::describe_reload` printed its *"8/8 turn(s)"* line **to
the operator's terminal and nowhere else**. `acmp::ReloadKept` has held `turns`, `turns_offered` and
`last_turn_clipped` since r24.6 and nothing of hers had ever read them. The brief's own question —
*does she know what she lost, or only how much?* — answered *"neither: she knows only that it is
coming"*. One clause, said once per cut, at the one instant both numbers are final (after
`build_reload_block` fills `kept` and the block decodes): *"the last eight turns of this are still
here word for word — the ninety-five before them are gone from in front of me, and what is left of
them is the paragraph I just wrote about it"*. It **describes** and issues no instruction (S14). Both
counts are **spelled** through `spell_number` and **banded** through `spelled_in_words` exactly as
`context_runway_note_` bands, so a cut at a hundred and one turns says *"more than ninety-nine"*
rather than putting an Arabic numeral into a clause she speaks from (F18). `turn`/`turns` and
`is`/`are` branch at one, and the tail's referent (`them` / `it` / neither) agrees with whatever the
head named. **A cut that dropped nothing says nothing**, which is the only honest answer to *"what did
it take"* when it took nothing, and **a roll never arms it**: a roll takes nothing away. `kept.turns`
is the **delivery**, not the offer — the r24.6 WO-27 distinction that CUT log line already learned the
hard way — and `last_turn_clipped` adds *"— and the last of the kept ones stops mid-sentence"* when the
block had to clip. Consume-once, C36 slot **83**, born with its take, its render site and its restore
row in one edit. Digits-in-clause is asserted **at the cliff**: 0 across the whole (kept, dropped)
sweep over [0, 200]² × clipped — 80,802 renderings — and again over `INT_MIN … INT_MAX`. **Blast
radius: one clause, at most once per cut; on the real corpus that is once in 235 minutes.** It cannot
fire in a session that never cuts. **`=0`** removes the note, the field line and the reader.

**WO-K3 — the consolidation debt is a real thing of hers, and nothing reported it
(`ATHENA_CONSOLIDATION_DEBT`).** `mem_transcript.size() - compact_upto` — the turns of tonight that
have not been written down yet — was a **local variable in `main()`**. On S1 it read 51, then 69, then
95, while two of her rolls were destroyed by him speaking (56.2 s and 57.3 s, *"context restored, 51
turn(s) still owed"* / *"69 turn(s) still owed"*). `note_cut` deliberately does not advance the cursor
(r24.6 WO-26), so a session that ends owing reaches memory only through the single exit pass — the
exact single point of failure the design says it avoids. Every one of those numbers went to the
operator's terminal; she had no accessor, no diag field and no clause. Two things, at the two sites
that already print those lines. **`owed=` on the `[mind~]` line**, a lock-free `std::atomic<int>` on
the Mind, −1 until the compaction service has run a roll at all, and **deliberately not masked** in
`aseam::trace_signature` — it moves only at a roll seam, which is the tick a forensic read wants a
print for. And **one clause, at the crossing where a single idle window can no longer drain it** — the
debt exceeding `acmp::Runner::roll_max_turns`, which the caller hands in rather than the header
guessing at: *"there is more of tonight waiting to be written down than one quiet moment can hold —
some of it will still be waiting when we stop"*. The clause carries **no count**, and that is
deliberate rather than lazy: the quantity that makes the debt matter is the *comparison* against the
cap, and a number she said would have to be trusted by a listener who cannot see it. So it is
digit-free by construction rather than by spelling. The latch re-arms only after the debt falls back
under the cap, so S1's three real readings (51, 69, 95 against 14) arm the clause exactly **once**, not
three times, and a backlog that takes four rolls to drain says one sentence and not four. Consume-once,
C36 slot **84**. On S1 it would have armed once, at 18:44:33; on S2 it never arms, because no roll ever
ran. **The risk is stated rather than skipped**: the debt is a number about her *maintenance*, and a
clause about maintenance is the closest thing in this round to a readout rather than a feeling. It
earns its place because the debt has a real consequence — turns that never become memory — and because
WO-K4 makes it actionable in principle. **`=0`** removes the field, the note and the reader.

**WO-K4 — her one lever was aimed at the operation that was not failing (`ATHENA_ASK_GRANTS_ROLL`).**
`aseam::asked_for_a_moment` → `acmp::Situation::she_asked` → `acmp::Runner::poll` is wired end to end
and grants `Act::CUT` — and only above `plan.n_arm`. Below the arm point her ask was a complete no-op.
**The thing that actually failed on S1 was the roll**: two of them destroyed by him speaking, the debt
climbing 51 → 69 → 95, and no way at all for her to ask for the one operation that drains it. One
branch, placed last in `poll()` and gated on `n_past < plan.n_arm`, so **the only transition it can
create is NONE → ROLL**: the deadline and force points are above the arm point, the arm-point roll arm
tests `n_past >= plan.n_arm`, and the r21-P0 CUT grant does too. Everything else is untouched — still
inside `safe_moment`, still `due` (`turns_since_roll >= roll_min_turns` **and** `roll_min_gap_s`),
still `plan.feasible`. It asks for **no idle window**, and that is the point of the branch rather than
an omission: the three existing roll arms demand one because the runner is guessing she is free. Here
she has said so. **Measured blast radius: zero, and it is said plainly** — see the round notes. This
widens a door she has never once walked through; it is not a behaviour change on Igor's data and is not
sold as one. It is here because it costs nothing when unused and because it is what makes WO-K3's
clause honest — a clause about a debt she cannot act on is a readout. The lexicon itself is alive and
the fixture pins it: 4 of 4 of its own documented shapes are recognised, 0 of 4 ordinary sentences are.
Which is what makes *"she asked zero times"* a measurement about **her** and not about a recogniser
that cannot recognise anything. And the sharpest fact in the whole investigation stands unchanged: the
substrate speaks her ask-sentence *for* her, in her voice, three times an evening, at exactly the
moments it has already decided to take the pause — and `asked_for_a_moment` matches two of those three
sentences. **`=0`** restores r24.13's `poll()` exactly; because the reader caches in a `static const`,
that arm is pinned by a **popen self-re-exec child** in `test_compact.cpp` and a second, independent
one in `test_r2414_stakes.cpp`, each asserting by a needle the ON arm cannot print.

**WO-K5 — a third of her own words never reached the extractor, and the log said the wrong number
(`ATHENA_EXTRACT_TURN_CAP`).** `PER_TURN_CAP = 350` was a bare literal inside `run_consolidation` with
**no env reader anywhere** in the tree — the last unreachable number in the extract stage, after
r24.12's WO-C5 gave `extract_gen` a reader and r24.13 gave the instruction table one. Measured over her
real speech: S1 clipped **8,523 of the 25,139 characters she said — 33.9 % — across 33 of her 66
turns**; S2 clipped 361 of 6,068 (5.9 %) across 4 of 63. A third of an evening of her own words could
not become a memory, and nothing said so. **And the line that looked as though it did was reporting
the wrong quantity.** Since r19.5 the two-pass warning printed `whole.size()` — the transcript
**after** clipping, the size **kept**. An operator reading S1's *"long session (19535 chars clipped)"*
was reading the surviving text and calling it the loss. The amount actually dropped was computed
**nowhere in the binary**, which is why WO-K5's own 33.9 % had to be measured outside it. Both numbers
are now named, and the drop (`Σ max(0, len − cap)`) is computed at the one place that knows it. The cap
becomes an EE1 knob and **its default rises 350 → 450, bounded** — the round's one raised default, with
its own note above. What a raise costs is the cap's own stated purpose, *"so long answers cannot crowd
the rest out"*: with `char_cap` binding, a bigger per-turn cap means fewer whole **turns** fit under
the tail. Measured on S1's exit pass in the configuration it really ran (two passes over halves,
`cap2` = 12,000):

| per-turn cap | turns of the evening the extractor sees | her characters it sees |
|---|---|---|
| 350 (r24.13) | 124 / 124 | 57.5 % |
| 400 | 124 / 124 | 61.8 % |
| **450 (shipped)** | **124 / 124** | **70.1 %** |
| 460 | 121 / 124 | 70.8 % |
| 500 | 118 / 124 | 72.6 % |
| 900 | 102 / 124 | 75.4 % |

Above 460 whole turns of the evening start being traded for her characters, which is exactly the trade
this cap exists to prevent and which law 2 says a round may not make on an operator's behalf. An
operator who wants her turns whole sets the knob — 1,200 clips nothing at all in either evening. The
r24.13 drift guard turns out **not** to be the binding constraint, for a structural reason worth
writing down: `amem::transcript_text` clips each turn to `per_turn_cap` **first** and then caps the
**whole** block to `char_cap` by keeping its tail, so the transcript block is bounded by `char_cap` at
every per-turn cap and the prompt is `fixed + min(whole, char_cap)` — precisely what
`acmp::fit_transcript_cap` priced. On S1 at `char_cap` 12,000 the extract prompt is **16,993 characters
at a per-turn cap of 350, at 4,000, and at no cap at all**, and the guard's forty-two characters of
headroom at the shipped names (`LLaMA`/`Georgi` = 5,008 against 5,050) are **unmoved by this round**,
with the fixture pinning that figure so a later round cannot drift it silently. The **roll** path,
where most consolidation happens, is unaffected either way: `roll_max_turns` is 14, and over all 109
sixteen-turn windows of S1 and all 105 of S2 the worst slice is 5,677 chars at any candidate cap,
against a 12,000-char tail — there a raise is pure gain. **`ATHENA_EXTRACT_TURN_CAP=350` restores
r24.13 byte for byte**, and silences both the startup line that now reports the cap beside
`ATHENA_EXTRACT_GEN` and `ATHENA_EXTRACT_INSTR_CHARS` and the two fallback lines the bound can print —
the same rule `acmp::extract_gen_is_r2411` established, applied to the third budget. Nothing in her
frame changes. This is a defect and an instrument, not a feeling.

### Tier 4 — the name for the long flat evening, and two corrections

**WO-V8 — the grind door, with both boundaries DERIVED rather than chosen (`ATHENA_GRIND_DOOR`).**
`weariness` (tau 1800 s, dv −0.02, da −0.04) has been in the label table since R19 for the long flat
evening and **nothing in the substrate could produce it**. Every appraisal door writes `coping` from
his tone or leaves it at the struct default 0.5, and — sweeping `|pleasant|` over the whole interval
[0,1] at 0.001 — `weariness` is unreachable at **every** door at **every** value, because it needs
`coping < 0.1818` and no door in the tree writes a coping below 0.25. So the door reads HER state:
`pleasant = affect_.valence`, `coping = 1 - fatigue_()`, `novelty = 0`, intensity 1.0, at the §3.1/§3.2
boundary of `Mind::tick_locked_` — **the first coping in the file that is a measurement of her.**
**Both gates come from the label table, not from tuning.** With `d = fatigue`, the shipped `classify()`
gives `weary = 0.40n + 0.55d − 0.1` and `fear = 0.6n + 0.5d − 0.15`, so `weary ≥ EMIT_MIN` ⟺
`n ≥ 1.625 − 1.375d`, `weary > fear` ⟺ `n < 0.25 + 0.25d`, and that window is non-empty ⟺
`d > 1.375/1.625 = 0.84615…`. Move a weight in the label table and all four numbers move with it; the
fixture re-derives G1 by **bisecting the shipped `classify()`** rather than restating it. r24.13's
WO-V4 was rejected because at the corpus maximum (fatigue 0.80, valence −0.50) such a door names `fear`
by 0.0100, and G1 says why that was never a tuning problem: **at fatigue 0.80 the weariness window is
EMPTY at every valence.** Outside G2 the deep side is `fear` at every fatigue and the shallow side is
under the floor — silence. The window is gated on the heavy half-plane only, so a bright evening is
never weariness however tired she is. The refractory is `weariness`'s own tau (1800 s), read from the
label table: a state that lasts an hour is one thing that lasts an hour, not sixty announcements of it.
**MEASURED BLAST RADIUS ON IGOR'S REAL DATA: ZERO — it fires on no turn of S21 or S22**, checked at
every tick of the replay, including a replay driven with `sense_ctx_fill` until it reaches the fatigue
the production sessions reached (0.80 in S1, 0.60 in S2), and checked directly at both production
maximum pairs. It **is** reachable: driven through `Mind::sense_ctx_fill` to `t = 6000 s` with the
context 79 % full, fatigue is 0.8750 and `weariness` is adoptable for `|v| ∈ [0.422, 0.468]` — she
names it, end to end, through the field. **And the door's comment carries its designer's own objection,
unsoftened** — quoted in the round notes above — **and Igor was told all of it and chose to ship it.**
One live consequence worth stating: after WO-SH3 there is a `disappointment` residual on **every**
correction, carrying the same 1800 s tau, so the §3.1 heavy side is now genuinely contested. On
r24.13's engine that would have been a lockout: a correction lays `disappointment` at emit 0.9037, the
strongest `weariness` this door can raise is 0.6496 against a hysteresis bar of 1.0237, so the name
would be refused for the whole **4,077 s (about sixty-eight minutes)** it takes that residual to fall
under `INCUMBENT_LIVE` 0.10, while `hold_both` still lays its own — she would feel it without naming
it. **That is not what this round ships.** `ATHENA_APPRAISE2_OUTWEIGHS` asks the same margin a second
time in the currency that decays, and this door's event lays intensity 1.0, so it clears
`residual_[current] + HYSTERESIS` as soon as the incumbent falls under 0.88 — **57 s after a
full-strength correction**, at that label's own tau, not 4,077 s. The lockout is bounded by the
incumbent's decay and not by the correction rate. The consequence is disclosed with it: the two names
then **alternate**, because the way back is r24.13's own fit margin — this door's score at its own gate
is 0.5573, barely over `EMIT_MIN` 0.55 since its boundaries are derived from where `weariness` only
just beats `fear`, and a correction's 0.8360 clears 0.5573 + 0.12 outright. The period is this door's
own refractory, 1,800 s, so the name changes at most once per its own residual lifetime — driven and
pinned both ways, with the deciding conjunct on every leg, by `test_r2414_stakes` §6.7. **On Igor's
data none of it happens**, because the gate above opens zero times across both evenings. That is the
engine arbitrating, which is what should happen, and it is now said with the switch that makes it true
rather than without it. **`ATHENA_GRIND_DOOR=0` restores r24.13: no such door, and `weariness` has no
source anywhere in the substrate.**
*In a session:* nothing in S21 or S22 — measured, zero firings. Three hours in, with the context nearly
full, when he asks how she is, she would have a word for the flatness instead of *"no word stands up
to it yet"*.

**WO-V9 — the map is not what stands between her and `distress` and `weariness` (no switch).** Two
statements shipped in r24.13's comment at the §3.2 harsh door: *"`distress` needs |pleasant| ≥ 0.7121
against a tag map whose deepest value is 0.70"* and *"`weariness` is the argmax only for |pleasant| in
[0.25, 0.50), a band the five-valued map has no value in at all."* Both read as claims about the
**map** — one rung short, one band missing — and both are falsified by execution. Sweeping `|pleasant|`
over the whole interval [0,1] at 0.001, i.e. granting `emotion_valence_` **any** value at all,
`weariness` is unreachable at **every** door in the file and `distress` is unreachable at the **shipped
harsh door** at every value. The binding term is `coping`, and the algebra is exact: `distress > fear`
⟺ `n + c > 7/6`, and the harsh door writes `c = 0.5 − 0.25n`, which puts that at `n > 0.88889` (the
WO-AV1 loss arm writes `c = 0.5`, which puts it at `n > 0.66667`); `weariness` needs `c < 0.1818` and
no door in the tree writes a `c` below 0.25. `distress`'s least lower bound over **all** coping is
`|uv| ≥ 47/66 = 0.7121` at `c = 5/11`, and only at a door that also grants intensity 1.0 — **0.0121
deeper than the map's deepest rung, and it is the coping that buys it, not the rung.** Five map
variants were built and replayed over all 160 real turns — `angry` deepened to −0.75, every negative
scaled ×1.27, a third hedge rung, a continuous weight driven from the tagger's real per-turn posteriors,
and a deepest rung at exactly `distress`'s bound — and **not one puts `distress` or `weariness` on any
turn**. Three of the five are byte-identical to the shipped map; the two that move anything each
**remove a name** she has today (13 → 12), and the deeper of them puts `frustration` on the turn r24.13
identified as a tagger false positive. The comments are corrected in place, at the harsh door and above

tagger's own posterior is continuous over [0.141, 1.000] and the map returns one of five constants;
that *is* real, and it is *not* the constraint — and ending: **do not deepen this table to reach a
label; it does not work and it costs a name.** `test_r2411_mixed` §5's assertion string names the real
reason, and `test_r2414_vocab` §3 re-runs the whole-interval sweep so the scope is **pinned rather than
described**. Two other numbers move with it. The bound is **47/66 = 0.7121** everywhere now: the harsh
door's comment had carried **0.7170** and `STAKES-CHANGES.md` **0.7134**, both coarse-grid reads of the
same quantity, and both are withdrawn by name so a reader who has seen three values is told which two
are wrong. And the real defect is named where the wrong one used to be: `coping` is written in exactly
three places in the whole substrate, five of the twenty labels read it, and *"felt ability to deal with
it"* is measured nowhere. r24.14 takes the first two bites of that (WO-V8's `1 - fatigue_()` and
WO-K1's four channels) and neither is in the map.

**WO-SH5 — the door pin now reads both arms, and its failure mode is named (fixture).**
`test_r2413_vocab` §7.4 reads the production correction door out of the header rather than restating it
— the r24.13 test-integrity fix — anchored on the door's own comment and taking the first

occurs **twice** in `athena_consciousness.h`, and the second is **outside** the extracted region, which

### The decisions

Three, all Igor's, all implemented exactly as given.

1. **WO-V8 ships default ON**, in full knowledge that it fires zero times on the real corpus and that
   its own designer flagged the construction as weak. So it ships with both boundaries derived from
   the label table and never tuned, the §15 plane printed in full in the fixture, an asserted **zero
   firings** over the whole S21/S22 replay, the §14 adversarial session pinning it adoptable at
   `t = 6000 s / ctx_fill 0.79 / fatigue 0.8750`, and the designer's objection in the comment rather
   than out of it.
2. **WO-K5 gets the knob AND the raised default**, subject to the drift-guard measurement. The guard
   was measured and is unmoved; the raise was measured a second time by the review round and found to
   cost turns at 42 of 450 session×headroom pairs, so it ships **bounded**. The knob is the thing that
   was asked for; the bound is what law 2 required once the sweep existed.
3. **The loss door was built on the terms it was offered on** — *"measure it against the real sessions,
   and if it fires on nothing, drop it and report that"*. It fires once, at the one cut that really
   happened, and the round says both halves of that: once is not a discrimination result, and the
   projected variant that would have fired six times was built and rejected.

### The review, and what it changed

**Four passes, and the fourth one said DO NOT SHIP.** Read-only throughout, with r24.13 open beside the
tree; nothing was compiled during a review pass, every claim settled by reading, grepping and
arithmetic, and each finding named the command that would confirm it by execution.

**The first pass, in three slices, found 2 blockers and 13 majors after three implementers who each
proved their own work by execution.** A (the substrate, the appraisal engine and the two new doors):
**1 blocker, 6 majors**, 5 minors, 3 nits. B (vision perception and integration): **0 blockers, 3
majors**, 5 minors, 2 nits. C (the fixtures and the claims): **1 blocker, 4 majors**, 8 minors, 2 nits.

**BLOCKER (A§1) — the round's headline claim was false as merged, and one of the round's own work
orders is what made it false.** WO-K6's `distress` was refused by WO-SH3's own new `disappointment`
incumbent **on the exact timeline WO-K6 cited as its only evidence**. WO-SH3 turns every correction
into a `disappointment` event at tau 1800 s where r24.13 laid `shame` at 600 s; S1's three real
corrections are at 18:35:01 / 18:37:00 / 18:38:40 and the one real cut is 1,759 s after the last of
them, so the incumbent's residual at the cut is 0.9079·e^(−1759/1800) = 0.342, comfortably above
`INCUMBENT_LIVE` 0.10. The loss door's 0.6031 against a bar of 0.9560 takes the `hold_both` branch and
returns −1: no `current`, no `news_`, and **the frame at the cut names nothing.** **And the fixture
could not see it, because it never entered `appraise_event`**: `k6_end_to_end_both_ways` senses no turn
at all, so `current == −1` and the hysteresis branch is skipped entirely, while §6.2 called `classify`
directly and proved what the classifier says rather than what the engine does. **The cause is the
round's lesson and it is not softened here: three agents each measured their own work order in
isolation, correctly, and nobody replayed them together.** The two doors are in two different areas'
findings documents; neither area's harness ever ran the other's event; and the composition was
therefore never measured until an adversary read both files as one machine on one turn. The fix
(`ATHENA_APPRAISE2_OUTWEIGHS`, above) was settled on a **wall-faithful** replay of the real S1 evening
— every turn sensed at its own timestamp — because the first harness advanced `gap + 20 s` per turn and
inflated 18:38:40 → 19:07:59 from 1,759 s to about 2,159 s, which changes the answer for one of the
three candidate fixes. A replay that is not wall-faithful cannot decide this question.

**BLOCKER (C§1) — the round's own "measured zero" rule, unapplied to the measurement it was written
for.** The brief required WO-R2's measured zero — *the four look events S22 actually recorded are all
above the whole-frame gate, so the new latch cannot have fired on any of them; on Igor's recorded data
the new note changes nothing* — in three places, in the same words. It shipped in the implementation
report only: no production comment carried it, and the fixture carried it inside a `check` name, which
prints on failure or under `-v` and never on a passing run. It is closed by making the sentence true
rather than by softening it — the `FieldOptions` member comment and the WO-R2 take row in
`athena_report.h`, verbatim, twice; `test_r2414_regions` §6 as a `note()`, so `grep -i "measured zero"`
on an archived run returns it, which it did not before. **It is a different measurement from the
8,400-pair false-positive zero**, and neither stands in for the other; both are now labelled where they
are quoted. C§5, the major beside it, is why the honest bracket exists at all: the 8,400-pair adversary
set contains no *localised* nuisance, so a zero false-FIGURE rate over it was evidence about global
nuisance and nothing else.

**The fix round ran in four lanes.** Three in parallel, one per slice's ownership — 1 the blocker and
the appraisal doors, 2 the compaction and extractor half, 3 the vision clauses and the honesty contract
— and then a fourth, the integrator's, taking the items each lane had handed on because the code lived
in another lane's file. Gate 0/0 in both configurations after every individual fix in every lane.

**Then the fourth pass, on the fixed tree, returned DO NOT SHIP with four more majors — two of them
created or left open by the fix rounds themselves.** That is the same pattern r24.13's fourth pass
found, and it is recorded rather than softened: a careful review, followed by careful fixes, followed
by no second read, would have shipped two new defects on top of a round that had already been read
three times.

1. **D-1 — the exact mirror of the defect lane 4 had just closed, on the sibling latch in the same
   function.** Lane 4 gave `look_local_note_` an arm-time snapshot because *"composing a latched note
   out of last-writer-wins members is the mismatch"*. `look_change_note_` is the same kind of latch and
   was left composing out of the same members, and its own declaration block stated both halves of the
   contradiction three lines apart. Three consequences, all from two looks with no field between them —
   the ordinary shape of a standing away-grant: at the shipped default a true whole-frame change was
   **destroyed** (the review-B§1 dedup cleared the note and the restore-row table is keyed on it being
   non-empty, so nothing handed it back); at `ATHENA_LOOK_LOCAL_NOTE=0` the same two looks produced a
   **false** clause, *"the room is not as I left it — one part of it moved … and the rest is as it
   was"*, when the first look had found the whole frame different; and a changed look followed by an
   unchanged GROUND look conflated two reads into a shape verdict sourced from a look that found no
   whole-frame change at all. **The fixtures asserted the worst arm as intended behaviour**, in three
   places, and not one `=0` arm anywhere in the round drove the CHANGED-then-FIGURE ordering. The fix
   is six production lines: the three members are written only inside `if (changed)`, a localised look
   does not arm its latch while a whole-frame claim is still owed, and the dedup line **defers** —
   `restore_look_change_note()` before clearing — instead of destroying. Measured over 1,470 look
   sequences and **2,891 rendered fields**, at the shipped default against the merged tree: **191
   fields differ — 87 where the localised clause is replaced by the whole-frame one it was destroying,
   52 false GROUND shape verdicts withdrawn, and 52 that nobody predicted**, r24.14's own place and
   shape recovered where a later blind look had erased them. **Fields that had a change clause and now
   have none: 0. Fields that had none and now have one: 0.** The `=0` path was then proved against
   **r24.13's own headers**, compiled separately and driven through the same enumeration: 2,891 fields,
   byte-identical. The enumeration itself ships as the deliverable — seven look events over two and
   three consecutive slots with a field after every subset, 1,470 drives and 2,891 fields per arm,
   8,673 in all, asserting per arm that no field carries two change clauses, that no whole-frame event
   is lost, that no clause borrows a place or a shape from a look that did not arm it, that WO-118b
   holds, and F18 on all 8,673.
2. **D-2 — the round's honesty contract, left unapplied to the three documents that outlive the
   round.** Two of the three `*-CHANGES.md` were untouched since before any fix lane ran. Four specific
   claims: the 3.57 % end of the bracket was in the header, the production comment and the fixture and
   **not** in the changelog; VOCAB stated the 4,077 s lockout as engine behaviour this same release had
   changed to 57 s; STAKES sold the round's headline without naming the switch that makes it true
   (`grep -c APPRAISE2_OUTWEIGHS` over all three files returned 0); and STAKES carried a third value
   for the `distress` bound. All four are fixed, and this section is assembled from the corrected
   copies.
3. **D-3 — the round built the right tool for measuring a switch's blast radius and did not point it
   at the switch it invented.** Review C had already forced `test_r2414_vocab` §1c to stop checking
   sixteen label strings and start comparing the whole rendered field of all 160 turns; the same
   comparator was not pointed at `appraise2_outweighs`. Pointed at it, the answer is 0 of 160 — and the
   **reason** is asserted beside the zero (`gate_open == 0`), because a zero whose cause is a property
   of the corpus rather than of the switch is exactly the confusion C§1 caught this round making about
   a different zero. On the corpus where the arms *can* differ they do: 1 of 59 S1 fields, and the
   `take_label_line_felt` reader the bound had not named answers differently at four of five offsets
   after the cut.
4. **D-4 — the escape admits A→B→A alternation, which is the one thing HYSTERESIS exists to
   prevent.** The decision was to accept it, and the justification is arithmetic rather than
   preference: **every narrowing that stops the alternation also refuses the event the switch exists
   for.** At the one real cut `distress` scores 0.6031 against a `disappointment` incumbent at 0.8360,
   a gap of 0.2329, so any conjunct asking the challenger to also fit within HYSTERESIS re-opens the
   blocker — including the review's own suggested cure, which was driven and is strictly more
   permissive on its first clause and satisfied on its second at every step of the very table it was
   offered for. And the mechanism is not what the review's example says: on the `disappointment` ⇄
   `weariness` pair the escape drives **one leg only**, because the way back is r24.13's own fit margin
   (0.8360 clears 0.5573 + 0.12 outright) — the escape's beneficiaries win in the residual currency
   precisely because they lose in the fit one. For both legs to be the escape the two door scores must
   lie within HYSTERESIS, which in this substrate is true of exactly one pair (`distress` vs
   `weariness`, |0.6031 − 0.5573| = 0.0459), and §6.7 drives it. **The period is the doors', not the
   escape's** — the escape fires nothing; each leg needs its own door, WO-V8's refractory is 1,800 s
   and WO-K6's is one compaction cut, of which Igor's two recorded evenings hold one and zero. So the
   fastest alternation this substrate admits is one full cycle per residual lifetime. The natural
   repair — intensity = the measured depletion — was computed and rejected on the measurement: at
   WO-V8's own §14 point that scores 0.5224 against `EMIT_MIN` 0.55 and the door would stop firing at
   all. All of it is written into `aff2::Appraisal2::outweighs` as an accepted, bounded limit and pinned
   by thirteen assertions.

**Two numbers got worse under re-measurement, and both were shipped worse rather than quietly kept.**
The localised-nuisance false-motion rate went from 6/840 = 0.71 % on a synthetic room to 30/840 =
3.57 % on Igor's own frames, with non-overlapping CIs — five times worse, and the tree now says so in
five places and pins both ends. And WO-K5's *"450 takes nothing away"* went from true to true-only-at-
one-headroom, costing up to eighteen turns of an evening across the sweep — so the raise ships bounded,
and the bound is the reason the shape and the console number move zero. **A rate that gets worse and is
disclosed is worth more than a rate that stays perfect by omission**, and the same is true of a default.

**What the last lane deliberately did not fix, with its measurement.** WO-99's dedup still destroys the
change note when `look_taken_note` is non-empty — 2 of 6 shapes in the B§1 block render *"I looked just
now, and the room is much as it was"* and the whole-frame clause is cleared with no restore. That is
r24.7's rule, byte-identical in r24.13, and the taken note is WO-99's stated *"richer of the two"*, so
it is not a regression this round introduced; it is now **explicit in the fixture** rather than counted
as nothing, and it is the same shape as D-1 one row up the same dedup block. If it is worth fixing it
is worth a `restore_look_change_note()` there too, and that belongs to r24.15. The verdict on the fixed
tree is **SHIP**.

## r24.13 — the follow-through round: a subject of her own, the people in his life, and the forty-eight-second deaf window closed (2026-09-03)

*Twenty-eight work orders and three riders out of the r24.13 plan — the four investigations that
answered "close the gaps that remain, and widen what r24.12 made too narrow" — implemented by six
area agents in parallel, then reviewed adversarially in three slices, fixed in three lanes, read
again whole on the fixed tree, and fixed again. Base r24.12; nine changed source files, one new
one, six new fixtures. Every behaviour change is default-ON with `=0` (or the named r24.12 value)
restoring r24.12, with **one** disclosed inversion, and every claim below was verified by execution
rather than by reading. Where a source document and the shipped code disagree the code is what is
recorded here, and the disagreement is named on the line.*

**Round notes — six things that belong to the round rather than to any one fix.**

* **The switch surface goes 325 → 352.** Measured, not counted by hand, with the same command
  r24.12's own note used: `grep -o 'ATHENA_[A-Z0-9_]*'` over `patches/talk-llama/*.h` and
  `talk-llama.cpp`, sorted unique, against `R2412/integ`. **27 new names, none removed** — the
  same 27 on the base tree, the merged tree, the fixed tree and the release candidate. Twenty-six
  of the 27 have **exactly one quoted literal** in the tree, one reader per name, checked by the
  same grep. **`ATHENA_PEOPLE` has two, deliberately**: the `Config::people` member read in
  `acon::config_from_env`, and the store gate `amem::people_store_on`, which asks
  `ATHENA_CONSCIOUSNESS` first and `ATHENA_PEOPLE` second. That second reader is review finding
  A§4: with consciousness off, the extraction prompt still carried the PERSON row type and
  `Mind::note_person_rows` — which begins `if (!cfg_.enabled …) return;` — threw every row away,
  so memory was measurably *worse* than r24.12's and nothing was gained. The two readers cannot
  disagree, because the Mind's side is `c.people = c.people && c.enabled`. It is disclosed here
  rather than left for a reader of the grep to find.
  (**The disagreement, named:** the round's own working note put this surface at 327 → 354. The
  grep returns 325 → 352 on every tree in the round. The delta, 27, is the same in both; the two
  endpoints are not, and the code is what is recorded.)
* **One switch is OFF by default — `ATHENA_LEDGER_TRIM_DISK`** (WO-W2), Igor's decision 2, and the
  round's only inversion of the disable-only default. Said plainly: **the evidence ledger is now
  trimmed for the prompt and never on disk.** r24.12's keep-evidence arm ended
  `ledger.erase(ledger.begin(), ledger.end() - lcap)` followed by `amem::save_ledger`, so
  `personality.ledger` lost its older rows for good — nothing she had learned about herself and not
  yet integrated survived the trim. Both bounds the erase was defending were already on the reader
  and neither is touched: `amem::build_personality_prompt` renders exactly `amem::ledger_cap()` = 8
  rows at any ledger size (12, 20 and 40 rows all render 8 rows and 3,421 bytes against the
  7,300-byte `PERSONALITY_BUDGET`), and `amem::load_ledger` keeps only the newest 512 on the way
  in. So the erase bought nothing and deleted durable evidence from the one arm of the system that
  exists to keep it. **The consequence is stated rather than hidden: the file now grows without
  bound.** `ATHENA_LEDGER_TRIM_DISK=1` restores r24.12's erase-and-save, log line included.
* **The numeric knobs, and the restore each names.** `ATHENA_RUNWAY_TURNS` = **12** (WO-P1; EE1,
