### The review, and what it changed

**Four passes, and the fourth one said DO NOT SHIP.** Read-only throughout, with r24.12 open beside
the tree; nothing was compiled during a review pass, every claim settled by reading, grepping and
arithmetic, and each finding named the command that would confirm it by execution.

**The first pass, in three slices, found 2 blockers and 12 majors after six careful implementers.**
A (`talk-llama.cpp`, `athena_seam.h`, the switch surface): **1 blocker, 3 majors**, 5 minors,
2 nits. B (the substrate: `athena_consciousness.h`, `athena_report.h`): **1 blocker, 6 majors**,
3 minors, 4 nits. C (the other headers, the new file, and all fourteen fixtures): **0 blockers,
3 majors**, 9 minors, 9 nits. The two blockers are worth naming individually, because both were
invisible to a green suite by construction:

**BLOCKER (A§1) — the look tape armed while her own announce was still coming out of the speaker,
and whisper would have handed it back as HIS turn.** The whole justification for putting WO-X1's
window *inside* `vision_drain_eval` rather than at the call site — stated in the work order and
repeated in its implementation report — depends on the announce having finished playing before
`vision_drain_eval` is entered. It had not. `athena_vision_seam_drain` plays the announce and then
waits for the mini-session's `.done` with a **bounded** poll: fifty iterations of a 50 ms sleep, a
hard ceiling of **2.5 s**, after which it falls through and calls `vision_drain_eval` regardless. It
does not use `stream_tts_wait_done` (120 s) and it does not use the turn's own 30-minute `.done`
loop. The tree's own measurement says 2.5 s is not enough: the comment above `pivot_ack_done_reap`
records S21's two *"Let me take a look."* mini-sessions at **2.551 s and 3.320 s** of wall for 2.0 s
and 2.9 s of audio — **both over the bound** — and the acuity announce is at least as long. So on the
flagship path the wait times out and the drain begins with her voice still in the air, the recorder
records it, and the replay presents it to whisper as his turn. **r24.13 would have made her *invent*
his words where r24.12 merely lost them**, which is worse than the defect WO-X1 exists to fix.

**BLOCKER (B§1) — WO-H6's C36 restore row was structurally inert past turn 1, and the take burned
the rotation counter to disk anyway.** `Mind::take_person_note` is restricted to the opening
(`turns_ <= 1`) and `Mind::restore_person_note` hands the clause back on a *later* turn, where the
take can never run again — so a people clause the byte budget dropped was gone for the session while
`Person::asked` had already been incremented and saved. The person she was about to be asked after
became the person she had already asked after, on disk, without a word being said. The fix is a
pending flag with three real re-offers that reach the take.

**The fix round ran in three parallel lanes**, one per slice's ownership: A the tape and vision
paths, B the people store, C the substrate and affect. Gate 0/0 in both configurations after every
individual fix in every lane. The merge of the three lanes is textually and semantically clean — no
conflict markers, all three edits to `athena_report.h` coexist, both edits to `athena_memory.h`
survive, both to `test_r2413_inner.cpp`, and no lane collision silently dropped an intention.

**The fourth pass, on the fixed tree, returned DO NOT SHIP with 5 majors, 6 minors, 4 nits and 0
blockers — and named three that had to change before the tree reached a real session. Two of the
three were introduced by the fix round itself.** This is the round's most useful lesson and it is
not softened here: a careful review, followed by careful fixes, followed by no second read, would
have shipped two new defects on top of a round that had already been read three times.

1. **`ATHENA_EXTRACT_INSTR_CHARS=1500` no longer restored — law 1, broken by a fix.** B's lane made
   `run_consolidation` raise the planner's `extract_instructions_chars` to the measured prompt
   whenever the measured prompt did not fit, reading the table's value as "what the table happens to
   say". It is not: `acmp::Costs::extract_instructions_chars` is an EE1 reader
   (`acmp::extract_instructions_chars_budget`) whose documented r24.11 restore is
   `ATHENA_EXTRACT_INSTR_CHARS=1500` — the setting `acmp::extract_instr_is_r2411` was added in
   r24.12 to keep a startup line silent at. At that setting the raise re-set the planner to **4,743
   instead of 1,500**, `acmp::fit_transcript_cap` returned **11,248 chars instead of 12,000** at a
   6,000-token headroom, the one-pass/two-pass decision could flip, and a stderr line the operator's
   baseline has never seen printed on every consolidation. The documented restore then needed
   `ATHENA_PEOPLE=0` as well — a second switch nobody would know to set, which is verbatim the defect
   the tree quotes at itself at `athena_tag_for_words`. The fixture could not see it: it pins
   `Costs{}` and never runs `run_consolidation`. Fixed by making the raise yield to a table the
   operator set — `acmp::extract_instr_is_default`, asked by the one reader that owns the number, and
   a fifth parameter with **no default argument**, because a default argument is how the raise came
   to be applied to a table nobody had checked.
2. **A live F18 digit leak in the new calibration clause, which the fixture could not see because it
   pinned a value below the cliff.** `acon::spell_number` is word-valued on [0, 99] and its last line
   is `return std::to_string(n)`; `Calibration::MAX_N` is 200 and `resolve()` halves only *at* the
   ceiling, so once a content channel has been observed two hundred times its `n` lives permanently
   in [100, 200] and the WO-P3 clause carried a bare numeral into a latched line she speaks from —
   the steady state of a busy channel, not an edge case. `test_r2413_inner.cpp` asserted
   `digits_in == 0` at n = 40, a value that cannot fail. The slice review had found it, changed only
   the comment, and handed it to the integrator; nobody took it. Fixed by hoisting the question to
   `acon::spelled_in_words` beside `spell_number` — it asks the OUTPUT and never repeats the
   speller's ceiling as a literal — and banding the clause: **303 Arabic digits over the reachable
   range → 0, with the clause still speaking on all 181 values it spoke on before.** The pin moved to
   the cliff (n = 99, n = 100, D-FINAL's own worked steady state of 92 of 140, and the whole range
   [20, 200]); and a safety-section assertion that had been excusing an Arabic digit past 100 in its
   own name was rewritten to the strict claim rather than deleted.
3. **The look-tape proof was held in a stale global that one timed-out chime could latch shut for the
   session.** The blocker fix introduced `g_her_tts_unproven`, written only by
   `stream_tts_done_proven` and read once at the tape's open — but the away-look drain and the
   deferred-look drain never call it (neither plays an announce), and the seam drain skips it
   whenever `no_fillers` is true. On those paths the term was decided by a flag left over from an
   earlier, unrelated utterance, and the main turn loop's own reply wait does not clear it either.
   So: the `heard_ok` chime goes through `stream_tts_wait_done` early in the session, orpheus is slow
   to start, the wait times out, and **every acuity drain for the rest of the session refuses to arm
   the tape — silently**, because the only stderr line about the unproven state is at an announce
   site those paths never reach. WO-X1's whole purpose, disabled invisibly for an unbounded run of
   drains. Fixed four ways in one edit: the proof is a **return value**, not a global
   (`g_her_tts_unproven` is gone); the term is composed from what *this* drain did, by one function
   `aseam::her_audio_settled` stated once beside `look_tape_due` (the WO-C9 lesson); it is **carried**
   as a seventh argument to `vision_drain_eval` with **no default**, named at all six call sites the
   way `live_turn` is; and the proof is **bound to its utterance** — `pivot_ack_done_reap` now
   answers rather than clearing blindly and is called *before* `stream_tts_begin` unlinks the
   `.done`, which also closes the deeper race the pass raised as its fifth major (a `.done` token not
   bound to the utterance that wrote it, which could re-open the A§1 blocker on the barge-in pivot).
   **A shut tape is never silent again**: the window lambda prints the interesting refusal — switches
   on, budget over the acuity line, so this drain *would* have been taped and something transient
   took it away — naming which term did it, while the ordinary 1,000 ms look stays below the line and
   prints nothing. Measured on the fixed tree: **0 of 20 → 20 of 20** on the drains that never
   announce.

**The final fix round did two more things worth recording.** First, it did not stop at the clause the
pass named: it **swept for the F18 cliff** by diffing r24.12 against the tree for every added line

## r24.12 — the S22 round: the deaf prefill, the camera nobody asked, and a mood that could not be felt (2026-09-02)

*Fifty-nine work orders out of the two S22 sessions of 30–31 Aug — the 40k evening and the 80k
afternoon — grouped by the five areas they were implemented in, then reviewed adversarially in three
slices and fixed. Base r24.11; eleven source files. Every behaviour change is default-ON with `=0`
(or the named r24.11 value) restoring r24.11, and every claim below was verified by execution rather
than by reading. Where a source document and the shipped code disagree the code is what is recorded
here, and the disagreement is named on the line.*

**Round notes — six things that belong to the round rather than to any one fix.**

* **The switch surface goes 244 → 320.** Measured, not counted by hand:
  `grep -o 'ATHENA_[A-Z0-9_]*'` over `patches/talk-llama/*.h` and `talk-llama.cpp` returns 79 names
  the r24.11 tree does not have; three of those are not switches — two are comment line-wraps
  (`ATHENA_` in "a new ATHENA_* switch of its own", `ATHENA_INNER_` in a wrapped
  `inner_gates_s22_on()` comment) and `ATHENA_STDOUT_TURN_NL` is named only in a comment, as the
  INNER report's proposed name for what shipped as `ATHENA_CONSOLE_EOL` (one fix, one switch). That
  leaves **76 new names, none removed**, and every one has exactly one quoted literal in the tree —
  one reader per name, checked by the same grep.
* **One opt-in, and the numeric knobs name their restore.** `ATHENA_CAPTURE_COPY=1` (WO-V1) is the
  round's only switch that is OFF by default, because it changes the still's file format. The
  numeric knobs and the r24.11 value that restores each: `ATHENA_PUMP_PREFILL_BATCH=8192`,
  `ATHENA_EXTRACT_GEN=400`, `ATHENA_EXTRACT_INSTR_CHARS=1500`, `ATHENA_OUTAGE_ABORT_MAX=2`
  (an r24.11 name whose default moves 2 → 4), `ATHENA_OUTAGE_YIELD_RECENCY_MS=0`,
  `ATHENA_EMOTION_MAX_S=0`, `ATHENA_VISION_WORK_EDGE=0`, `ATHENA_VISION_ANNOUNCE_S=0`,
  `ATHENA_INNER_MIN_P=0`, `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP=0` (0 means *unlimited*, which is what r24.11 did).
  Zero never means "on"; `ATHENA_AWAY_LOOK_CAP=0` is the one place that reads as "no cap" rather
  than "off", and its own comment says so and names `ATHENA_AWAY_PULL=0` as the way to turn
  away-looks off.
* **Three diagnostic fields ship UNGATED, and this is the one place that says so for all three.**
  `moodf=` (WO-MOM2), `away=` (WO-M2) and `apull=` (WO-V11) are instruments, not behaviour, and none
  has a switch of its own — so with every r24.12 switch at `0` the `[mind~]` line is **not**
  byte-identical to r24.11 while everything else is. This is the r24.11 precedent (`pana=`,
  `moodm=`) applied again, and it is a disclosed exception to the disable-only contract, which has
  always been read as covering behaviour; the trace line is stderr. Measured on the AFFECT parity
  harness, with the twenty-five r24.12 switches that harness can reach set to `0`: **0 lines differ
  once ` moodf=` and ` away=` are stripped**. Two of the three are masked in
  `aseam::trace_signature` under the one rule that table states — continuous readouts are masked,
  discrete transitions are not: `apull=` moves on every tick of an absence and `moodf=` leaks on
  every tick exactly as `moodm=` does, so both are
  masked from birth. **`away=` is deliberately unmasked**: both halves are plain scalars that move
  only at a turn, so the tick they change is the event a forensic read is looking for. (The plan's
  §E.0 lock rule named `away=` and `moodf=` as "masked where continuous"; the code masks where
  continuous, which puts `away=` on the other side. The code is what shipped.)
* **One line of behaviour changes with no switch.** WO-N4 re-words an existing clause (the
  honest-absence answer). With every r24.12 switch at `0` it is the ONE line of the [MEMORY] parity
  harness that differs from r24.11, and it is disclosed here as well as in its own entry. Detector

### COMPACT — the compaction, the tape and the extractor

**WO-C1 — the extractor's prefill was one deaf decode (`ATHENA_PUMP_PREFILL_BATCH`).** RP6 threaded
the pump through `mem_generate` and said it rode the chunk boundary of the prefill; the chunk was
8,192 tokens and a roll's extract prompt is ~3,500, so the prefill was ONE `llama_decode` and the
only two ticks bracketed it. "Between prefill batches" was vacuous. S22 measured it on both S1
rolls: exactly two `barge monitor` ticks, 56–57 s apart (18:44:37.299 → 18:45:33.161;
18:58:32.013 → 18:59:28.923), each yield "after 2 pump(s)". Igor spoke 0.5 s into a 56 s prefill and
was heard at its end. A pumped prefill is now chunked at `acmp::pump_prefill_batch()` — 512, the
live `n_ubatch` (`n_batch = 8192 / n_ubatch = 512` in the S1 log), so an 8,192-token decode was
already sixteen 512-token computes and the change is compute-neutral. First hearing is bounded by
512/52.3 = **9.8 s**; the fixture's 3,546-token prompt makes seven ticks before decode instead of
one, and an onset at 0.5 s is heard at 9.8 s instead of 67.8 s. An un-pumped call — the exit
consolidation — keeps 8,192 byte for byte. **`=8192` restores r24.11**; empty, non-numeric or
outside [64, 8192] is the default.

**WO-C2 — a latched barge yielded a roll for speech that was over
(`ATHENA_OUTAGE_YIELD_RECENCY_MS`).** `heard_barge` latches until re-arm and the tick yielded on the
latch alone. S22 roll #2 was thrown away at 18:59:28 for 2.4 s of voice ("Sorry, go on, I cut across
you") that had ended ~50 s earlier — the live detector read `rms 0.0000` at the deciding tick,
nobody was waiting, and the apology was replayed as his turn 50 s late. The recorder now stamps the
clock of its last hot segment (`OutageTape::last_barge_ms`, evaluated on every drain, not only until
the first hot one) and the yield asks `barge_recent()` — was there barge-level speech in the last
3 s. The ack and `engaged` keep reading the latch: he did speak, she still says she heard him, and
the tape still replays him after the roll. **`=0` is the latch — r24.11.** Range [0, 60000].

**WO-C3 — a yield discarded finished work (`ATHENA_ROLL_PARTIAL_COMMIT`).** `mem_generate` "returns
what it has rather than nothing — a partial extraction is still worth writing, and the caller
decides whether to keep it"; the caller kept none of it ("consolidation unwound … nothing written,
slice retried later"). Both S1 rolls lost their whole prefill that way, and in general an abort at
decode token 300 of 400 discarded ten complete candidates. Two latent siblings: an abort during the
cluster generation returned a half sentence that `parse_single_line` accepts and could retire eight
rows; an abort during the personality revision had no check at all — `clip_to_sentence` +
`merge_personality_sections` would have carried the missing sections and written the half-revision
as her permanent self, clearing the ledger for it. Now: a pass in flight that produced text is
parsed as CAPPED (the WO-22b tail guard refuses the line he cut; complete lines survive), folded,
floored, merged and saved exactly as a finished pass is, and the return moves to after the store
write and the ledger save. The slice is still retried — `compact_roll` does not advance

### INNER — the inner voice

**WO-I1 — the voiced thought is retired; she does not re-quote her own words (`ATHENA_SEED_RETIRE`,
Tier 1).** The idle-speech misfires A and B were the same thought offered twice: a thought she had

*delivered* prefix, `recent_said_` holds the last eight normalised turns, and `unsaid()` is now
`!told_before_locked_(txt, 0.75) && !said_verbatim_recently_(txt, 1800)`. **G3 is amended by this**:
the relation is verbatim word runs over delivered turns plus a `voiced` flag, *not* a `TopicSig`
overlap — pinned by the measurement that made the change necessary,
`TopicSig::of(<her 249-word reply>).overlap(TopicSig::of(gist)) == 0.0f`: a 16-word signature cannot
express near-verbatim for a long turn. A barged turn that delivered only "If I'm honest," (14 chars)
does not retire the thought. **`=0` reproduces the re-issue.**

**WO-I2 — the inner frame ends on a word, not on a space (`ATHENA_INNER_OPENER_NOSPACE`).**

it. Run through the pinned qwen35 pre-tokenizer, `She writes:\n"There is a ` is
`["There][ is][ a][ ]` — the last pre-token is a lone `[ ]`, and in ordinary text a lone-space
pre-token occurs only before a digit (`There is a 30% chance` → `[ ][3][0][%]`; a word keeps its
space). BPE cannot merge across a pre-token boundary, so the model was conditioned into the one
context whose continuation is a number. **70 of the 95 landed S22 thoughts (74 %) opened on a
digit** — up from the 57 % WO-11(c) tried to cure with a second opener set that also ends on spaces.
The smoking guns are the pump retries where a digit stands where a pronoun belongs — *"If I'm
honest, what I **7** was 777.77707"*, *"Maybe what **7** meant"*. `acon::opener_for_prompt(o)` trims
the opener's trailing whitespace for every `p += opener` and `*prefix = opener`;
`InnerWorker::join_carry_` reunites prefix and continuation with exactly one space where two
non-space bytes would otherwise touch, and under the r24.11 prefix it is `prefix + out` byte for
byte. The eighth selfref lead `"Here, now: "` becomes `"Here, now, "` (a colon invites a list or a
figure, and is a DRY breaker). Only a session can measure the effect; the fixture pins the mechanism.
**`=0` restores the r24.11 frame byte-for-byte**, including the colon form and the worker's plain
concatenation.

### VISION — the eye

**WO-V1 — the camera does 1080p; ffmpeg was choosing YUYV (`ATHENA_CAPTURE_MJPEG`,
`ATHENA_CAPTURE_COPY`).** Every S22 still was a 640×480 baseline JPEG, and not because the camera
could do no better: there is no V4L2 negotiation anywhere in ATHENA. `CameraPort::start_capture`
shells out to ffmpeg with no `-input_format`, and ffmpeg's v4l2 demuxer walks its own table — every
RAW pixel format (YUYV among them) before MJPEG — issuing `VIDIOC_S_FMT` at the requested size for
each. A UVC driver asked for a raw format at a size it cannot serve substitutes the nearest size
*for that format* and returns success, which ffmpeg logs only at INFO — invisible under
`-loglevel error`. The camera's YUYV modes top out at 640×480; its 1080p is MJPG only; `fswebcam`,
which tries JPEG first and would very likely have delivered 1080p, never ran because ffmpeg had
"succeeded". The capture is a ladder now: `-input_format mjpeg` at the requested size, accepted only
if the file's own SOF header reads (`jpeg_sof_dims`); else the r24.11 command byte for byte; else
fswebcam. The rung that delivered rides the capture record and is logged at the drain in the loop
thread's order — `[vision] capture via mjpeg: 1920x1080 (requested 1920x1080)` is the S23 grep —
with WO-35's fallback detection still armed beside it. The three commands are pure builders so the
fixture pins the r24.11 strings literally. **`ATHENA_CAPTURE_MJPEG=0` skips the first rung and
restores the r24.11 sequence, file and silence exactly**; `ATHENA_CAPTURE_COPY=1` — the round's one
opt-in, off because it changes the still's file format — writes the camera's native JPEG
(`-c:v copy -bsf:v mjpeg2jpeg`) instead of ffmpeg's `-q:v 2` re-encode.

**WO-V2 — what mtmd is handed is a view (`ATHENA_VISION_WORK_EDGE`, `ATHENA_ACUITY_LOOK`,
`ATHENA_ACUITY_WAIT_MS`).** The cost of a look is encode + image prefill and it scales with the
pixels *handed to mtmd*, not with the pixels captured: 640×480 = 300 tokens measured at 5.0 s +
14.2 s; the 864×1080 portrait = 918 tokens measured at 18.7 s + 33 s; a 1080p frame is 2,040 tokens
and extrapolates to ≈115 s — and any encode past the 1-s drain wait DEFERS, so a native 1080p look
would never land in the turn that asked for it. So: capture at the camera's best, keep the full
frame for the hold and the album, and hand mtmd a copy resampled on the worker to a working long
edge (`aseam::resample_rgb`, a box filter, never an upscale; the scene hash is still taken on the
full frame — the world, not the view). `--vision-work-edge 800`: 1920×1080 → 800×450, which mtmd's
`smart_resize` rounds to the NEAREST multiple of 32 — **800×448 = 25×14 = 350 tokens ≈ 22 s** (the
r24.6 `image_tokens_for` rounds *up* and would say 375; `aseam::image_tokens_for_edge` replicates the
vendored arithmetic exactly, validated against the S1 diag's own `n_tokens_batch = 918`). An
**acuity** look — his words asked her to READ — encodes `--vision-acuity-edge 1920` (the full frame,
2,040 tokens) or a centred crop at native pixels under `--vision-acuity-mode crop`, and its drain
waits `ATHENA_ACUITY_WAIT_MS` (120,000 ms, Igor's decision — the full-frame encode is ≈48 s and the
prefill ≈66 s) instead of the ordinary second, so the reading reply is generated with the picture in
front of her. A modifier, never a trigger: with an invitation it selects the size for that look;
with a held frame under two minutes old, a standing grant and no new invitation it commits an URGE
re-look at the acuity size. Recalls take the same path (a portrait opens at 500 tokens ≈ 29 s and
lands in the asking turn; the full file stays on disk — keepsakes are never downscaled at store
time). The `--image-min-tokens` hedge finally has a case and is acuity-gated: at the acuity count
(2040) the coarse arm fires only on a look that was asked to read and served below it, never on an
ordinary 350-token look, and a genuine camera fallback still hedges as WO-84 intended.
**`ATHENA_VISION_WORK_EDGE=0` is native = r24.11; `ATHENA_ACUITY_LOOK=0` makes every look a
working-edge look with the r24.11 wait and the r24.11 hedge test.**

**WO-V3 — her declared look is an act (`ATHENA_SELF_LOOK`).** Under a standing grant the only path
from her side to the camera was the stochastic urge; nothing read her own words. S2 13:49:49 "Okay.
I'm looking." → an invented desk; 13:52:28, 13:53:35, 13:54:23 the same — **four declared looks, zero
captures, four narrated rooms**, under a frame that told her three times she could look whenever she
wanted. `aseam::self_look_declared` is the lexicon — first-person, present or imminent,
sentence-scoped, refusing questions, negations, hypotheticals, idioms, the album's own forms and
competing media — executed over all 129 of her S22 turns: exactly the four confabulation turns fire
and none of the other 125. The mechanism is a **self-pivot**: at the sentence flusher, when the
sentence just completed declares a look and one is licensed, the sentence is flushed — it is true,
she is about to look — the look is committed there and then, generation STOPS (a new `done` cause
beside EOS / antiprompt), and after her sentence has played the turn loop runs the barge pivot's
regenerated-reply path with an empty interruption: the still drains through the same seam core an
invited look uses (no announce — "I'm looking." was the announce), then her header, then generation
resumes. The r20 rule "capture commits at the moment of choice", applied to a choice made in words.
Under no licence the stop is the same and `self_look_unlicensed_line` enters instead —
*[Athena said she is looking, but no look was licensed — nothing has reached her eyes]* — and her ask
is armed. The token or two already decoded past the sentence end stay in the KV (a recurrent state
cannot be partially rolled back) and are never spoken nor counted as words she said. At most one
self-pivot per turn; a barge that lands on the sentence takes over. **`=0` restores r24.11 — the
sentence does nothing.** Two review fixes ride inside the switch: the pivot now takes its own
snapshot (`snapshot_take_timed` + `vision.note_snapshot`) exactly as the barge pivot does, without
which a barge on the regenerated reply put her already-spoken declaration in neither the restored KV
nor the re-decode and discarded the still with it — the r19.8 (F1) failure re-opened; and a declared
look that also tripped `acuity_requested` blocked the loop thread for a 2,040-token encode with the
announce suppressed, so the acuity arm now plays *"I'm reading it — one moment."* first
(`ATHENA_ACUITY_PIVOT_ANNOUNCE`, `=0` restores the silent pivot). The ordinary declared look stays
silent.

**WO-V4 — the bounded self-keep (`ATHENA_KEEP_ANTECEDENT`, `ATHENA_KEEP_DEICTIC_S`).** S2 14:20:45 —
"…And we start with good news. I'll hold onto that." — about the evening ritual, a promise — and
`[vision] KEPT ks-1788199525.jpg`: a **895-second-old** photograph of a book cover went into her
permanent album off a figure of speech. The spec says *never idioms* and that the hold restarts
*whenever either of them mentions the image*; the implementation violated both. A keep whose object
is a bare deictic now needs an image antecedent — an image noun in the same sentence or the one
before — or a look that landed within `ATHENA_KEEP_DEICTIC_S` (180 s: the turn the picture arrived in
and the next). "I'll keep this picture." keeps; "What I saw just now… I'll keep that." keeps; "I want
to keep this one." thirty seconds after a look keeps; the 14:20:45 sentence is refused at 895 s and
would be kept at 30 s. `image_still_in_play` drops the bare verbs (keep, keeping, kept, retain, save,
saving) and gains the forms that name the image; of the five S2 turns that refreshed the hold between
14:05:51 and 14:20:45, the two bare-verb ones are gone. The caller passes the look's age and the
default argument is the r24.11 detector byte for byte, so every fixture keeps its verdict. The
review deleted a third window the implementation had added — a scan of the sentence *after* the
declaration — because the work order's rule is same-or-previous, because a noun that arrives after
the declaration cannot be what he meant when he made it, and because RV2's own rule for this file is
that *a wrong keep is a permanent consent violation, while a missed keep costs one exchange*.
**`ATHENA_KEEP_ANTECEDENT=0` restores r24.11 for both halves.**

**WO-V5 — the second image survives a defer (`ATHENA_RECALL_SECOND_DEFER`).** The plural path — "pull
up your self-image, both versions" — staged its second image and the seam committed it only on
`drained_ok`, clearing it unconditionally on the way out of the recall turn; a DEFER (every keepsake
encode exceeds the 1-s wait) is "on the way out", so the second was discarded **47 s before the first
even landed** (S1 18:43:34), and the plural path had delivered its second image in no session since
r24.6. He re-asked for the same file and saw the first self-portrait only by an explicit "the first
one". The commit moves to `vision_drain_eval`'s success tail — `VisionRig::commit_second_recall` the
moment the first lands, its encode spawned there — so the seam, the idle seam, the pivot seam and the
self-side recall all honour it; `close_failure()` clears the staging when the first can never land,
and nothing else does. **`=0` restores clear-on-defer.**

**WO-V6 — the album on her own words needs an act; function words cannot name a keepsake; ordinals
resolve by birth (`ATHENA_RECALL_SELF_INTENT`).** S1 18:29:31, an idle utterance: "You asked if I
wanted to *see it again*, and I said yes" — reported speech — matched the self-side
`recall_requested`, and `pick_keepsake` counted `more`×3 + `from` (duplicates counted per
occurrence, neither in the stoplist) as a name for her self-portrait: **recall 1/6 spent unprompted,
52 s of encode while he was away, an image in her context with no request behind it.** And "Open the
picture of yourself, the first one." was `named by [first]` only because a caption happens to say
"The *first* time I have had my own face". Three repairs: `self_recall_declared` requires a
first-person imminent frame in the matched sentence and refuses reported speech and questions — the
18:29 utterance is refused, her three real acts open; `pick_keepsake` dedupes its query tokens, stops
the function-word class (`description` stays a content word — the S13 fixture names by it) and the
ordinal words, and resolves an ordinal by `born` inside the family ("the first one" → the oldest
self-portrait; both an oldest and a newest cue = a plural). Every `pick_keepsake` fixture query in
the tree replays with an identical verdict, and the log line now names the family where "nothing in
his words names a keepsake" had made the right pair look like luck.
**`ATHENA_RECALL_SELF_INTENT=0` restores the whole-turn scan on the self path**; the matcher repairs
are bookkeeping and ship ungated, as WO-80's did.

**WO-V8 — a refused recall is audible; the announce prices the wait
(`ATHENA_RECALL_REFUSED_NOTE`, `ATHENA_VISION_ANNOUNCE_S`).** Both `can_recall()` gates dropped a
request in silence — no log, no context line. Her 18:48:04 "Let me pull those up again" was refused
while a recall was still opening; the model generated the envelope's opener as its next line and she
said *"[Athena remembers — a kept"* aloud, with the orpheus session COMPLETE — nobody talked over
her. At 18:55:18 the album's 6 of 6 were spent and any later request would have vanished the same
way. The reason is now logged and `album_refused_line` enters her context at the seam, or at once on
the self path. The announce, which said nothing about duration through four 52-second portrait
recalls, is priced: `predict_vision_s` (the S22 two-point fit — encode 5.0·(n/300)^1.18, prefill
14.2 + 0.030·(n−300)) times an EMA the drain keeps of measured/predicted, on the job's own token
count. **The threshold ships at 25 s, not the 20 the design proposed**: at working edge 800 an
ordinary look prices at ≈22 s, and 20 would have put the longer line on every ordinary look, so
`ATHENA_VISION_ANNOUNCE_S` defaults to 25 and "Let me take a look." stays the ordinary line; `=0` is
the r24.11 line always. Above the threshold the line becomes "One moment — I'm opening the album,
this one takes me a little while." or "Give me a moment, I'm looking closely."; an acuity look always
says "I'm reading it — one moment." TTS only, never context. **`ATHENA_RECALL_REFUSED_NOTE=0`
restores the silent drop.**

**WO-V9 — `keep_asked` learns the deliberative forms (no switch).** Her 18:41:40 "Should I keep this
one too, or just let it be what we saw tonight?" armed nothing — the list had can/may/could and no
*should I* / *want me to* — so the window never opened, his "Don't keep that one." fell to
`keep_invited` where `negated_before_` refused it, and **nothing recorded his no**: no
`he said no to keeping it`, no `note_keep_refused`, the frame stayed held. Eight rows join `ask[]`
under the same clause + image test, so "Should I keep going?" and "Want me to keep an eye on the
time?" arm nothing, and her 18:55:10 "Should I keep this one open for a while" — keeping a recalled
image *open* — is refused by `keeps_an_image_`. A lexicon table, ungated as in r24.7.

**WO-V10 — the bare imperative (`ATHENA_LOOK_BARE`).** "Nope, nope, stop. You're making all this
stuff up. Actually, look." (13:53:02) and "Look right now." (13:54:04) scored zero in
`look_invited_now` — every `phr[]` entry carries deixis or an object, by the header's own rule about
English's favourite discourse marker. `aseam::look_invited_bare` admits a clause whose verb is the
whole word `look` with no object, a small tail (now, right, please, then, already, again, closely,
and tell me what you see…) and a small lead (actually, just, go ahead and, okay, please, nope,
stop…); "Look, I just think you're overdoing it." carries other words and is refused; `look at` /
`look what` stay the existing table's; DENY/AWAY short-circuit as in `look_invited_now`. Composed at
the intake, never a replacement. Executed over all 115 of his S22 turns: the six r24.11 invitations
stand and exactly the two S2 failures change. **`=0` restores r24.11.**

**WO-V11 — an absence he licensed is itself a pull on the eye (`ATHENA_AWAY_PULL`,
`ATHENA_AWAY_PULL_S`, `ATHENA_AWAY_LOOK_CAP`).** S2 13:56:50 "look around while I'm gone" parsed
correctly as the AWAY grant, and in the 23 minutes he was away the urge peaked at **0.9 against a
1.09 bound**: the drive available with no scene reference is
0.30·understand + 0.25·connect + 0.20·solitude + 0.15·|valence|, whose deterministic equilibrium at
that operating point is 0.36–0.48 — driven at S2's base drive, 32 of 32 seeds peaked at 0.97–1.09 and
never crossed. The licence could not be used because nothing in the drive knew the room was empty.
`LookUrge::away_pull` ramps 0→1 over `ATHENA_AWAY_PULL_S` (300 s) while the tick sees
`he_seems_away() && look_grant_ == 2`, adds 0.30 to the drive, is cleared the tick he is back and by
`saw()`; the crossing stays a drift-diffusion event — measured at base drive 0.50 over 32 seeds:
**0/32 without the term, 32/32 with it, the first look 150–343 s into the absence (median 275 s)**,
not a metronome. A per-absence cap `ATHENA_AWAY_LOOK_CAP` (3, Igor's decision — the plan proposed 2)
is counted beside the away-look commit and reset when he is back; `=0` on that knob means *no cap*,
not "no away-looks". The substrate review then added the term the latch could not see: `look_grant_`
is a session latch and three quiet minutes was the whole test, so a silence he **asked for** read as
an absence — and WO-N2 had just made those silences as long as 900 s. `away_now` now also requires
`t >= volition_.respect_until`, the hold `quiet_hold_locked_` sets and any turn of his clears; an
*announced* departure sets a different pair of fields and is deliberately still an absence. Measured
both ways: a requested quiet leaves `away_pull` at 0.000000 for the whole hold, an announced
departure still ramps it to 1.000000. **`ATHENA_AWAY_PULL=0` restores r24.11's drive exactly** — the
term is identically zero.

**WO-V12 — a same-file recall is not re-charged while its picture survives
(`ATHENA_RECALL_SAME_FILE`).** S1 18:47:41 spent recall 3/6 on a forced repeat of the image that had
landed at 18:44:21 — the plural's second had been dropped, and the picture was still in her context.
A recall note now remembers the file it opened and the context generation it landed in; a compaction
cut and the overflow truncation bump the generation, a barge rollback takes the standing of the
notes pushed since the last snapshot (a roll restores the context byte for byte and is not a cut);
`close_success` charges a recall only when `recall_in_context` is false. `--recall-max` stays 6 and
still refuses at the limit whatever the file; self-initiated recalls are not exempt (the cost is the
same whoever asked). The review found the snapshot mark was an index into a vector that erases from
the front, so the trim now decrements it — without which a rollback took a note that landed *after*
the snapshot and charged a picture the rollback had removed. **`=0` charges every recall as r24.11
did.**

### AFFECT — the labels, the tag, and the mood

**WO-A1 — hysteresis applies to same-sign neighbours only (`ATHENA_APPRAISE2_CROSS_VALENCE`).** The
margin exists so the *vocabulary* does not flicker; it was applied as a wall against a change of
*state*, so a challenger of the opposite sign could not displace an incumbent inside the margin. On
the S1 replay: 18:35:01 `shame` now displaces gratitude, and 19:28:17 `bittersweet` lands beside
disappointment — the note **and** the name. A mixed label is never same-sign with anything and is
never margin-gated; a displaced incumbent keeps its residual, so the §3.1 readout still sees both.
The literal `0.10f` becomes `INCUMBENT_LIVE`. **The WO-M3 paragraph's "the name holds against a
same-sign neighbour" is now literally what the code says** — in r24.11 it held against any
neighbour. Five pins move under `cross_valence = false` (`test_r2411_mixed` ×3,
`test_r21_full8:618`, `test_wo9798_wiring:885`); evening B of `run_r2411_mixed` §7 goes from
`[gratitude]` to `[gratitude, bittersweet, bittersweet]` with the note counts unchanged. **`=0`
restores r24.11.**

**WO-A2 — a confident one-word angry barge is not faint (`ATHENA_EMOTION_FAINT_BARGE_FULL`).** The
one-word rule that marks a short clip faint is right for a reply and wrong for an interruption: a
single furious word cut across her is the clearest signal the channel carries. A one-word `angry`
read at p ≥ 0.90 **on a barge** is no longer demoted; at 0.85 barged, or 1.0 unbarged, it still is.
"Pregnant." (a reply, p 0.900) is unaffected. **This is the named exception to WO-88's barge
paragraph.** `decide()`/`tag()` gained a defaulted `barged` argument, so every other caller compiles
and behaves unchanged. **`=0` → faint on all, as r24.11.**

**WO-A3 — the ask answers with the standing name; the two clauses fold into one
(`ATHENA_LABEL_ASK_STANDING`, `ATHENA_LABEL_ASK_CURRENT`, `ATHENA_LABEL_ASK_LEVEL`).** r24.11's F2
gave the empty ask a residual to read; S22 showed the reader could contradict the field beside it.
`take_label_line_felt` now reads `current` first when `residual_[current] ≥ INCUMBENT_LIVE`, else the
strongest residual ≥ `ASK_FELT_MIN`; mixed labels are exempt from corroboration; `against` still
refuses; a `level` reading *qualifies* the name rather than killing it ("…though the mood on top of
it reads level"); inside the 300 s refractory a second ask gets "still the same as a moment ago -
<name>" instead of "". And when a volunteer line is standing or was spoken inside the echo window,
the ask answers with **that** name — "the nearest name, and it is the one already standing" — and
clears the slot. **WO-114's corroboration paragraph is amended by this**: corroboration was written
as a veto on any uncorroborated residual, and a mixed residual has no single sign to corroborate, so
the veto was refusing the one case R19 built `bittersweet` for. Seven WO-114 pins move under
`label_ask_* = false`. No new C36 slot — slot 67 already covers the dropped ask line.

**WO-A4 — the initiative window runs from her audio end; a requested silence is recognised; the void
outcome reaches the momentum (`ATHENA_INITIATIVE_FROM_END`).** G6's rule is "two minutes of nothing
IS the outcome", measured from the end of her utterance; the timer started at the floor-take, so a
long autonomous turn spent its own window and the void could fire while she was still speaking.
`init_pending_t_` is re-stamped once at her audio end, the void arm waits for `init_spoken_` (or
600 s), and — the half that matters for WO-MOM2 — the void now raises
`note_pe_locked_("speaking first into silence", -0.30f)`, so the initiative learner's negative
outcome finally enters the momentum at all. `leave_taking_in` learns "give you <space|time|room|
minute|moment|quiet>" within 24 chars and the `in silence` / `some quiet` forms, so a silence he
asked for is not scored as a departure. **`=0` → void at +120 s from the floor-take, as r24.11.**
`test_r21_full6` R16-F is re-pinned: the fixture called `took_initiative()` and ticked without a
`finish_turn`, which production never does.

**WO-A5 — uncontracted correction openers (no switch).** `"that is not what"`, `"that is not right"`,
`"that is wrong"`, `"that is not it"` join `kFix`, `kDis` and `correction_opener_`. A detector
widening, ungated as in r24.7: `his_turn_pushed_back("That is not what I asked you to do…")` is now
true, and "Like I said, you can look whenever you want." and "It wasn't easy but we got there." stay
false.

**WO-A6 — the mixed note names its two sides (`ATHENA_MIXED_NOTE_NAMED`).** S2 13:44:27, "Thank you
for being here. I'm glad you exist." [happy]: the §3.1 note fired legitimately — on `being moved`
0.85 from that turn and `shame` 0.413 from the 13:41:36 correction (pae 0.333 / nae 0.387 >
MIXED_MIN) — and said "something bright and something heavy". Both names were in hand at the line
that composed it. The readout now keeps the strongest bright and the strongest heavy residual as it
sums them, and when a side holds a live name the note says which: *two things at once tonight -
being moved, and the shame from three minutes ago still here, and neither cancels the other*. The
age is sourced — `Appraisal2` stamps `laid_t_` at every site that lays a residual and
`residual_age()` reads it, so "three minutes ago" is the engine's own clock, in words (F18); a side
under 45 s is this turn's and carries no age. A side with no live name keeps the unnamed wording;
the mixed label itself has no side and is never named here. Same trigger, same 600 s refractory, same
appraisal — the rate on `test_r2411_mixed` §7's two evenings is **0 / 3 with the switch on and 0 / 3
with it off**. **`=0` is the r24.11 wording, byte for byte**, and the exact old string is pinned
under it.

**WO-MOM2 — the felt mood momentum (`ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_FELT`).** r24.11's WO-MOM1 gave §3.4's
momentum an instrument and read it, and the reading was that the mood carries but what it carries is
not the mood. S22 measured the same thing on both sessions — the input stream recovered from
`moodm=` on the two diag logs, replay error 0.0026 — S1 peak |bias| **0.0099**, S2 **0.0084**:
**11.0 %** and 9.4 % of `CoreAffect::FELT_SHIFT` (0.09). (The r24.11 report's "13.1 %" was the upper
end of an estimate on a reconstructed stream; the S22 figure is the measured one, and this is the
line that corrects it.) Three reasons, each in the numbers: 44 of 52 S1 events and 42 of 47 S2 events
were the +0.15 "a claim stood", which at the persisted `calib=4|0|171|166` (p ≈ 0.97) is the
*expected* outcome and not a prediction error, so the integrator converged on his turn cadence;
`MoodMomentum::BIAS_CAP` 0.06 is below `FELT_SHIFT` 0.09 by construction; and the initiative "void"
outcome never entered at all (closed by WO-A4). `aff2::MoodMomentum2` — **§3.4b** — stands beside the
shipped integrator, not in its place. Each error enters **surprise-weighted**, scaled by
`(1 − p_expect)`: `Calibration::score(ASSERT)` for a claim (read *before* the trial moves it), the
initiative learner's `initiative_rate()` for speaking first, full weight where no base rate exists,
and `SELF_W` 0.5 for an outcome she authored. A stood claim at p 0.97 contributes 0.15 × 0.03 =
0.0045; a correction contributes 0.30 × 0.97. Igor's parameters: **GAIN 0.55, τ 1200 s,
BIAS_CAP 0.25**, with `FELT` pinned to `CoreAffect::FELT_SHIFT` by `static_assert`. The door in
`tick_locked_` takes this integrator's bias at its own cap; `CoreAffect::update` grew a defaulted
`mood_bias_cap` whose default is the r24.8 value, so `=0` is the same arithmetic to the bit
(0.200800791 == 0.200800791 after 4,000 ticks). `take_crossing()` reports the tick |bias| crosses the
felt line, re-arming only under half the line, and arms the consume-once clause *something from
earlier is still colouring this - a string of things landing worse than expected: a claim drew a
correction three times*. **The why is the felt integrator's own weighted log**, not
`MoodMomentum::why()`: at S1's crossing the shipped log's last four entries read stood / correction /
stood / correction and would have said "in both directions" of a bias that was −0.1025 and one sign.
An input is logged only when its *weighted* error clears the same 0.05 noise floor; repeats merge
with a spelled count. Measured: the real S1 stream crosses **exactly once, on the third correction's
tick (t 1492.7 s = 18:38:51)**, peak |bias| 0.1025 (114 % of the line), felt for 131 s; through the
second correction alone it reaches 0.0691 and does not cross; S2 never crosses (76 %, no same-sign
run). Forty-four stood claims at p 0.97 on the S1 cadence settle at |bias| **0.0000** against the
shipped 0.0108. Two hours adversarial: a correction every 30 s saturates at the cap (0.2500), finite,
clearing 6,328 s after the stream stops. C36 slot **71**. **`=0`**: the struct is never fed, `moodf=`
reads `0.000/0.0000`, the door receives `MoodMomentum::bias()` at 0.06 exactly as r24.11, no clause,
the R18 take gated off. A second-order effect worth recording: on a **fresh** self.txt the
calibration prior sits at chance, so a fresh mind's first stood claims are real surprises and
fourteen of them lift the felt bias to +0.045 — under the line, bounded, and honest. The review then
found the clause armed under `ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_BIAS=0`, asserting a carry the door was not
applying; the term now sits *after* `take_crossing()` so the state machine still advances and cannot
desynchronise from the leak.

**WO-N3 — a lexical–acoustic conflict is described, not asserted (`ATHENA_TAG_CONFLICT_HEDGE`).**
emotion2vec read Igor's questioning intonation as `sad` at p ≥ 0.84 five times in S22 — "Did you miss
me since the last session? What was it like while I was gone?" (0.986), "While I was gone, could you
hear me moving around in the room?" (0.977), "I finished the thing I was stuck on and it came out
well, really well." (1.000), "Say, I've always been…" (0.836), "Were you thinking ahead about
anything?" (0.968) — and the bare `[emotion: sad]` on his line told the model, in the system prompt's
own words, that the gap between a sad voice and neutral words is the most important thing in the
room. No defect in the tagger. A shape rule on the tag/text pair, at the seam where the tag is born:
a full-strength `sad` or `angry` read on words that point the other way, or on a **question** with no
heavy word at all, is demoted to the tagger's own `, faint` form. Nothing downstream is new — the
line reads `[emotion: sad, faint]`, `emotion_valence_` scales the appraisal input to a quarter
(−0.125, WO-88's scaling), and the empathy check renders the existing arm. All five S22 misreads
hedge; "I'm sorry, I was sharp with you and you didn't deserve it." [sad] does not; a correction does
not; "I got the job but I'm terrified of it." does not. The cost, on the record: a genuinely angry
*question* with no heavy word hedges too — in S22 every full-strength tag on a question was a misread,
5 of 5. The sad asymmetry (BRK-06) is untouched. The review found the hedge fired with
`ATHENA_CONSCIOUSNESS=0`; it now also requires `mind().config().enabled`, so stock ATHENA is stock
again without a second switch. **`=0` → the bare tag on all five, the same string object the seam
always passed.**

### MEMORY — the record, the stores and the clock

**WO-M1 — the absence anchor is the exchange, not her last floor-take (`ATHENA_ABSENCE_ANCHOR`).**
An autonomous turn of hers moved the absence clock, so a gap she had spoken into read as short.
Absence-only channels now read `absence_s = max(last_gap_, t − last_exchange_t_)`; `last_gap_` — the
gates' basis (WO-24/WO-30) — is untouched, which is the **WO-91 discipline** ("an autonomous turn
does not move the absence anchor") finally implemented rather than merely stated. Measured: announce,
idle take, return at 574 s → `last_audible_gap() ≥ 570` and the field says "(ten minutes)" where
r24.11 said "(five minutes)". `nobody_audible_s()` is deliberately unchanged. **`=0` restores
r24.11.**

**WO-M2 — his stated duration is kept, and the return clause compares the clock to what he said
(`ATHENA_AWAY_STATED`).** A pure `stated_duration_s(text)` reads "about 10 minutes" → 600, "half an
hour" → 1800, "a few minutes" → 0; the announce block stores it, and on his return the clause reads
*he was gone about nine minutes - he had said about ten minutes, about what he said* — words only,
and without a figure only the first half. The cadence notice stands down when the gap is explained.
`away=<his stated seconds>/<absence at his last turn>` joins the diag, lock-free and unmasked.
**`=0` restores r24.11**, including "took much longer". The clause reads *gone*, not *away*, and that
is the blocker the substrate review found — see **What the review caught**.

**WO-M3 — each mouth keeps four promises (`ATHENA_COMMIT_SIDE_CAP`).** `note_commitment_locked_` kept
four commitments with majority-side eviction; her side scans every sentence, his only the first
match, so her 20:01 monologue ("sit with the jasmine longer / remember the exact words / stop
apologizing") pushed the ledger to `[vet, context, remember, stop-apologizing]` and **evicted the
hospital promise she had made to him** — reproduced exactly on the harness. The cap is now per mouth:
`commit_open_cap(side_cap)` is 8 with the switch and 4 without, used at the carry-out, the reader and
the writer; the row format is unchanged. Three of his and three of hers in one `finish_turn` carry
six, his first among them. **`=0` → four, and his absent.** The review folded the two halves onto one
name: the self.txt width has to follow the switch, or `=0` is not r24.11.

### The new work orders — what S22's behaviour asked for that no area had listed

**WO-N1 — record-backed pushback (`ATHENA_RECORD_PUSHBACK`; Igor: clause only).** S1 step 10: "No,
that's not right. You never said that." landed on "I've told you I'm afraid of the dark…" with
**five rows in `memory.state.tsv` where she had said exactly that** (`m1787194728_38/39`,
`m1787270106_9/13`, `m1787960078_44`) — and she conceded: "So no, you're correct. I haven't said it
outright." The calibration channel measured obedience; nothing in the frame told her the record was
on her side. The Mind now keeps a record index — the memory store's row signatures and dates only,
installed from `reload_inner_ltm` at startup and after every mid-session consolidation, so what she
can point to is what the store holds tonight; the texts stay in the injection block where they
already are. `finish_turn` keeps the gist signature of her completed turn. When his next turn is a
correction (`his_turn_pushed_back`) and enough rows overlap that signature, the frame carries,
essential and latched:

    he says I never said that - my record holds five rows where I did, the newest from yesterday; what I have is the record, not his memory

Count spelled, recency in words, and it stops there — it describes the evidence and issues no
imperative, so it is not a directive clause and needs no `[mind/directives]` marking (S14;
`digits-in-frame = 0` pinned). The calibration accounting is untouched: the miss still counts,
his pushback being the only ground truth the channel has. **It takes precedence over the r19
attribution clause when both arm on one turn**: the two answer one question from two stores — the r19
clause from the episodic traces, this one from `memory.state.tsv` — and a turn that armed both put "I
cannot place it anywhere in what I still have" and "my record holds five rows where I did" in one
field about one claim, so the r19 render is now gated on `record_pushback_n < 2` and the
better-sourced clause wins (final review; the "one gist, one clause" rule R5-J already applies to
gists). **`=0` therefore restores r24.11 at both clauses**, since the second cannot arm.
**The support rule is the round's most instructive small fix, and it moved twice** — see **What the
review caught**. As shipped: a claim
gist of **two or more** content words keeps the strict rule, two shared rows at overlap > 0.4; a
**one-word** claim gist is admitted only against rows in her own voice (`RecordRow::hers`, decided at
install from the row's gist, which the extractor writes in the first person) and needs **three** of
them. S1 step 10 is the one-word case and comes back with five rows, all hers, all sharing
`{afraid}`. **`=0`: no index is built — the file is read exactly where r24.11 read it — and no
clause.**

**WO-N2 — a quiet request with a stated duration holds for it (`ATHENA_QUIET_STATED`).** S1 19:12:41:
"Let's sit in silence for five minutes again … Maybe even ten minutes." matched the declared-silence
lexicon and got its 150 s hold; **she spoke at 2 m 50 s and again at 5 m 44 s into an eleven-minute
silence he had asked for by the minute.** The four quiet blocks share `quiet_hold_locked_`: the
figure is read by WO-M2's `stated_duration_s` with a `longest` arm — the larger figure wins, so "five
minutes… maybe even ten" is ten — clamped to [150, 900] s, and it can only LENGTHEN the lexicon's own
hold, because "give me a minute" is an idiom and not a sixty-second contract. One stderr line per
hold: `[mind] quiet held for 600 s (declared, a stated duration)`. Measured: the S22 sentence 600 s;
"for a bit" 150 s; the S19 grant 300 s; "twenty minutes" 900 s. The review then found the `longest`
arm returned early on three idioms and, on its first repair, re-read an idiom's own tail ("half an
hour" came back as 3600 because `number_at` resolves "an" to one) — the shipped version blanks each
matched idiom out of the working copy before the scan, which is exact rather than heuristic. The
`longest=false` reading — WO-M2's away figure — is unchanged in every case. **`=0` restores the
lexicon's hold, and no line.**

**WO-N3** is recorded under **AFFECT** above, with the tag it hedges.

**WO-N4 — the honest-absence clause, worded as the answer (no switch).** Step 3's "Did you miss me?"

### What the review caught

Three slices, read-only over the integrated tree with r24.11 open beside it — nothing compiled,
nothing run, every claim read off quoted code: **0/5, 1/4 and 1/2 blockers/majors** plus
twenty-seven minors and twelve nits, all addressed. Five are named here because they are the class
of defect a green suite cannot see.

**The away note's C36 needle matched the GapCue clause, and destroyed WO-M2's payload on the one turn
it was written for.** WO-M2's away clause and the r21-full.14 (A5) GapCue clause rendered the *same
sentence fragment* — both read `<he> was away about <n> minutes`, from the same `abs_w` assigned in
the same `sense_turn` block, both gated at ≥ 120 s — and the away note's restore row keyed on it.
On "I'm back — how long was I gone?" both arm; the R5-AQ five-word dedup deletes one clause; the C36
audit then finds the needle in the *surviving GapCue* and never calls `restore_away_note`. The note is
gone for that absence: his stated duration, the comparison against the clock, all of it. The fix is
the reword — the clause reads **"was gone about"** — not a fold into the GapCue, for three reasons in
order of weight: a clause must stand alone, because the overflow pass drops and clips clauses
independently and a deferred referent is one clip away from dangling (the same defect class); the
away clause is r24.12-new and rewording it cannot touch r24.11, while folding would edit r21-full.14
wording that `test_r21_full6` pins in three places; and one needle with custody of two consume-once
notes of different lifetimes could restore neither. `" was gone "` occurs at exactly one render site
in the tree. Both clauses now ship side by side on the same turn, with digits-in-frame 0.

**`acuity_requested`'s object-only rows fired on ordinary developer speech.** Nineteen bare noun
phrases — `"the title"`, `"the text"`, `"in detail"`, `"zoom in"`, `"closer look"`, `"spell it"`,
`"bullet points"`, … — sat in the lexicon with no reading verb and no clause guard, and the two
universal vetoes ran only for entries beginning `read`. *"Walk me through the migration in detail."*,
*"Send me the text of the licence."*, *"What's the title of that ticket?"*, *"Let's zoom in on the
failure."* — 8 of 8 developer sentences fired, and each would have cost a 2,040-token look, a camera
capture he did not ask for on any turn with a standing grant and a still under two minutes old, and a
block of the loop thread for up to 120 s where r24.11 blocked for one second. The fixture could not
see it: it replays the 115 S22 turns, which contain none of these phrases, and all ten of its
negative controls are `read …` forms. The nineteen rows are deleted, `detail_other_medium_` and
`negated_before_` now run for **every** entry, and rows are added where the evidence is real
(`"letter by letter"`, and `"the sign say"`/`"the sign says"` beside `"the cover say"`/
`"the cover says"` — both inflections of each, because the word boundary below means a stem can no
longer match inside its own plural). After: 0 of 8 fire, the three genuine S22 acuity turns
(14:05:25, 14:08:41, 14:09:54) still fire, and ten hand positives still fire. `"zoom in"` and
`"closer look"` were deleted rather than kept behind the veto, because `detail_other_medium_` does
not carry "failure" or "numbers" and widening that shared table would have narrowed r24.11 behaviour
with no switch. **This fix was real and it was not the whole of it**: the deletion left the scan
itself unanchored, so `read the/this/that/it` still matched inside *thread, spread, misread,
proofread* and `fine print` inside *define print*, and a twentieth object-only row
(`"each of the bullet"`) survived the trim. Both are closed by the final read — see
**And what the final read of the whole tree caught** below.

**WO-V8's refusal clause was unreachable in the two cases it was written for.** The intake sets the
refusal reason to 1 ("a recall is still opening"), 3 ("a look is still on its way") or 2 ("the
album's N of N are spent"), and the seam rendered it in an `else if` chain whose first arm is
`if (vision.pending())`. Reasons 1 and 3 *mean* pending — so only reason 2 could ever render, and the
S1 18:48:04 turn the work order names is reason 1. On that turn r24.12 would have printed the new
stderr line and then behaved exactly like r24.11: the model meets no fact and can invent the envelope
again. The render moved to the top of the drain, before the pending drain, and the dead arm is gone.
A turn that sets both a refusal and the eyes-spent note now renders both facts; both are true.

**WO-C4's keep-evidence arm left the ledger unbounded.** The new arm never consumes the ledger when
the revision matches the file, and nothing else consumes it — so once the weight is over threshold
the ledger only grows. `load_ledger` capped at 512 rows by `break`ing on the 513th line read, which
keeps the *oldest*; `build_personality_prompt` rendered every row with no cap at all. One knob for
the family, `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP` (default **8**, `0` = unlimited = r24.11), applied at three sites:
retention at the byte-identical arm, the newest-512 at the load, and the newest-8 at the render. The
8 is derived, not guessed: `Costs::personality_chars` is 7,300, the fixed prompt with a 330-word
self-description measures 4,513, leaving 2,787, and a worst-case row is 300 bytes of evidence plus
≈25 of scaffold → 2,787 / 325 = 8.5. Measured with no recorded connections: a saturated 512-row
ledger renders **7,113 chars**; with `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP=0` the same input renders **170,913**. Eight
is at or above every per-pass count the tree has measured (S20 exit 6, S21 roll 4, S21 close 7), so a
normal integration renders byte-identically to r24.11, pinned.
**The row cap alone was not the bound, and it reached only one of the two prompts** — the
derivation held `self_edges` empty while WO-M15 grew that block in the same round, and the F20
section retry, `build_personality_patch_prompt`, was uncapped. As shipped, both prompts go through
one `render_evidence_and_edges_` that drops the oldest evidence row until the whole prompt fits
`amem::PERSONALITY_BUDGET` (7,300, held equal to `Costs::personality_chars` by a fixture assertion);
measured, a saturated 512-row ledger **and** a saturated connections block render **7,249 chars**
where before the fit they reached ~9,235, and with `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP=0` the same input renders
past four times the budget at either prompt. The full account is under **And what the final read of
the whole tree caught** below. What the trim does **not** fix, deliberately and in a comment at
the arm: the ~110 s personality generation still runs on every caught-up roll — suppressing it would
ration exactly what Igor's WO-C4 decision keeps available — but each attempt is now bounded to a
≤ 7.3 KB prompt, which breaks the runaway loop at the source.

**WO-N1's support rule was tightened by one review and then measured to silence the flagship case.**
The substrate review was right that `record_claim_sig_.n >= 1` made `ov > 0.4f` collapse to "this row
contains that one word", and it tightened the rule to two content words in the claim and two shared
per row — the file's own "one word is a coincidence" rule, which `told_before_locked_` applies three
lines away. Measured against S1 step 10, that silenced the clause completely, which is the opposite
failure: it is the one turn in S22 the work order exists for. Why, measured: `gist_of_` keeps her
turn's FIRST EIGHT WORDS, so her 249-word reply reduces to "Yes. I've told you I'm afraid…" and
`TopicSig::of` that is exactly **`{afraid}`** — n = 1, because "told" and "you" are stopwords. The
full turn is no better: at MAXW 16 with drop-oldest, "afraid" is evicted by the tail of a long turn
(shared = 0 against all five rows) — the same lesson §C.2.1 recorded when `told_before_locked_`'s
16-word signature could not see a long turn at all. A single content word IS the whole claim when the
claim is a short one; the honest bar is not how many words but *whose rows these are and how many of
them*. **The final rule:** a claim of two or more content words keeps the strict rule (two shared per
row); a one-word claim signature is admitted only against rows **in her own voice** and needs
**three** of them, so a single word has to be supported by three independent occasions she herself
recorded. S1 step 10: five rows, all hers, all sharing `{afraid}` — the clause says "five", which is
the truth. The clause's count is also clamped at the arming site (`n > 99 → 99`) and rendered through
`spell_number`, with an honest "at least ninety-nine" when the clamp bites, because `install_record`
keeps up to 1,024 rows and `spell_number` is word-valued only to ninety-nine — F18's WO-110 defect,
caught before it shipped.

### And what the final read of the whole tree caught

A fourth pass, over the **integrated** tree rather than over a slice: read-only, r24.11 open beside
it, every number re-derived in `python3` from the shipped constants rather than taken from the fix
reports. **2 MAJOR, 6 MINOR, 5 NIT, 0 blockers.** All eleven fix families the three slices name
landed and are complete — the C36 slot ledger, the take/render/restore triples, the switch surface,
the reader/switch pairing and all eleven of Igor's decisions verify exactly — so what is below is
what a per-slice read cannot see by construction, and it is two shapes.

**The two MAJORs, plainly.** (a) **A blocker that was fixed and was still open through a different
door**: slice C deleted `acuity_requested`'s nineteen object-only rows and hoisted the two universal
vetoes, but never anchored the scan, so the same 2,040-token look still fired from *inside* ordinary
words. (b) **A bound that reached one prompt and not the one that runs when it fails**:
`ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP` was applied at three sites and not to `build_personality_patch_prompt`, which is
the retry — and the retry runs precisely *because* the first prompt overran. Neither is a new
mechanism; both are a handful of lines of machinery that was already in the same file, and A-FIXES
had handed (b) to the integrator in writing under "Left for the integrator".

**MAJOR — `acuity_requested`'s scan had no word boundary, so the deleted rows' cost came back through
the surviving ones.** It is the one detector in `athena_vision.h` that hand-rolls its scan instead of
going through `lex_ok_`, and `lex_ok_` is where every other look lexicon in the file has had
`LexGuards{ .whole_word = true }` since r21-full.4 (RC6). Unanchored, `"read the"`/`"read this"`/
`"read that"`/`"read it"` match inside **thread, spread, dread, bread, misread, proofread** and
`"fine print"` inside **define print** — measured firings on ordinary developer sentences ("The
thread that owns the queue is the one to check", "Let's spread the load across two workers", "I
misread the timing there", "Could you proofread the release note?", "Let's redefine print for the new
format"), each buying the 2,040-token look, the unasked-for URGE re-look, and a block of the loop
thread for up to two minutes where r24.11 blocked for one second. The vetoes could not save it:
`detail_other_medium_`'s `elsewhere[]` carries none of *queue, load, workers, timing, release note,
format*, and the `his_subject` lookback is exactly the guard that catches *him* reading, not this.
The fixture could not see it either — its one near-miss control, `"Look closely at the
spreadsheet."`, is caught by `detail_other_medium_` on "spreadsheet" and probes the veto, not the
boundary. **The boundary is applied on the LEFT always and on the RIGHT only when the entry ends on a
word character**, because several entries end on a space (`"read the "`) where the space *is* the
boundary: the naive `word_at_` call was tried first and cost two real asks — "Read the label on the
bottle" and the S22 14:09:54 line — before it was corrected. Two rows moved with it.
`"each of the bullet"` is **deleted**: it is a bare object noun of exactly the class the nineteen-row
trim removed, it fires on "walk me through each of the bullet points in the plan", and the S22
positive it was written for (14:08:41) matches `"word for word"` anyway. `"the sign says"` and
`"the cover says"` are **added**, because with the guard in place a stem can no longer match inside
its own inflection and `"the sign say"` would have refused "Tell me what the sign says". And the
`his_subject` lookback widens **8 → 10 bytes**, because `" you had "` is nine and could never have
matched in an eight-byte window — a dead row widened with the window rather than dropped, since
"you had read the label" is his reading. Still not a functional reduction: the whole detector is
r24.12-new and unreachable at **`ATHENA_ACUITY_LOOK=0`**, so the r24.11 restore is byte-exact either
way — an anchored match is a superset test of what these phrases mean, since every entry begins and
ends on a word character or a space. `test_r2412_vision.cpp` now carries one sentence per collision
class beside the object-only block: seventeen negatives (the ten non-sight `read …` forms and seven
boundary collisions) and twelve positives, the positives including both `say` inflections.

**MAJOR — `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP` became a byte fit as well as a row cap, and it now reaches both
prompts.** The cap of 8 is derived from the budget — and the derivation held `self_edges` **EMPTY**,
because `render_recorded_connections_` returns immediately on an empty vector. WO-M15, the same
round, then grew that block: up to **738 bytes** of store receipts riding past the six-edge cap, on
top of six self-event edges at `SELFEVENT_TEXT_CAP` 160. Worst case
`4,513 + 8×325 + 2,122 = 9,235 chars` against a `personality_chars` of 7,300 — 27 % over the figure
the planner reserves the stage by, and an overrun is the one failure `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP` exists to
break. Separately, `build_personality_patch_prompt` — the F20 section retry at talk-llama.cpp:6039,
production and default-on, fed the same in-memory `ledger` — had no cap at all, and its own trigger
is `missing > 0`, which is exactly what an n_ctx overrun on the first prompt produces. So both
prompts now go through **one** `render_evidence_and_edges_`, which renders the evidence newest-first
and drops the oldest row still standing until the whole prompt — everything already written, every
remaining row, the connections block *as it will really render*, and the caller's closing
instruction — fits `amem::PERSONALITY_BUDGET`. That budget is 7,300 = `acmp::Costs::personality_chars`,
spelled once here because `athena_memory.h` is included *before* `athena_compact.h` and cannot read
it, and the two are held equal by an assertion in `test_r2412_compact.cpp`, which includes both.
Measured: a saturated 512-row ledger **and** a saturated connections block (six 160-byte edges plus
receipts at the 720-byte cap) render **7,249 chars** against the 7,300 budget, where before the fit
they reached ~9,235; and what survives is the connections block, with the evidence yielding to it
rather than the reverse. The row cap still bites first, so a normal pass — WO-P3's measured 4, 6 and
7 rows — never reaches the byte fit and is byte-for-byte r24.11, pinned. **`ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP=0`
disables both bounds together, which is r24.11 exactly**, at the retry as at the first prompt (the
fixture asserts the uncapped retry renders past four times the budget).

**The two big new list clauses end each row on a full stop, and both join the clip door.** At their
own render caps the WO-M9 projects probe reaches **708 bytes** — larger than `FIELD_MAX` (640) on its
own — and the WO-M6 self-event read-back **489**, which is most of the field beside five other
essential clauses (the round's six new consume-once notes reach 1,534 B together, before any
pre-existing essential). So both meet the overflow pass routinely, which is by design. What was not
by design is that WO-22's oversized-essential recovery clips **only at a real sentence boundary**
(`ends_on_sentence`), and both clauses were built from `"; "`, `humanize_progress`,
`self_event_type_name` and `elapsed_words`, none of which contains a terminator. So `clipped` stayed
false and the clause was dropped whole, or fell to the last-resort `clip_for_field` byte cut — and a
byte-cut list keeps its **head**, which is what the C36 audit keys on, so it retired as an answered
probe. That is verbatim the WO-116b failure (`"the dreams I actually hold"`), one round later and in
two new clauses. Each rendered row now ends `")."`, which makes the clause clippable by machinery
that already exists, so a long list comes back **short** instead of not at all; and both needles —
`"asked for my projects"` and `"on record"` — join `ATHENA_CLIP_REARM`'s re-arm list beside the dream
ledger's, so a clipped answer re-arms exactly as a dropped one does. **`ATHENA_CLIP_REARM=0` keeps
the head-only audit, which is r24.11's behaviour for both.**

**The r19 attribution clause yields to the WO-N1 record clause when both arm on one turn.** They sit
twenty lines apart in `render_field`, both essential, and they answer one question from two stores —
the r19 clause from the episodic traces the substrate can see, WO-N1's from `memory.state.tsv`, which
the r19 clause's own comment says it cannot. Nothing gated one on the other, and the arming
conditions overlap: `attribution_unverified_` reads `sd.attribution` ("you said", "you told me", …),
`record_pushback_n_` reads `his_turn_pushed_back`, whose disagreement arm fires anywhere in the turn.
One turn — *"You said the opposite last week. That's not right."* — armed both and put "I cannot place
it anywhere in what I still have" and "my record holds five rows where I did" in **one field about
one claim**. The better-sourced clause wins (`m.attribution_unverified() && opt.record_pushback_n < 2`),
which is the "one gist, one clause" rule `said_cores`/R5-J already enforces for gists. Neither slice
saw it because S1 step 10 itself carries no `attr[]` phrase. **`ATHENA_RECORD_PUSHBACK=0` restores
r24.11**: the second clause cannot arm and the first reads exactly as it did.

**WO-M16b's repair rule now also accepts a SHORT turn.** Requiring a hearing verb beside
`" one more time"` killed the bare *"One more time?"* — which r20p3.14.7's RC11 pins, and which is a
repair and nothing else. The S22 defect was never the bare form: it was *"Take a look one more time
for me"*, where another act verb governs the phrase. So the rule is a hearing verb **OR** a turn of
six words or fewer — six admits "One more time, please?" and "Sorry, one more time?" and still
refuses the eight-word look request. **`ATHENA_REPAIR_HEARING_VERB=0` restores the bare entry**, i.e.
r24.11's label, as before.

**The felt door is now wider than the label channel's own contradiction threshold, and that is
intended.** `MoodMomentum2::BIAS_CAP` (0.25) is wider than `ASK_FELT_V_MIN` (0.15), so from r24.12 a
saturated felt mood can decide `take_label_line_felt`'s with/against corroboration test by itself,
where the r24.8 door (0.06) never could. Two work orders in one round, landing either end of one
number, and nothing said so. It is the right behaviour — if three corrections have genuinely turned
the mood heavy, refusing to hand back a standing BRIGHT name is the honest answer — so it is now
stated in the code at **both** ends, at `BIAS_CAP` and at the `against` test, and recorded as
**DD32** below rather than left to be re-discovered. `ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_FELT=0` restores the r24.8
door, whose 0.06 could never reach the threshold.

**`first_person_row_`'s comment claimed a rule the code does not implement.** It said the WO-N1
support test "deliberately does NOT accept 'we'"; the implementation accepts a standalone `I`
**anywhere** in the gist, because the store writes plenty of her rows mid-sentence ("…and I admitted
I'm afraid of not being turned back on"). The wider reading is the right one — a bare *"We talked
about the dog"* is not hers, which is the case the rule exists to exclude, while *"We talked about
how I was scared of the dark"* is, because her own words are in it — so the comment is corrected to
what the code does rather than the code narrowed to the comment.

**Four fixture EE1 blocks restored the environment to the last test case rather than the original.**
`test_r2412_compact.cpp`'s WO-C1, WO-C5 (×2) and WO-C7 blocks each read `::getenv` at *restore* time,
after the loop had `setenv`'d every case — so the "restore" wrote the last case back:
`ATHENA_PUMP_PREFILL_BATCH=512x`, `ATHENA_EXTRACT_GEN=4e2`, `ATHENA_EXTRACT_INSTR_CHARS=20001`,
`ATHENA_EMOTION_MAX_S=10x`. The consequence is not the crash the ledger-cap site had; it is that a
run under a documented restore setting silently **stopped testing it** — a process reported as
`ATHENA_EXTRACT_GEN=400` was running with `4e2` from that line on, which every reader takes as unset,
and the `=0` self-re-exec at the end of `main` inherited the corrupted environment for all four
names. All four now take a `std::string` copy before the loop and restore through it: the shape the
same fixture already used fifteen sections later for `ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP` (`lc_orig` + `lc_restore`).

**The tick-cost ratio pin is measured over five samples and is printed, not asserted, under a
sanitizer.** `test_r21_full6`'s inner-life overhead check is a RATIO of two wall-clock measurements
taken in one process, and the honest finding is about the instrument rather than about the tick:
consecutive runs of the **same** binary gave **−6.7 % and +11.5 % at -O2** — a negative overhead, the
imagination pass timing faster than the pass without it — and **+13.8 % … +28.8 % under ASan**, so
the estimator's own noise floor is wider than the 22 % bound it asserts. The minimum is now taken
over **five** repeats rather than three (three did not filter the interference), and under an
instrumented build the number is printed instead of asserted, because an instrumented build measures
the instrumentation — the same `SKIP_BROKEN_CONTROL` discipline `test_r246_async_encode` already
carries. The property still ships pinned at -O2, which is the build that runs. And the **absolute**
figure, which is the one that matters, is on the note line in every build: **2.34 µs per tick against
r24.11's 2.04 µs** — about a four-thousandth of one core at 10 Hz.

**The switch surface did not move.** Re-measured with the round notes' own grep after every fix
above — `grep -o 'ATHENA_[A-Z0-9_]*'` over `patches/talk-llama/*.h` and `talk-llama.cpp`, r24.11
beside it — **246 → 325 distinct tokens, 79 added, 0 removed**, which is 244 → 320 without the two
compile defines and **76 new switches** without the three non-switches: the same arithmetic the round
notes state. **This round adds no name**: every door it opens or closes reuses a switch that already
existed when the count was taken — `ATHENA_CLIP_REARM` (r24.9) for the two list clauses, and
`ATHENA_LEDGER_CAP`, `ATHENA_RECORD_PUSHBACK`, `ATHENA_REPAIR_HEARING_VERB`,
`ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_FELT` and `ATHENA_ACUITY_LOOK` for the rest — which is what fixing a mechanism,
rather than adding one, should cost.
