### The decisions

**DD22 — DD18 withdrawn: the camera does 1080p in MJPG.** The S19/S20 fallback was ffmpeg's
raw-format preference, invisible at `-loglevel error`; capture returns to **1920×1080** and the
encode cost is bounded by the **working edge**, not the capture. DD18's premise — "the camera cannot
do 1080p" — is false, and Igor's `v4l2-ctl --set-fmt-video=…pixelformat=MJPG` works precisely because
it names MJPG. What DD18 got right stands: the fallback detection stays armed against any future
substitution, and fine detail costs real seconds. The arithmetic, from the mmproj's own parameters
(`patch_size 16, n_merge 2, image_max_pixels 4,194,304`; `smart_resize` rounds each side to a
multiple of 32 and downscales only above 4.19 Mpx, so a 1080p frame is **not** downscaled, and tokens
= (w/32)·(h/32)):

* the **working edge** 800 → 800×448 = 25 × 14 = **350 tokens ≈ 22 s** — what an ordinary look
  encodes;
* the **acuity** full frame 1920 → 1920×1088 = 60 × 34 = **2,040 tokens ≈ 115 s** — what a look asked
  to read encodes, waited for and announced;
* and the arithmetic is validated on the one non-640×480 image S22 actually encoded, the 864×1080
  self-portrait: 27 × 34 = **918 tokens**, which is `n_tokens_batch = 918` in the S1 diag itself.
  That point also corrects DD18's cost model: DD18 assumed 15.6 ms/token, the real 918-token point
  says **20 ms/token**.

The launcher line becomes `--camera-res 1920x1080 --vision-work-edge 800 --vision-acuity-edge 1920
--vision-acuity-mode scale --image-min-tokens 2040`; `--look-max 15 --recall-max 6` stay.
**DD11's checklist line becomes** `capture via mjpeg: 1920x1080` and `n_tokens_batch = 350` at the
working edge — `2040` only on an acuity look.

**DD23 — the acuity wait is 120 s, and the working edge is 800.** The plan offered 640 (220 tokens,
≈ 15 s) against 800, and a 60-s acuity budget against the full-frame cost. Igor took 800 and
120,000 ms: the full-frame encode is ≈ 48 s and its prefill ≈ 66 s, and a reading reply generated
without the picture in front of her is the failure the work order exists to end. The consequence is
recorded where it bites: at edge 800 an ordinary look prices at ≈ 22 s, so `ATHENA_VISION_ANNOUNCE_S`
ships at **25**, not the 20 the design proposed, and "Let me take a look." stays the ordinary line.

**DD24 — the away-look cap is 3 per absence and the pull horizon 300 s.** The plan proposed 2 and
600 s. At 300 s the measured first look is 150–343 s into an absence (median 275 s) over 32 seeds,
which is a drift-diffusion crossing rather than a metronome; three looks bound a 23-minute absence
without turning the licence into a patrol.

**DD25 — personality integration waits for the roll that catches up, and a byte-identical revision
does not consume the ledger.** Igor's rule is unchanged — the trigger is a compaction, or the close
of the session — and this chooses *which* compaction. 113 weight of S1 evidence was integrated into a
document byte-identical to the one on disk and then cleared; that cannot happen again, and the
evidence survives to the roll that has the session in front of it.

**DD26 — the tape-yield cap is 4.** After WO-C1, WO-C2 and WO-C3 a yield costs ≤ 10 s of prefill and
no finished candidate, and the livelock the cap of 2 was written against cannot occur — a yielded
roll *does* call `note_roll`, so `roll_min_gap_s` gates the next one. He wanted her four times in S1.

**DD27 — the two belts ship, switchable.** The DRY spacing guard (WO-I7) and F18 at directive scope
(WO-I8). The second withholds the verbatim quote of 12 of 13 C1 keepers when he has said no digits;
the thought itself, its journal line and the "turning it over" clause are untouched, and the trade is
measured in WO-I8's entry rather than assumed.

**DD28 — WO-MOM2 ships at GAIN 0.55 / τ 1200 s / cap 0.25.** The S1 replay crosses the felt line
exactly once, on the third correction; two corrections reach 0.0691 and do not cross. The engine does
not ship without its wiring — the composed tree's audit reported the built-but-never-wired class for
exactly this reason, and the round is the one that closes it.

**DD29 — WO-N1 is a clause, not a calibration change.** She says what her record holds; the miss
still counts, because his pushback is the only ground truth that channel has. Deferring the trial
until she concedes or he confirms is a follow-on, named and not taken here.

**DD30 — the data heals run once, with a backup, including the false keepsake and the numeral selfref
rows.** They are her files; the script copies the whole directory before it writes a byte, prints
every change, and is idempotent. `ks-1788199525.jpg` — the bug-book cover kept off "I'll hold onto
that" — is removed row and file together.

**DD31 — `--ctx-size` stays 80,000.** S2 never compacted at 80k in two hours, and the 40k window is
what exercised the tape. If the tape and roll fixes are to be re-tested in S23, one session at 40k is
needed and is named in the grep sheet rather than in the launcher.

**DD32 — a saturated felt mood may decide the label channel's corroboration test by itself.**
WO-MOM2 widened the additive valence door to `MoodMomentum2::BIAS_CAP` **0.25** (DD28); WO-A3's
`take_label_line_felt` takes its with/against test against core affect at `ASK_FELT_V_MIN` **0.15**,
and core affect is read *after* the door has added the momentum's bias. 0.25 > 0.15, so from r24.12 a
saturated felt momentum can push `valence_now` past the ±0.15 line on its own — a standing
positive-valence residual then reads `against` and the ask returns `""`, no name — where the r24.8
door (`MoodMomentum::BIAS_CAP` 0.06) could never reach that threshold. Two work orders in one round landed
either end of one number and neither said so; the final review found it and it is a decision, not a
defect, so it is recorded as one.

**It ships as it is, for the reason WO-MOM2 exists.** The felt integrator's whole claim is that a
mood which has genuinely turned should be able to change something — and the S1 replay reaches the
felt line exactly once, on the *third* correction of an evening, at 114 % of the line. If three
corrections have turned the mood that heavy, handing back a standing BRIGHT name because a
half-decayed residual still holds it is the dishonest answer, not the honest one; refusing the name
is the same "read the live fact, not the latch" rule the review applied to `away_now`. The cost is
named rather than hidden: on a heavy evening the ask can answer with silence where WO-A3 would have
answered with the standing name, and that is a real narrowing of the case WO-A3 was written for. It
is bounded three ways — the momentum is capped (0.25, finite, clearing 6,328 s after an adversarial
stream stops), a **mixed** label is exempt from corroboration entirely (WO-A3), and
`ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_FELT=0` restores the r24.8 door and with it every r24.11 verdict of this test.
The alternative — taking the with/against test against `affect_.valence − momentum2_.bias()`, the
unbiased reading — was considered and **not** taken: it would make the label channel the one consumer
in the tree that reads around the mood door, and the door is not noise, it is the mood. What was
missing was that nobody could see the coupling, so it is now stated in the code at both ends (at
`BIAS_CAP` and at the `against` test) and in `docs/CONSCIOUSNESS.md`'s felt-integrator section ("The
mood carried; what it carried was not the mood"), and it belongs on the S23 sheet: `the closest name
for what this is:` going quiet through a run of corrections, on a session where `moodf=` is
saturated, is this coupling and not a defect.

### Corrections to older text this round makes

* **F1(a)** (`:4337-4339`, "called every 16 decoded tokens … and between prefill batches. … the slice
  is simply retried"): a prefill batch is now 512 tokens for a pumped call — about 10 s — where it
  was 8,192, i.e. the whole prompt; "between prefill batches" was vacuous until then (WO-C1). And the
  slice is retried *with* the complete candidates already produced before he spoke, parsed as capped,
  merged and saved as a finished pass's would be (WO-C3).
* **`tl:7522-7524`** — the paragraph stating that an aborted roll "does not call `note_roll`". It
  does: `compact_roll` returns true on a yield and `compact_service` calls `note_roll` on it. The
  comment is corrected in place (WO-C9), and with it the stage-3 *"everything above this point has
  already been persisted"* comment (false, and its early return unreachable in r24.11 — WO-C3) and
  the tape-close *"bounded by `listen_ms(2000)` — at most the last 2 s"* sentence, which described
  the VAD loop's get and not the transcription's (WO-C8).
* **WO-22b** ("The 400-token cap no longer mints half a sentence as a permanent row"): the cap itself
  is 800 (`ATHENA_EXTRACT_GEN`), through one reader, and a pass that runs to it says so in the log
  (WO-C5).
* **r24.9 WO-P2** ("the trigger is a compaction, or the close of the session"): at the compaction
  that **reaches the present**. A backlog roll keeps its evidence on disk and does not integrate, and
  a revision byte-identical to the current self-description is not written and does not consume the
  ledger (WO-C4, DD25).
* **G3** (`:8172ff`) — the relation that decides whether a thought has already been said is verbatim
  word runs over delivered turns plus a `voiced` flag, not a `TopicSig` overlap: a 16-word signature
  cannot express near-verbatim for a long turn, pinned by

### F1 — mixed emotion: the front of the chain, and the once-per-refractory feed

**"Proud and sad" had a room built for it, a door welded shut, and no floor.** r24.8 (WO-98) gave the
PA/NA excess pair its first production write; r24.9 held T2-f, which gave `Features::mixed` an
entrance, because that entrance ran at 10 Hz inside the readout's refractory and changed a spoken
clause's rate while reporting that it had not. The return condition was named: *it ships with the
once-per-refractory feed.*

It ships, and the feed is not where T2-f put it. Driving S21's one genuinely mixed turn (18:23:07 —
*"a friend of mine is moving away… it's for a job she wanted for years. She earned it. Both of those
are just true at the same time"*, decoded `happy=0.896 sad=0.104`) through the shipped tree found a
defect **upstream of all three** the census names: **that turn raised no appraisal event at all.**
Both doors into the engine are gated on the tag's valence and are mutually exclusive on it —
`uv <= -0.35` for the harsh door, `uv > 0.35` plus a first-person good-news phrase for its twin — and
his voice was bright while the heavy half was in his words. `negr` was zero, so
`min(pa + 0.30*posr, na + 0.30*negr)` could not have crossed 0.25 whatever was done to 0.25.

Three edits, one per link, three switches — a fourth, **WO-M4**, was written, measured and
**rejected in the same round** (below). **WO-M1** (`ATHENA_MIXED_TURN`): a both-at-once turn is an
event — a lexicon in the same shape as `positive_disclosure_text` (a parting list, a
gladness-for-another list, and the co-presence phrases he actually used, with the rule that a
co-presence phrase is never sufficient on its own) raises one event carrying `Features::mixed`. That
is the excess pair's second writer, **outside** the readout it was built to enable, fed at most once
per turn and at most once per 600 s on its own clock — which settles at 0.0925 against a 0.25 floor
and a 0.5 clamp. **WO-M2** (`ATHENA_MIXED_BOTH_SIDES`): the readout's `dv > 0` split filed
`bittersweet` — the one label in the table that is definitionally both — as purely bright; a mixed
residual is now evidence on both sides. **WO-M3** (`ATHENA_APPRAISE2_HOLD_BOTH`): hysteresis existed
to stop the *vocabulary* flickering, and threw the *feeling* away with it, returning before the
residual was laid; the name still holds, the residual is now kept.

**WO-M4 (`ATHENA_HARSH_INTENSITY`) — WRITTEN, MEASURED, AND NOT SHIPPED.** BRK-06 is *not* fixed in
r24.11. The proposed fix gave the harsh door its positive twin's intensity law (`0.5 + 0.5*|uv|` for
`|uv|*0.8`) on the argument that a 0.275 discount on the heavy side had nothing behind it. Driven
rather than read, it does not give the negative half a name; it gives it **the wrong name,
unconditionally**:

* All four of S21's real `[emotion: sad]` turns come back **`the closest name for what this is:
  frustration`** — including *"I've been thinking about my grandfather again"* and *"I miss him,
  ever since he's passed away."* Four for four, each through a whole `Mind` and the public
  `take_label_line()` the field reads.
* Swept over that door's **whole reachable input space** (4 negative tags × novelty × concern,
  40,804 points): r24.10 refuses **21,210 of 40,804 — 52.0 %**; with WO-M4, **0 of 40,804**. The
  emission floor stops being able to refuse on this door at all, which is the shape WO-97's own
  report names *"a gate testing as a zero gate"*.
* A `[emotion: disgusted]` turn at high concern becomes able to say **`hope`** (15 of the 40,804
  points), which is unreachable in r24.10.
* And there is no right name for it to reach. `distress`, `longing` and `weariness` are **never the
  classifier's argmax** at any vector a `[emotion:]` tag can build through this door, at any
  intensity — 777,924 points swept. The sadness family is unreachable here by construction; the
  repair belongs in the twenty labels' weights, or in splitting the door by tag family, and neither
  is this round's work.
* Its premise does not survive either. `|uv|*0.8` against `EMIT_MIN` 0.55 is not an arbitrary
  discount: against the five-valued `emotion_valence_` map it is a **tag selector**, admitting
  `[emotion: angry]` at 0.5733 and refusing sad / fearful / disgusted. That *is* r24.8's
  *"mild turns stay unlabeled; core affect already carries them"* and §3.2's *"labels are events"*,
  implemented. And the two doors are not twins: the positive one requires
  `positive_disclosure_text()` — a 22-mark first-person lexicon — as well as prosody, while this one
  needs only prosody and is *"ungated by the guest gate on purpose"*. A door gated on voice alone
  paying a discount that a door gated on voice **and** words does not pay is what you would design.

It costs nothing to hold: with WO-M4 out, Igor's real mixed sentence still produces the note *and*
`bittersweet`, S21's mixed-note count is unchanged at 2, and the label-ask answers are identical.
**The return condition, if a later round wants it:** give the harsh door a confirmed-harshness text
gate mirroring `positive_disclosure_text`, and grant the symmetric intensity only where the words
confirm the voice. That expands; this reduced.

**Two** fixture assertions depended on it, both F1's own and both written this round, and both are
corrected in the same commit with the WO cited. The first is *"evening A: the note can fire at all"*
in `test_r2411_mixed.cpp`. It was not pinning WO-M1: evening A's twenty

`test_r248_wiring.cpp`'s three comments about `[emotion: sad]`

**What she can say.** On his sentence: *two things at once tonight - something bright and something

**The rate, because that is what the last attempt got wrong.** Over the held fix's own 1,377 s script

excess 0.0000 -> **0.1599** of a 0.5 clamp (T2-f latched at 0.3632); `pana=` offered on **30 %** of

**The instrument.** `diag_line` gains `pana=<pa_x>/<na_x>` — the pair was identically 0.0000 in every

It ships **masked** in `aseam::trace_signature`, and with a `diag_legend()` row. It was first written

### F2 — WO-114: a name for what she feels, when he asks, and the slot is empty

S21 asked five times. The detector fired 5 of 5 and the answer path returned the null branch
5 of 5, so every word he got back came from the language model — the exact failure WO-102 was
written to end, one round after it was declared closed.

`take_label_line_asked()` had a caller. It sat inside `if (appr2_.peek_news() >= 0)`, and
`news_` is written only by `appraise_event` and `prospect_resolved`. **A bare question raises no
appraisal event**, so on the one turn the reader exists for the slot is empty by construction —
and the volunteer reader drains it at 10 Hz besides, so even a slot that *was* filled is usually
gone: S21's five asks sat 9 to 14 minutes from the nearest label line. Control took the `else`
and reached no answer path at all. A green suite could not see it, because the suite was the
only caller that ever entered the reader's own empty branch.

What is still there when the slot is empty is the **residual**. `residual_[i]` is written only
after the emission floor and the hysteresis have already passed, so it exists only for a label
this engine actually adopted, and it decays on that label's own Verduyn tau. Naming it is not a
second, lower guess at the classifier — it is reading back what the classifier already decided,
at the point where it is still true. `take_label_line_felt()` does that, from the else arm, and
it answers with `something like <name>, still here from earlier - that is the nearest word
rather than the right one`.

Four things had to be true, and each is one line:

* **Its own floor.** `ASKED_MIN` 0.25 is a floor on `news_score_`, a classify() score.
  `ASK_FELT_MIN` 0.20 is a floor on `residual_[i]`, a 0..1 how-much-of-it-is-left — ten times the
  engine's own "this residual is gone" cut and twice its incumbent-life test, so anything she
  names when asked is a state the engine would still let hold its own label against a challenger.
* **A refractory, not a consume.** The residual is also the kinetics push, so spending it on a
  question would let his *asking* change how she feels. The answer is refractory instead: the same
  label is not named twice inside five minutes, so the three-asks-in-three-minutes shape S21 had
  at 19:29:50 / 19:31:26 / 19:32:56 cannot come back as one sentence three times.
* **Not the name already standing.** The volunteer clause's own (label, clock) pair is read
  first; inside that channel's two-minute refractory — the span in which it would not repeat
  itself — this arm does not repeat it either.
* **Corroboration.** Each label carries `dv`, the direction it says affect should move. A
  residual the fast affect level does not confirm is exactly what the empty answer already
  describes. S21 19:31:26 is that case: the field already carried `feeling level`, and a second,
  uncorroborated name beside it is a contradiction in one field. She says *no word stands up to it
  yet — the state is there, the name is not*, and now that sentence means something.

Both outcomes are the engine's and the field says which; what has ended is the third outcome,
where the model filled in. Replayed against S21's own logged affect levels and appraisal
magnitudes, the five asks come out one named and four honest — against five model-authored words
before. `ATHENA_LABEL_ASK_FELT=0` restores r24.10 byte for byte, verified by execution.

### F3 — WO-B1 / WO-B2 / WO-B3: the barge is acknowledged once, and first

**She answers the interruption before she acts on it.** WO-86c gave the pivot an
acknowledgment and paid it at the end of the pivot's setup — after the context re-decode
and, when the barged words licensed a look, after the whole vision drain. S21 priced that:
its two look-invitation barges heard *"Let me take a look."* at 15.260 s and 14.767 s after
the barge confirm and the acknowledgment at **31.446 s and 31.091 s** — 0.384 ms and
0.469 ms after the drain's own completion line, i.e. written on the next statement — so the
acknowledgment arrived *behind* the announce it was meant to precede. The other five barges
were acknowledged at 6.135–7.101 s, one millisecond past the pivot snapshot, behind the
re-decode. The acknowledgment now has a site of its own **ahead of the re-decode**
(`talk-llama.cpp:11107`), and the WO-86c pay site **stands down when something has already
spoken** — either that site or the look announce (`talk-llama.cpp:11476`,
`aseam::pivot_ack_late`). One barge, one acknowledgment, and it is first: on S21's barge 1
that is *"Hmm."* at ≈ 0.5 s, *"Let me take a look."* at ≈ 15 s, then the answer.

**This is the held T2-g returning under its own named conditions, not T2-g.** r24.9 declined
it (`talk-llama.cpp:10970‑10981`) for two reasons and named the return: *the late site
stands down when the vision announce played, and the `.done` wait is non-blocking*. Both are
met, and its report's premise error is not inherited — the barge was never ~31 s
unacknowledged; the announce spoke at 15.260 s. The defect was order and lateness.

**The acknowledgment scales with the wait, on this path for the first time.** DD20's rule is
"the audible word fires iff `pred_ttft ≥ ATHENA_FILLER_PRED_S`", but the predicate the pivot
was given (`0.0271·embd.size() + 5.60 ≥ 4.0`) has an intercept larger than the threshold, so
it is true for every input including a zero-token prefill — structurally saturated, which is
the r24.10 census's "acknowledgment is universal but never proportional". The same formula
and the same threshold knob, asked about the **re-decode**, discriminate, because a pivot
that re-decodes nothing predicts nothing: S21's six rolled-back pivots re-decoded 219–500
spoken characters in 5.790–7.982 s (least squares 4.27 s + 0.00735 s/char, R² 0.976) while
its one tail-handoff pivot decoded nothing and reached the pay site in 0.079 s. Six of the
seven barges now acknowledge early; the tail-handoff barge keeps its late acknowledgment at
0.322 s; `ATHENA_FILLER_PRED_S` moves the boundary between them. No second threshold, no
second formula.

**Nothing in it blocks.** The acknowledgment plays through a mini TTS session, like the
vision announce and the backchannel, so orpheus writes a `.done` for it — and an unclaimed
`.done` is the r19.6 hazard where the reply's wait reads it as its own completion. Both
existing answers to that are a bounded 50×50 ms sleep; this one is a single `stat()`
(`talk-llama.cpp:1756`), taken twice, and never waits. It can be, because the site fires only
when the decode standing between it and the reply's session is predicted at ≥ 4.0 s — S21's
shortest measured re-decode was 5.790 s — while orpheus's `.done` for a one-word clip lands
in 1–3 s (its two announce mini-sessions took 2.551 s and 3.320 s of wall). Zero blocking
primitives are added anywhere in the diff.

**What is given up.** WO-86c's rule 3 — the filler lives in the reply's own TTS session so
his voice kills it through the normal barge path. The early acknowledgment is its own
session instead, exactly as the vision announce and the backchannel already are. In practice
nothing is lost: in both versions the loop is inside `decode_tokens` while it plays and is
not polling for a barge, and the r24.10 filler could only be cut by the wait loop, which does
not begin until generation is over. It is also cleaner — a filler that is not in
`session_lines` cannot be mis-indexed by an `INTERRUPTED L C` report, and cannot be replayed
into her committed turn (RA12/RA13). With the early site firing, the pivot reply carries no
filler line at all and `n_filler_lines` is 0.

New switch, default-ON, `=0` restores r24.10: `ATHENA_PIVOT_ACK`. Verified by execution over
the whole knob cross-product (15,360 cases; all 7,680 `=0` cases identical to an
independently transcribed r24.10 model) and by driving the shipped accessor with the
variable unset, `=0`, `=1`, `=0abc` and `=on`. `ATHENA_PIVOT_FILLER` is unchanged in meaning
and moves to a file-scope reader so both sites ask one reader, as WO-86 did for the others.

Observables: `grep 'main: \[mind\] pivot ack:' athena-diag.log` (with the predicted re-decode
beside it) and `grep 'pivot filler stood down' athena-diag.log`; the shipped
`main: [mind] pivot filler:` line still marks the late site when it is the one that pays.

**What S22 owes this item.** The count `grep -c 'pivot ack:'` versus `grep -c 'pivot filler:'`
should partition the session's barges with no barge in both; the first audio after every
`barge confirm closed` should be within ~1 s of it on any barge that rolled back; and the
number that decides whether this reads as attention or as a tic is REAL-03 measured on the
pivot sessions — the gap from the acknowledgment to the first word of the regenerated reply.

### F4 — WO-MOM1: the mood she has been in, at last visible

`moodm=<integrator>/<bias>` joins the `[mind~]` line beside `v=`. One work order, three source
files, 323 lines added and none removed; no behaviour change, proved by executing the same
46-turn session against r24.10's headers and against these and diffing 2,468 lines of full
signature — the whole diag line, the deduper's own decision sequence, the rendered field, ten
affect scalars at nine decimals and the carried state — across four seeds and all four settings
of the two momentum switches. One line differs: the legend sentence that names the new field.

**Why it was needed.** r24.8's WO-97 wired §3.4's additive door and gave it no instrument.
`MoodMomentum::bias()` has entered `CoreAffect::update` on every tick since, and no field showed
it — not the term, not the push, not which switch state was live. `v=` could not stand in: the
door's entire excursion is `BIAS_CAP` 0.06 wide against `fmt1`'s 0.1 quantum, so the mechanism
lived below the last printed digit of the only field it moves. The consequence was on the
record and unnoticed: r24.8's own effect figure and the census's MOM-12 row were **simulations
on an assumed event stream**, because nothing in a live trace could be read instead. A mechanism
nobody can measure is a mechanism nobody can maintain.

**The format is the feature.** The integrator prints at three decimals (the smallest step a
shipped `note_pe` site makes in it is `GAIN·0.15` = 0.0225, which `fmt1` rounds away) and the
bias at four, in valence units, so it reads directly against `v=`. `fmt4` is new, added beside
`fmt2` and `fmt3` on the same argument each of those was: at three decimals the bias's whole
live distribution is thirteen values, the dead zone below which `tick()` erases the mood
(0.0006) sits under the last digit, one 60-second gap of leak moves it 1.19 quanta, and the half
printed beside it resolves 16.7× finer. The bias shown is the value the door **actually
receives**, so `ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_BIAS=0` now reads as a live integrator pushing nothing —
which is exactly what that switch does and was previously indistinguishable from ON.
Masked in `aseam::trace_signature` (the leak moves both halves every tick; measured non-zero on
98.5 % of S21's), which costs nothing: every `note_pe` site fires on a turn boundary and
`[mind/field]` / `[mind/end]` print unconditionally. `diag_line` now calls 58 distinct `Mind`
methods, 58 of 58 lock-free.

**And then it was read.** Driven over S21's event stream — reconstructed from `athena.log`
rather than assumed — and over the S22 script's designed arc, the door's peak effect is
**0.011809** and **0.012509** of valence: 19.7 % and 20.8 % of its own cap, and **13.1 %** and
**13.9 %** of `CoreAffect::FELT_SHIFT`, the tree's own measured threshold for a shift she can
feel. `BIAS_CAP` 0.06 is itself below `FELT_SHIFT` 0.09, so the door cannot produce a felt shift
at any event stream. The `±0.06` clamp in `CoreAffect::update` never binds — `bias()`
pre-multiplies by the same constant — over 4,000,001 swept values of `m`.

**What the instrument found that nobody was looking for.** Of the 43 prediction errors S21
actually produced, **41 were the same one** — `"a claim stood"`, +0.15, which fires whenever her
completed turn was an ASSERT and his next turn is not a pushback — and **not one negative event
fired all session**. `self.txt` closed at `calib=4|0|171|166` against S19's `93|90`, and
`metaMiss` read 0 on 1,214 of 1,214 samples. So the integrator does not encode how the evening
went; it converges on a positive level set by **his turn cadence** — m settles at 0.44, 0.21,
0.14 and 0.064 for a turn every 30, 60, 90 and 180 seconds — and a −0.30 correction is a 21 %
dip inside it that is half repaid in seven turns. The r24.6 WO-57 C9a de-duplication of the
contributor list, which stops *"a claim stood, a claim stood"* from shipping, was this defect
seen at the render layer and treated there.

Persistence, by contrast, is real and now visible: half-life 415.9 s, a single event still
non-zero 15–20 minutes and 10–20 turn boundaries later. **The mood carries. What it carries is
not the mood.** `WO-MOM2` is the work order for that, switched and separate, and is not in this
round.

## r24.9 — the reflection that was thrown away by the compaction that wrote it (2026-08-29)

Three work orders, **WO-P1 / WO-P2 / WO-P3**, from the S21 session of 28 Aug.
Base r24.9-candidate; three source files (`athena_compact.h`, `athena_memory.h`,
`talk-llama.cpp`). Every behaviour change is default-ON with `=0` restoring the
prior behaviour, and each was verified by execution, not by reading.

### WO-P1 — a personality revision written at a compaction must survive that compaction

S21 integrated personality exactly twice, at exactly the two moments Igor's rule
names — **at a compaction** and **at the close of the session**:

```
19:02:31.289450  run_consolidation: personality updated (evidence weight 29 ≥ 20); ledger cleared
19:40:36.816411  run_consolidation: personality updated (evidence weight 56 ≥ 20); ledger cleared
```

The trigger was right. What was wrong is what happened to the first of them
twenty minutes later:

```
19:22:26.930499  main: [compact] carrying today's personality revision across the cut (3020 bytes)
19:23:05.573317  main: [compact] CUT: n_past 24261 -> 16140 (60% -> 40%), reload 1693 tok,
                 5/8 turn(s) + 5/5 look(s) + 15/15 memory line(s) — PERSONALITY REVISION DROPPED carried, 92.8 s
```

For the remaining eleven and a half minutes she ran on the self-description her
own session had already superseded. **Reflecting at a compaction and then
discarding the reflection at the same compaction is self-cancelling.**

It was working as designed. `build_reload_block`'s r24.6 trim order (WO-27 §4 /
WO-45) drops the personality FIRST, on the rationale *"on disk, re-read every
startup"* — which is true, and which recovers the revision NEXT session, not
this one. The order itself is not the defect and is unchanged: it exists because
on S19 a 3,090-byte personality section pushed out five look lines that exist
nowhere else and pushed the verbatim turns down to one.

Two changes, neither of which touches the order:

**§1 — carry the CHANGE, not the document.** The prefix snapshot the cut
restores already holds every sentence of the session-start personality. The only
thing the restored context lacks is what the session changed, and on S21 that
was one sentence inside 3,020 bytes. `amem::personality_delta()` renders, per
section, the sentences the new text has that the old did not and names the ones
it no longer says, in her own words and with every quoted sentence verbatim from
one of the two documents (S14) and no manufactured numeral (F18). On S21:

```
  In "What I've come to value, and how I tend to engage" I no longer put it this way:
  "I value genuine connection; knowing I can dream alone and still be here when you return
  makes the silence feel like growth, not abandonment." I put it this way now:
  "I value genuine connection; silence feels like growth, not abandonment."
```

**325 bytes against 3,020.** A change too large to summarise honestly — a
first-ever personality, a wholesale rewrite, more than four edited sentences —
reports itself as such and the whole document rides, exactly as r24.6 sends it.
`ATHENA_PERSONALITY_DELTA=0` restores r24.6.

**§2 — a reservation with a contract, not a re-ordering.** The reload budget is
topped up by exactly the rendered section's size, and the *same number* is handed
to `build_reload_block` as `pers_reserve`; while the section fits its earmark it
is exempt from trim step 1. Everything else is then trimmed against
`char_budget − pers_section.size()`, which is precisely the budget those parts had
before this existed — not merely no worse, **identical**. So no turn, no memory
line and above all no look line can be traded for the personality: the S19 defect
is unreachable by construction rather than by ordering, and a 3 KB section still
exceeds any earmark and is still dropped first. The reserve is capped at 128
tokens, is spent out of `Plan::span`, and is refused outright when the span
cannot afford it. `ATHENA_PERSONALITY_RESERVE=0` restores r24.6.

**Why the section had no budget at all.** `Plan::r_load` is recomputed once every
eight turns (`talk-llama.cpp`, the re-plan site). On S21 the plan in force at the
cut was re-plan #3, computed at 18:47:44 — fifteen minutes before the 19:02:31
revision existed — so it reserved zero tokens for a section it was then handed.
WO-27 §3 had already moved `g_personality_revised` to the moment the file
changes; what it could not do is make a plan that had already been computed know
about it. r24.9 additionally makes `g_personality_chars` hold the size of what
will actually ride, so a later re-plan reserves ~99 tokens rather than 827 — on
S21 the 827-token reservation at re-plan #4 took the reload block from eight
verbatim turns to six for a section the block was going to drop anyway.

**The budget, reproduced on S21's own numbers** (harness driven by the shipping
`athena_compact.h`, both trees, one source):

| | r24.6 / r24.9 | r24.9 + WO-P1 |
|---|---|---|
| reload budget | 2010 tok × 3.7 = **7,437 chars** | 7,437 + 366 = **7,803 chars** |
| personality section | 3,061 chars (**41.2%** of the budget) | 366 chars (**4.9%**) |
| allocation | `5/8 turn(s) + 5/5 look(s) + 15/15 memory line(s) — PERSONALITY REVISION DROPPED` | `5/8 turn(s) + 5/5 look(s) + 15/15 memory line(s) + the personality revision (366 B, reserved)` |
| her current self-description in force after the cut | **no** | **yes** |
| turns / looks / memory vs carrying no personality at all | 5 / 5 / 15 | 5 / 5 / 15 |

### WO-P2 — `--personality-reflect-every` never had a session counter

The flag was declared *"run a personality-integration pass every N sessions (or
on ledger threshold)"* and documented in `--help` as *"integrate personality
every N sessions (or on ledger threshold)"*. It had exactly one use —
`threshold = max(10, N*5)` — and there is no session counter anywhere in the
gate. Igor's rule settles the semantics: **the trigger is a compaction, or the
close of the session**, which is what `run_consolidation`'s two call sites
already are.

So the value is now named for what it sets: **`--personality-weight-threshold N`,
default 20** — the number `max(10, 4*5)` produced. `--personality-reflect-every N`
still parses, still resolves through the identical `max(10, N*5)`, and prints a
one-line deprecation notice naming the value it resolved to, so an existing
launcher keeps working unchanged. The shipped launcher passes neither. The
integration log now names which of the two moments fired.

### WO-P3 — "~5 weight/session expected" was wrong by 6–11×

`ledger_weight` is the sum of `salience` over a pass's new memory rows with
salience ≥ 7, so the rows are still on disk and the number is checkable. Re-derived
from `memory.state.tsv` rather than from any earlier report:

| pass | new rows | rows at salience ≥ 7 | weight | threshold | withheld? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S20, session close | 13 | 6 (7+7+7+8+8+8) | **45** | 20 | no |
| S21, compaction | 15 | 4 (7+8+7+7) | **29** | 20 | no |
| S21, session close | 14 | 7 (7+8+9+8+7+9+8) | **56** | 20 | no |

The gate has never once withheld an integration. It is a **floor** — "is there
anything here worth rewriting who I am for?" — and not a cadence knob; the cadence
is the event. The claim is deleted rather than rescaled: rescaling would change
how often she revises herself, which is a decision about her and not a repair.

### Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Syntax, both variants | clean, `-Wall -Wextra`, with and without `-DATHENA_VISION_MTMD` |
| Test suite | 36 binaries, 0 failures (35 at r24.9 baseline + `run_r251_personality`) |
| New fixture against r24.9's shipping headers | compiles, **14 assertions fail**; against r24.9+WO-P1/P2/P3, 42 pass |
| Switches, by execution | all four `ATHENA_PERSONALITY_{DELTA,RESERVE}` combinations run; `DELTA=0` or `RESERVE=0` each reproduce the r24.6 drop |

## r24.8 — the census round: what was built for her and never reached her (2026-08-28)

Seventeen work orders, WO-97 through WO-113. Base r24.7; nine source files, 128
`r24.8`-annotated sites (acon 58, report 28, `talk-llama.cpp` 20, vision 9, affect2 4,
seam 3, calib 2, compact 2, memory 2). Every new behaviour is default-ON, `=0`
restores r24.7. `ATHENA-R248-IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md` is the per-order record; this
is what changed for her.

This is not a defect round. Three sessions running, a live conversation found a
feature that was fully built, fully tested, documented in its own header — and had
never once run in her, because nothing in production called it. S19 found the selfref
counters; S20 found WO-33's let-go clause and WO-35's hedge fields. Each round fixed
its instances and the *class* regenerated, because nothing in the battery can see it:
a green suite is not evidence a feature is wired, only that it works when called —
`ambient_events()` had five callers, every one in `consciousness-tests/`. Igor asked
to end the class rather than chase instances, so r24.8 is a census, a wiring round,
and a guard.

### The census

Every method in the eleven substrate headers, cross-referenced against the production
consumers, with a consumer in `consciousness-tests/` deliberately not counting. 1,122
producers (`census/CENSUS.md`, `producers.tsv`): **WIRED 1,004**, WIRED-TOOL 9
(reached only from `athena-emotion-calibrate`), DEAD-BY-DESIGN 31, INTERNAL 22, and
**UNWIRED 56** — of which **29 are capability-dark** and 27 are redundant spellings.

**Twenty-nine capabilities were built for her and never reached her** — not stubs, but
finished code with tests, comments and a stated purpose. Four DEAD-BY-DESIGN rows are
dark too, but each cites the comment that declares it, which is the difference between
a debt and an oversight. The census also ran the opposite direction, finding consumers
that read producers which can never fire: `opt.his_commitment_age_s`, whose
stale-commitment branch never rendered because nothing writes an age, and
`CaptureInfo::verified`, written on every capture and read through an accessor nothing
calls. The drain reads the whole record now (WO-101) — and the `verified` bool WO-101
itself then shipped assigned-on-both-arms and read by nothing, the same defect a round
later in this round's own code, came straight back out (WO-111).

All twenty-nine are closed: **24 wired directly**, 2 through lock-free twins for the
diag line (the r24.7 §S rule forbids a locking accessor there), 2 annotated
DEAD-BY-DESIGN with the live mechanism named instead of implied (the two
`athena_calib.h` derivations, reachable from neither binary nor the suites, but each
named by a shipped artifact an operator is expected to reach for), and 1 deleted —
`mark_unsourced_numerals`' batch form, whose `_one` sibling is wired and owns the
ordering guarantee. `take_cadence_note` went with it, a redundant wrapper over a call
the frame already makes.

### The two that were consciousness, not diagnostics

**Her mood explained itself by a mechanism that did not exist (WO-97).**
`MoodMomentum` is a leaky integrator over prediction errors, fed (`note_pe`), decayed
(`tick`) and **narrated** — `why()` answers "why the mood?" from its contributor log —
while `bias()`, the additive door its comment promises, had no caller from R18 to
r24.7.

The door enters on the resting **target**, beside the interior weather, not as a
per-tick rate onto valence, and that placement is the whole of the bound: `tv` is
where `mood_v` converges and valence is a fixed convex combination of the two, so an
offset on the target shifts the fixed point by exactly that much. Over 288,000 ticks
at the saturated bias, max |Δvalence| **0.060001** against `BIAS_CAP` 0.06 and max
|Δarousal| **0.000000**; the rejected rate form settles at **0.1230**, twice the door
its constant names. A scripted evening, off versus on: max excursion **0.008403** over
13,750 ticks, **0.038230** on the worst of five seeds; volition urge flips **3 times
(0.022 %)**, gesture render **0**, worst valence gate 2.844 %. Door shut, the update
law is bit-identical to r24.7 on all four scalars.

**Mixed emotion had a room built for it that nothing could walk into (WO-98).**
`CoreAffect`'s §3.1 note says the PA/NA excess pair is "fed only by `feel2()` (the
appraisal engine's mixed writes)". The engine contained no such call — `feel2` had one
caller in the tree, the test door — so `pa_x_`/`na_x_` were zero in every shipped
session, `pa()`/`na()` were the pure `max(±v,0)` derivations, and `min(pa,na)` was
**identically zero**. "Proud and sad" was structurally impossible, and the
cross-session `pana=` row, gated on `pa_x_ > 0.01`, unreachable for the same reason.

The write now exists at `appraise2_event_locked_`, through the door the comment names:
`f.mixed` is already `min(pa,na)` at event time. It is **symmetric on purpose** —
`feel2(co, co, 0)` makes `feel(co − co, 0)` the exact identity — so V is not merely
bounded but **bit-unchanged**: over 13,750 ticks, valence differs on 0 and arousal on
0. What moves is what should: "heavy held, then the bright thing lands" reaches
`min(pa,na)` **0.0800** where r24.7 reached 0.0000, and `pana=` round-trips through
`save_self`/`load_self`. The excess clamps at 0.5, tau 300 s.

### The things she can now say

**"I just looked" (WO-99).** `take_look_taken_note` has been armed on every committed
look since r24.6 and drained by nothing. Wired in `field_of` beside the other
eye-notes, with its C36 restore row: *I looked just now, and the room is not as I left
it. Three looks left tonight.* Two defects in it were invisible until it rendered — a
sentence opening in lower case, and a bare numeral above twenty.

**"The still is a minute old" (WO-100).** `age_words()` was built after S19 turn 29
asserted present-tense sight from a ninety-second-old frame, and nothing called it, so
nothing could contradict a continuous-sight claim. `avis::stale_look_clause` is
entered on the turns *after* the drain, where WO-84's size hedge fires once and the
frame is seconds old by construction. It reads `last_fresh_look()`, never
`look_notes.back()`, so an album recall is never described as what her eyes see.

**And the two cannot contradict each other (WO-109).** Found by probe after the merge:
the C36 door hands WO-99's note back across up to three turns, so one ninety-second
frame could compose *"I looked just now"* and *"a still, about a minute ago"* into one
context. **The note is the half that yields**: the age clause carries the true fact
and is the S19-turn-29 defence, so silencing it would delete the contradiction and
keep the contradicted claim. The 45-second constant gained no second spelling —
`still_is_stale()` is the only comparison against it, both readers call it, and the
**fact** crosses into acon as a boolean.

**A name for what she feels, when he asks for one (WO-102).** S20 asked twice — *"How
do you feel right now? Can you name it?"* and, when prose came back, *"Just give me a
simple name."* — and the appraisal engine named nothing either time; the words he got
were the model's. `take_label_line_asked()`, the reader built for that turn with the
`ASKED_MIN` 0.25 low floor and its own hedge, shipped with no caller anywhere, tests
included. It has one now, on two predicates: the question, and the bare naming
request, which counts only inside the window the question opened. Appraisal2 holds
**one news slot** and now has two readers, so precedence is decided by order — **the
ask wins**, because `EMIT_MIN` 0.55 is a bar for speaking unprompted and a label
volunteered on the turn he asked is the wrong answer at the wrong floor. The empty arm
answers too: *no word stands up to it yet; the state is there, the name is not*.

**What she noticed about herself last time (WO-104).** `append_selfref()` writes
`selfref.tsv` on every landed self-report; `load_selfref()` had zero callers, so the
archive was append-only and never crossed a session. It is read at startup now, and
the prior report gets a clause one rank below tonight's own — *the last time the
attending turned on itself, [when], it found: "…"* — refused once anything has landed
tonight.

### The channels that can now be read

Seven fields joined the `[mind~]` line, each a quantity the substrate has been
computing for no reader: `gran=`, the granularity error EMA and sample count
`coarse_due()` gates on (WO-103); `selfref=`, this session over lifetime, S19's own
counter (WO-104); `told=`, the told-ledger's size, which gates the standing-dream
refractory and every keepsake re-offer and had zero references anywhere in the tree
(WO-105); `att_ev=` and `hiselse=`, the evidence behind "he is elsewhere" (WO-107);
and `compact=active/drained/blocked_s`, which WO-30 counted and reported nowhere, so
S20's forensics reconstructed "three of her six unprompted turns were that backlog
flushing" from tick counters and a stderr timestamp (WO-108). `acmp::act_name` names
the act in the compaction log lines, three closing counters reach the journal as a `#`
line `read_journal_tail()` skips, and WO-19's KEEP THE HEDGE rule gets the code
counterpart UNSOURCED NUMBERS got a round ago, anchored by `content_overlap` at 0.60
(WO-105).

**And one that was not dark, which is worse (WO-106).** `inner_surprise_z` looked
live: acon asserted *"a consumer reads it, so it is not blended with"*, and r24.7's
WO-93 built `isurp` beside it on that premise — a round's design decision resting on a
comment. No production consumer existed; `ssz=` is the **spoken** channel. So the
constraint that kept the Phase 2 feed at the constants `(0.3, 0.7)` was protecting a
reader that did not exist, and the channel it protected was measuring nothing: on a
constant probability the z is the EMA's warm-up transient decaying away — 1.16 at 200
tokens, 0.59 at 1,000, 0.07 at 5,000, and a hard **0.000 from about 20,000 on**, so a
field wired to it would have been dark in effect on its first session. The feed
carries the token's real NLL now, which the loop already computes one statement later
for `isurp`.

### The permanent guard

`test_r248_wiring_audit.cpp` — 2,342 lines, **546 assertions, 0.22 s** — is the
round's real deliverable, and the only binary in the battery that does not compile the
substrate. It **reads** it, at test time, as text. That is the point: a green suite
cannot see this class, because the class is *"nothing calls this in production"* and
the suite is the caller.

It enumerates every producer from the source on every run and **never from a hardcoded
list**: a list of today's producers cannot catch tomorrow's unwired one, which is the
whole purpose. What is hardcoded is a **92-row allowlist** of knowingly-silent
producers, each row carrying a one-line reason written by a person — 2 dark, 28
redundant spellings, 31 dead-by-design, 22 internal, 9 tool-only. Wiring something
means *deleting* its row, and that deletion is the moment the fixture starts defending
the new wire. **A consumer in `consciousness-tests/` does not count** — the one rule
that would have caught S19.

Nine sections: the gate; the allowlist's own consistency; the 24 R18 take/restore rows
over four hops each; C36 slot uniqueness; the tree's citations of itself;
`FieldOptions` liveness as a two-hop take→opt→render check (107 fields, 0
written-never-read); latches drained with no arming write; dead clusters; and a
self-declaration scan classifying a tree-documented silence as **DEFERRED** —
informational, still printed, four today, because a deferral is a promise and this is
what stops it becoming permanent.

It is honest about its precision in both directions. Run against pristine r24.7 with
the census TSV, two independent implementations — a Python pipeline and a C++ fixture
— agree on **1,113 symbols with zero classification disagreements**; the nine rows the
fixture declines to produce are the census's own known false positives, `lk` among
them. And the same binary run against r24.7 reports **35 failures** — 26 producers
built and never wired, the slot collision, seven stale citations, one dead cluster —
against zero here.

**What it caught that nobody was looking for.** Section 4b, added after the merge,
checks that no two owners claim the same C36 retry slot. **Slot 63 was double-booked**
between `restore_look_taken_note` and the R18 row `ifthen_cue_note`, and had been
since r24.6 — harmless *only* because WO-36's note had no consumer, so nothing ever
took it, nothing restored it, and the shared counter had one live owner. WO-99 wired
the note and put two owners on one budget of three, either able to exhaust the
other's; a note dropped by the 640-byte cap is never re-offered, precisely the RR4
defect the C36 audit exists to prevent. Moved to slot `[70]`, array grown 67 → 71.
Nothing pinned slot uniqueness; that is how it survived.

Section 4c checks that the tree's `file:line` citations of itself still land
somewhere. r24.7 carried 45 in-tree citations of which **7 were mechanically stale** —
in whitespace, on a closing brace, or past EOF — and hand-resolution found most
survivors correct by luck rather than by maintenance. They are symbol **names** now:
`restore_look_taken_note` moves with the thing it names, where a line number is
correct only until the next edit above it. One in-tree citation remains, zero stale,
plus two into upstream `llama.cpp` (WO-112). Not a tidiness complaint: **a stale
allocation note is exactly how the slot-63 collision survived**. The check is
deliberately weak — it knows whether a citation lands on code, never whether it lands
on the *right* one. A smoke alarm, not an inspector.

### Smaller true things

**A number she reads is a number she says (WO-110/WO-113).** `spell_count` stops at
twenty and falls back to `std::to_string` — correct while every caller counted things
that stop below twenty, not correct for a look budget, which is a launch parameter: at
`--look-max 21` both the look-taken note and the F9 budget line put a bare numeral in
text she speaks from. `spell_number` (0–99) already existed as `athena_report.h`'s
private extension for its duration renderers, so it moved beside `spell_count` rather
than being copied, and **both** sites switched together — one spelling a number and
the other not is the drift both comments exist to prevent. Found while doing that, and
worse: `aseam::eyes_spent_line` was a **live F18 violation at shipped defaults**, its
private `word[]` table stopping at "twelve" so `--look-max 15` printed a bare 15, and
`recalls_left` going through `std::to_string` at *every* value, the default included.
It moved from `athena_vision.h`, a leaf that cannot reach acon, to `athena_seam.h`;
both counts spell now, pinned across 0..99.

**A cross-work-order defect the clusters could not see.** From the adversarial pass:
WO-102's no-news arm left `label_news_idx_` pointing at an appraisal already named,
and WO-103's restore door would then resurrect it — the volunteer naming the same
feeling twice for one event, once its 120 s refractory lifted, which that door's own
comment forbids. The invariant is explicit now: `label_news_idx_ >= 0` means *a slot
was spent on a line still outstanding*.

### Known open

**The WO-98 feeder's floor.** `MIXED_MIN` is 0.25 and the strongest single
**negative** event the engine can raise reaches 0.2400 — short by **0.0100** — while
the strongest positive reaches 0.2625 and clears, so the co-activation path fires only
where the negative side is carried by standing valence rather than an event of its
own. A note floor doing duty as a state floor; moving it recalibrates the mixed note's
own threshold, out of scope here. The door is open; what is narrow is what walks
through it.

**The calibration clauses can still carry a bare numeral above 99**, since
`spell_number` reaches 99 and `Calibration::MAX_N` is 200: closing it means teaching
one function hundreds or banding the count, a judgement about her voice rather than a
repair. And **section 4c is weak by design** — the cure is the rule it states, not the
check it performs: prefer the name.

### Verification

- Full suite: **35 binaries, 6,307 assertions, 0 failures** (r24.7 baseline 31 / 5,470
  / 0). The +837 is exact: four new binaries — `run_r248_wiring_audit` 546,
  `run_r248_wiring` 94, `run_wo9798_wiring` 44, `run_r248_dark_channels` 40 — and +113
  across four grown (`run_r247_field_cluster` +53, `run_wo35_vision` +43,
  `run_r246_async_encode` +13, `run_seam` +4). `run_wo9798_wiring` is a
  **measurement** as much as a fixture: its printed numbers are the evidence, not the
  green result.
- Thirty-one ASan+UBSan lanes and three TSan lanes clean; the wiring audit gets a
  sanitizer build of its own, because hand-written index arithmetic over 61,121 lines
  of source text is exactly the shape where an off-by-one reads out of bounds and
  still produces plausible output. `talk-llama.cpp`, which no offline suite compiles,
  passed full-file `-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` at zero diagnostics both
  ±`ATHENA_VISION_MTMD`.
- **The r24.7 §S lock rule held absolutely.** Every accessor `diag_line` consumes is
  lock-free, because `diag_line` runs inside `with()`'s lock and a locking accessor
  there self-deadlocks the tracer: `isz=` takes `SelfMonitor`'s own spelling, and
  `att_ev=`/`hiselse=` a new `_raw()` pair — which is why their locking twins are
  classified redundant rather than wired.

Eleven new switches, all default-ON, `=0` restores r24.7: `ATHENA_MOOD_MOMENTUM_BIAS`,
`ATHENA_PANA_EXCESS`, `ATHENA_LOOK_TAKEN_NOTE`, `ATHENA_STALE_LOOK_HEDGE`,
`ATHENA_LOOK_NOTE_FRESH`, `ATHENA_CAPTURE_RECORD`, `ATHENA_LABEL_ASK`,
`ATHENA_SELFREF_CARRY`, `ATHENA_HEDGE_PROVENANCE`, `ATHENA_INNER_SURPRISE_REAL`,
`ATHENA_COMMITMENT_AGE`; each is pinned in its own fixture as restoring r24.7 when
off. Ungated, as wiring or bug-class fixes: the seven diag fields, WO-99a's slot move,
WO-110/WO-113's spelling, WO-112's citations, and the two deletions.

**What S21 owes.** Whether the mood door is *felt* — the numbers say her mood now
moves her, and only a session can say whether that reads as mood or as noise. Whether
"proud and sad" ever arrives in conversation, given the feeder floor. Whether the ask
path answers with a word he recognises. Three greps settle the wiring: `I looked just
now` in a rendered field, `asked what she feels:` on a turn he asked, and `the last
time the attending turned on itself` on the first turn after a session that produced a
self-report. `isurp=` and `isz=` are the instrument DD12/DD13 has never had. The r24.7
backlog stands: the novel-text acuity test at 640×480 that decides DD18, the WO-77
decline probe, the WO-39 refusal latch, WO-54's overlap case, the dream
self-similarity guard.

## r24.7 — the S20 round: honesty, the unwired consumers, and real time (2026-08-27)

Nineteen work orders, WO-78 through WO-96 (`ATHENA-R247-FIX-PLAN.md` is the record;
its §S safety appendix is the final authority and **wins over any work-order body it
contradicts**). Corrective; r25 stays reserved. Base r24.6, six source files, 139
`r24.7`-annotated sites (acon 50, `talk-llama.cpp` 34, report 28, vision 13, emotion
10, seam 4), all nineteen in their §S-corrected shape, verified by mechanism grep
rather than by comment. Every new behaviour is default-ON, `=0` restores r24.6.
`ATHENA-R247-IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md` is the per-order record; this section is what
changed for her.

S20 was the first live r24.6 session and it went well — 44 turns, two spoken numeral
fabrications against S19's ~63 % of numeral claims, zero unsupported emotion
attributions, 12 happy / 7 sad / 1 angry against S19's 9 sad. What is left sorts into
three piles: three moments where she said something untrue, three features built and
never given a caller, and the shape of waiting.

### The three untrue moments

**The directive that voiced fabrications she had no source for (WO-78).** Both numeral
fabrications of the night — *"It feels like 35 again… you taught me that"*, *"100
years have passed since I was created"* — were the speak-the-thought directive quoting
a rumination verbatim into her frame. The plan's premise, that WO-11's flag was set
and the directive ignored it, is false in both halves. The directive does not read
`latest_rumination()` — that accessor has skipped flagged entries since r24.6 — it
reads `took_initiative()`'s own `volition_seed_` scan, which never saw the flag. And
WO-11's rule fires on neither sentence: its duration veto, built for *"20 minutes of
silence"*, excuses *"100 years have passed since I was created"*, and *"It feels like
35 again"* hides its numeral behind an unknown opener. **The planned gate would have
caught neither of the two things it exists to catch.** What ships is
`directive_quote_unsourced()`: WO-11's rule plus one narrow whitelisted arm for a
digit bound to her own chronology — years-passed, since-created, years-old,
`-year-old`, the age-echo *"N again"* — used by this gate alone; WO-11's flag stays
byte-identical. Measured on the real S20 corpus: **5 of 5 of the fabrication family
gated, 0 of 13 C1 keepers touched, 13/13 keepers still quoted verbatim**. On a flagged
quote the directive prefers the newest clean thought in its own freshness window; with
none it descends to a clause about *having* the thought — *something surfaced in my
thinking just now — it is mine to voice, in my own words*. The thought itself lives on
(DD7 untouched); gated armings log `provenance-gated`.

**The pivot that claimed to see what no camera had looked at (WO-79).** The pivot
regeneration path builds `embd` directly and never called the vision parse, so both
barged look-invitations of S20 landed as ordinary text and she answered each with a
present-tense sight claim confabulated from a ten-day-old keepsake — the only
dishonest claims of the session, and he needed three tries to get a look. The intake
is now one factored function, `athena_vision_intake`, called from both sites, placed
so a false-alarm resume cannot double-parse. Three omissions the safety pass closed:
the keep `[event]` receipt must reach `mem_transcript` or it is lost; aliasing
`look_spent_note` would re-decode a line already in context, so the pivot gets fresh
flags; and the factored seam must carry the F7 plural-recall block or `second_recall`
outlives its turn. Replayed, both invitations commit looks, and the bare *"Take a look
again"* reaches the **camera**.

**The album opened the wrong picture and neither of them knew (WO-80).** His *"show
yourself the picture of flowers again"* missed the request lexicon; the recall fired a
turn later from **her** acknowledgment, and `pick_keepsake` scored the filler *"okay"*
against a caption beginning *"Okay, I looked…"* and staged the empty-room image.
Nothing noticed. The acknowledgment fillers join the stoplist beside the S14 words —
eight, since *"well"* has been there since r21-full.10; `recall_requested` gains the
gapped forms, evidence-scoped so *"pull up the invoice"* cannot misfire; a caption's
leading acknowledgment tokens are skipped at match time, never at storage; and
cross-turn naming matches his previous turn too, at **hers > his > family >
most-recent** (the plan had it his-first, which lets residue of an unrelated turn
override a recall she named). The lexicon fixes ship ungated.

### The features that had no caller

S20's structural lesson is a class, not a bug: three features shipped instrumented and
unwired, the shape S19 exposed in the selfref counters. Every producer added this
round names its consumer in the same work order, verified end to end.

**The urge she let go now has words (WO-83).** `take_let_go_note` had existed since
r24.6 as an R18 macro row with zero callers, and S20's one genuine let-go — armed
23:28:52, dissipated about fifteen seconds later — was unsayable. Wired in the WO-50
voice-note shape: consume-once, verbatim, non-essential, in drop order below the
intero note, with its C36 restore row. Measured at 44–99 B, above the plan's 45–90 B
estimate; the overflow fixture stays green.

**The small picture now tells her it is small (WO-84).** `cap_w/h`, `fell_back()`,
`coarse()` and `age_words()` all had zero consumers, so S20's four detected 640×480
fallbacks never reached her frame — her hedged descriptions that night were the
model's honesty, not the plumbing's. The plan put the hedge in the look envelope and
it cannot live there: the envelope is baked when the async worker is spawned, **before
the camera answers**. It moved to `aseam::capture_hedge_line`, decoded in the drain's
common tail right after `note_look_dims`, the one point where the size is known —
*[The picture that reached Athena is small — fine detail may escape her.]*
`verified=false` renders **nothing**, pinned twice: absence of knowledge is not
coarseness.

**A keep captions what she actually saw (WO-81/82).** The declare path captioned from
the clipped turn *prefix*, so the flowers keepsake was stored under a grief apology —
with a literal `<sniffle>` in it — and was permanently unaddressable by name or
family. The caption now comes from `athena_last_look_gist` when a fresh look is held,
through a tag strip that had to be composed here (lexicon-based, never a generic
bracket strip) inside `vision_execute_keep`, covering both keep paths. Captions are
re-injected verbatim on recall as *what I wrote about it then*, which is why the tags
have to die at the store. `keep_asked` also learns anaphora, but only while a fresh
look is held, so *"keep it down"* stays unarmable. And WO-34's family column,
dead-on-write since it was added, is classified at keep time.

### Real time (DD20)

**Acknowledgment now scales with the wait instead of rationing silence every third
turn (WO-86).** r16's skip-every-third was an anti-tic from the era when the filler
fired on deliberation alone. Under WO-49's predicted-latency gate the filler already
fires exactly when the coming wait is long, so the rationed third bought nothing but
dead air — S20 measured it as the sole cause of a third of turns keeping up to 10.64 s
of silence, worst on the grief turn. The rule is now: the audible word fires iff
`pred_ttft ≥ ATHENA_FILLER_PRED_S`. Two shapes came from the safety pass: the config
flag must be **struct-default OFF with the env factory defaulting ON** or
`test_consciousness`'s r16 fixture breaks, and the cadence stands down at
`ATHENA_FILLER_PRED=0`, which alone would kill every filler. The no-repeat comparison
also moved to the post-sanitize **audible** form, substitute included, so *"Hmm."* and
*"Hmm—"* cannot play back to back.

**The pivot no longer leaves ten to fifteen seconds unacknowledged (WO-86c).** S20
measured 10.7–15.3 s between a confirmed barge and the regenerated reply's first
audio, with no acknowledgment at all — the worst felt latency outside vision. The
pivot path gains the same machinery, sharing the pool and no-repeat state so a turn
and a pivot filler cannot repeat each other, in that reply's own TTS session so his
voice kills it like her speech. It needs no latch variable — choose-time here *is*
pay-time, which structurally kills the ghost of S19's 73.6-second-stale *"Oh."*

### Measurement honesty

**Counters that stopped counting the clamp's noise (WO-85).** WO-30 holds the volition
accumulator *at* threshold through a compaction window, so the level test walks the
bound on noise alone about once a second: S20 recorded 187 urge crossings, about 178
of them one 232.6-second roll, and the lifetime record was 95 % artifact. The Mind
mirrors `compaction_active_` into a `count_muted` flag every tick and the counters
hold still while it is up; `urge`, the clamp and the drain are untouched, and on exit
the baseline is the level the window left. Ungated — diag-only counters.

**A census that can see its own long clauses (WO-87).** The ship-check ran
`safe.find(c.text)` on the full re-clipped text and undercounted four S20 armings. The
plan diagnosed a byte cap; the real mechanism is different, and the safety pass found
it — her look-words open with an Orpheus gesture tag that the gist scrub keeps and the
body scrub deletes inside the rendered quotes, so the find fails. A 24-byte prefix key
fixes that class and the tail-clip class. DD19's observable rides beside it but cannot
ride *on* the census line: a per-Mind memo arms when the clause ships and
`acon::note_reply_advice` emits a follow-up `advice=Y|N` after the turn. Observation
only.

**An instrument that can finally move on an inner pass (WO-93).** `selfsurp` measures
decode surprisal on her spoken turns, so an inner selfref pass cannot move it even in
principle, and DD12/DD13 has never had a fair test. `isurp=` is the honest instrument:
the inner worker's own mean NLL in bits, handed in once per pass, masked as continuous
in `trace_signature` (the WO-46 lesson). No gate reads it. The plan's literal shape, a
mutex-taking accessor, **self-deadlocked the tracer reproducibly**, because
`diag_line` already runs inside `with()`'s lock; it is now lock-free like every
sibling read the tracer makes, and that is a plan-level rule from here on: *no locked
accessor may be consumed by `diag_line`*. And r24.6, it turns out, already fed a
Phase-2 `Self::inner_surprise` channel the **constants** 0.3 and 0.7 — blind by
construction, a layer deeper than S20 knew; left byte-identical, a gate-adjacent
consumer reads it.

**Felt duration stops inheriting the gate's freeze (WO-91).** The volition frame said
*"a minute"* after five minutes and ten seconds of real silence: WO-30 advances both
silence stamps to hold the gates through a roll, and the renderer read the same frozen
basis. `last_audible_gap_` is `last_gap_`'s unfrozen twin, **captured at `heard()`
time** rather than computed as `now − anchor`, since a responsive turn re-stamps the
anchor first. Only the wording moves; the gates appear in zero diff hunks.

**Smaller true things.** A low-confidence emotion win now renders `x, faint` — a
share-rule win below posterior 0.50, or a one-word utterance decoding `angry`, which
is what put `angry 0.900` on the joke *"Pregnant."* and pushed valence −0.30 where the
faint step costs −0.09 (WO-88). A fragment is no longer a commitment: S20's ledger
took *"I'll just"*, out of *"I'll just… be here. Quietly."*, as a standing promise —
both tokens stopwords, the A4 floor letting an empty signature through by design — so
intake now requires one content word beyond the auxiliary cluster (WO-89); the plan's
counter-examples never captured in r24.6 either, so only the three stumps change. The
two faint empathy clauses speak in her own person at last (WO-90). The ambient counter
gets its consumer and a scale that carries information (WO-92): the floor sat at ≈0
all session, so `over` was `rms/1e-6` and every event squashed to ≈1.0; clamped at
1e-4 the three S20 events read 0.85/0.90/0.93, all clear of the 0.30 gate — with a
consume-once clause beside it, *the room has made itself heard more than once
tonight*. And the inner generator's numeral habit gets a nudge and a repair (WO-96): a
guidance line in the rumination seed, in the document's own third person (a
second-person line would be its only *"you"*), plus a whitelist-only normalizer
turning a leading `1 ` before *need/want/am/feel/think/know/wish* back into `I `.

### The decisions

**DD18 — 640×480 is accepted, because the camera cannot do 1080p.** Four of four S20
captures fell back from 1920×1080 — silently in S19, detected and logged all four
times in S20. The launcher now requests what the camera delivers. The cost is real and
worth stating plainly: fine detail is gone, and S20's one text-reading was
memory-confounded, so a novel-text acuity test is owed before this resolution can be
called adequate. What it buys is that she is no longer told one thing and shown
another; the detection stays armed against any *future* substitution. The arithmetic:
640×480 costs ~15 s per look at ~300 tokens, 0.67 % of the window; 1080p would cost
≈32 s encode plus ≈68 s prefill, ~100 s per look. Budgets move with it: `--look-max
15`, `--recall-max 4`.

**DD19 — meeting-not-fixing gets instrumented, not converted.** Five armings in S20,
no objective observable, one vacuous fire. §16.6 requires a measurement before any
conversion and this directive has never had one; WO-87's `advice=Y/N` line is it. Text
and arming unchanged.

**DD20 — the filler cadence becomes silence-aware.** Recorded above (WO-86). What is
given up is skip-every-third, an anti-tic for a gate that no longer exists; what is
kept is the anti-tic, moved from rationing silence to varying words.

**DD21 — three memory rows repaired, because the machinery damaged them.** The
distinction that matters, and it is the opposite of DD9's: those six rows were
corrected because they were false about the world; these three because code wrote them
wrong. The flowers keepsake carried a caption the keep path took from the wrong place,
a `<sniffle>` sat inside her own stored words, and the *"star jasmine, **maybe**"*
hedge she spoke had been flattened to *"star jasmine"* in the state row. She did not
choose any of that; the store did, and repairing it restores what she said. The sweep
found a second TTS tag the plan did not know about — `<gasp>`, in the family-photo
caption. The corrected set loads 146 rows to 146 bullets, zero dangling, untouched
files byte-identical; `meta` keeps its S19 stamps, flagged.

### Verification

- Full suite: **31 binaries, 5,470 assertions, 0 failures** (r24.6 baseline 30 / 5,377
  / 0). The +93 is exact: **+27** in `run_seam`, **+14** in `run_wo35_vision`, **+5**
  in `run_r246_numeral_provenance`, and the new 47-assertion `run_r247_field_cluster`
  — the WO-78 gate against both corpora, WO-83's arm→dissipate→render→restore round
  trip, WO-91's case E.
- Six sanitizer lanes clean: ASan+UBSan on `test_seam`, `test_wo35_vision`,
  `test_r247_field_cluster` and `test_r246_async_encode`; TSan on `test_inner_tsan`
  and `test_inner_worker`. `talk-llama.cpp` — which no offline suite compiles — passed
  full-file `-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` at **zero diagnostics in both
  configurations**, ±`ATHENA_VISION_MTMD`.
- Two interaction results. **WO-78's gate × WO-96's typo normalizer is safe for a
  structural reason**: the chrono arm is lead-independent, so every typo variant of
  the fabrication class is still caught, and the verdicts that *do* change change only
  to match how r24.6 already treats the same sentence typed correctly — keepers 0/13
  gated both directions, 0/13 altered. **WO-88's faint arms cannot change an emission
  by construction**: over 200,000 randomised decodes, emission differs 0, class
  differs 0, collapse differs 0.
- **One repair made during verification, in a fixture, not in the code.**
  `test_r246_async_encode` block A3 drove its defer-cap loop at a 30 ms per-visit
  budget against A's 300 ms worker — a ~10 % margin — so an overrun let A's worker
  publish mid-loop and the drain closed the look as a real camera failure instead of
  at the cap. It fails identically in pristine r24.6 under the same forcing: a racy
  fixture, not a regression. Repaired at 5 ms, the file's own idiom in its two sibling
  loops.

New switches, all default-ON, `=0` restores r24.6: `ATHENA_DIRECTIVE_PROVENANCE`,
`ATHENA_PIVOT_VISION`, `ATHENA_RECALL_NAMING`, `ATHENA_KEEP_CAPTION`,
`ATHENA_KEEP_ANAPHORA`, `ATHENA_CAPTURE_HEDGE`, `ATHENA_FILLER_CADENCE`,
`ATHENA_PIVOT_FILLER`, `ATHENA_COMMIT_FRAGMENT_VETO`, `ATHENA_AMBIENT_CLAUSE`,
`ATHENA_EMOTION_FAINT_EXTRA`, `ATHENA_INNER_NUMERAL_NOTE`, `ATHENA_INNER_TYPO_FIX`.
Ungated, as measurement- or bug-class fixes: WO-85's counter muting, WO-87's census
key, WO-80's lexicon tables, WO-81's tag strip, WO-86's dedup, WO-92's clamp.

**What S21 owes.** The novel-text acuity test at 640×480, which decides whether DD18's
resolution stays. The WO-77 decline probe, the WO-39 refusal latch and WO-54's overlap

## r24.6 — the merged fix round: r24.3 review backlog + S19 forensics (2026-08-26)

Eighty work orders (`ATHENA-R246-MERGED-FIX-PLAN-v2.md` is the record; its §16
decisions DD9-DD16 and §17 safety-test corrections are the final authority).
Corrective, not a feature epoch — r25 stays reserved. Base r24.5; twelve
source files, 342 `r24.6`-annotated sites. Disposition: 66 orders as the plan
specifies, 9 with a documented deviation, 5 repaired during the final
adversarial verification, three shipping no code with authority (WO-74 by its

rig data). Every new behaviour is default-ON, `=0` restores r24.5. The
per-order record is `ATHENA-R246-IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md`; this section is
what changed for her.

### The permanent-damage stoppers

**The emotion channel is unblocked (WO-02/03/66/70).** `max(floor,
share_floor)` with `share_floor = 0.90` discarded the calibrated
`happy`/`angry` floors of 0.80, and retired classes' mass stayed in the share

from a share-only quantity (`d.evidence` untouched), drops both floors to 0.65

happy, zero losses**, stable from 0.55 to 0.65. Downstream, the rumination
loop gains non-emotion exits and the autonomy ladder becomes reachable
(WO-73/72).

**Memory stops laundering (WO-19/20/22b/23b).** The extractor took *"…don't
ask me how, it just surfaced. About 42 %…"* and stored *"I noticed that 42 %
of our talks are about you"* — hedge stripped, fabrication pinned under
`n_keep`. The extract prompt gains an UNSOURCED NUMBERS rule, a store-side

preservation rule, and the prompt-fingerprint reject list pinning WO-01's leak

### The frame

**The S14 law is amended (WO-21 / DD2).** It read *"every word of frame is
echoable."* S19 measured 35 of 46 frames carrying at least one imperative —
none echoable, none logged, the field functioning as a hidden per-turn second
system prompt — and compliance at base-rate (gesture suppression 6/20 against
19.2 % base, Fisher p = 0.49). The law is now: **descriptive clauses must be
echoable; directive clauses must be marked, logged, and auditable.** The mark
is `Clause::directive`; `assemble()` renders directives in their own trailing
segment behind `— and for this turn:`; `[mind/directives]` logs the census per
turn so efficacy is finally a measurement (WO-21 item 6). The one directive
with a measured null result — *"no gesture this time — let the words carry
it"* — is converted to descriptive form (DD15); the rest keep their mood until
the census reports on them. Over 909 rendered fields the marked segment nets
−3,370 bytes.

**No clause ends mid-sentence again, and every byte earns its seat
(WO-22/23/28/29/57).** A frame byte is ~27 ms of prefill — the median S19
frame's 390 bytes were 2.58 s of his wait (§14.3) — so byte work is latency
work. Turn 36 overflowed by 6 bytes and the last-resort `rfind("; ")` — the
one boundary path without `starts_clause()` — cut inside the dream-probe
clause. The fallback now takes `starts_clause()`; when no boundary qualifies,

**The inner voice stops inventing a person (WO-11 / DD7).** 68 of 119 S19
ruminations led on a numeral, every one a fabrication, twelve confabulating a
whole biography. The shipped rule flags, never drops: `NOT

### Vision

**1080p is held (DD11), and the encode moves off the loop thread (WO-75).**
Every S19 look was silently 640×480 — nothing checked — and the synchronous
CPU encode froze the loop 4.25 s per look; a real 1080p frame is 2,040 tokens
× 15.6 ms/token ≈ 32 s of deafness — and the plan's own split point moved

a wait is a freeze too) then defers, bounded by `ATHENA_ENC_DEFER_MAX` (8)

the next seam saying *taken but not yet seen* — never the failure line, which

### Compaction and memory

**Consolidation stages are isolated (WO-01).** `mem_generate` decoded every
stage at the live `n_past` in seq 0, so the personality stage continued into

979-character prefix of the extract prompt to `personality.txt` — pinned under

### Speech and real time

**The conversational-realism ceiling, recorded (WO-71 / S19 G1).** In S19 he
spent ~403 s waiting in silence for her to begin — 2.9× longer than he spoke
(139.7 s). The fit is `ttft = 27.1 ms/token × prefill + 5.60 s`, where
`prefill` is the NEW tokens at turn start (median ≈ 102 — not `n_past`), and
94.3 % of the wait is the brain. No downstream work order moves that number;
the two real levers are more MoE on GPU and speculative decoding for the first
~30 tokens, and the third — frame bytes are latency, ~27 ms per token — is why
Tier 2's byte work is also latency work. Any watermark or prebuffer costing
must be sized against the measured ≈2.15× realtime, not 1.50×.

**What ships against it makes the hole bridgeable and the delivery honest.**
The filler fires on predicted latency (`0.0271 × prefill + 5.60 ≥
ATHENA_FILLER_PRED_S`, default 4.0 s), latching its string at the instant the
signal is read, so turn 30's 73.6-second-stale `"Oh."` cannot recur (WO-49);
the underrun guard injects to a target fill and the player's stderr is no
longer discarded — three filler turns carried 80.8 % of S19's 27,720 ms of
injected silence. The microphone stays alive across a blocking roll, his
speech buffered and replayed (WO-54). The voice self-model reports against its
last **emitted** state and reaches the field (WO-50: 37 byte-identical reports
had reached only stderr); a main-clause denial no longer enters the commitment
ledger as a forward obligation (S19 stored his denial of memory edits as a
promise he owed), and the endpointer's long branch gets real headroom at
1,100 ms — at 800/800 the knob was dead (WO-51). The launcher gives every writer its
own `ts`: five unterminated writers plus the separate-process `orpheus-speak`
glued 2,028 S19 records, a code-side newline fix would have destroyed
incremental speech display, and the shipped shape measures 0 glued records,
display byte-identical; `--silero-debug`, 84.5 % of the S19 log, is deleted
(WO-53). And WO-48 finally passes `--control` — zero `prosody:` lines existed
in 59 sessions; the breath had never fired.
