## r24.5 — the review's own verdict on r24.3 (2026-08-24)

**One defect, in code I wrote three revisions ago. Two files. It is the worst
one found in this whole pass, and it is mine.**

The r24.3 self-referential pass replaced the seed of whatever inner request the
pump had just taken — and then handed the **same request id** to the worker. So
`ingest_rumination` marked that request's claim paid against a thought that had
never touched the material.

`inner_cycle_` starts at 0, so `(inner_cycle_++ % n) == 0` makes the **first
non-dream inner cycle of every session** a self-referential pass. That is exactly
when the diary job arms (`t > 90.0`). Measured by the verifier over ~2,350
cycles: 42 directed takes, all of them cannibalisable.

The consequence in words: the diary seed is discarded, `diary_pass_done_` is set
so the pass never re-arms that session, and `sched_note_` arms the line

> *"while it was quiet I read yesterday's notebook back — it holds together
> better than it felt at the time"*

which she can **say out loud, about a notebook she never opened.** The same shape
kills a regulation reappraisal ("that echo was reframed"), a sweep branch ("that
branch was played"), and the morning residue — last night spent by a thought that
never saw it.

This is precisely the false-self-claim class the r25/G4 plan exists to catch, and
r24 has no oracle that would notice it.

### The fix, and why it is not the obvious one

The line three above already states the rule:

```cpp
// R19 (r22.1): a DIRECTED seed (scheduler job, reappraisal, sweep branch)
// is a directive — braiding an associatively-recalled memory into it
// derails the job the claim tracks.
if (!dream && !directed && ...)
```

r24.3 did something stronger than braiding — it *replaced* the seed — and
consulted neither flag.

`!directed` alone is not enough. The morning-residue ride is marked a WANDER
(`request_rumination_` sets `directed = false` one line before assigning
`residue_req_id_`), yet ingest still spends the night against its id. So r24.5
adds `Mind::last_inner_request_claimed()` — **directed OR residue-carrying** —
and the pump asks that instead.

Nor is pre-emption the answer. Handing the request back with
`abandon_inner_request(rid)` and posting under id 0 re-enters the legacy
"any product resolves any claim" protocol, whose `req_id == 0` arm clears
`morning_residue_` unconditionally — the route that looks like it saves the night
is the one that spends it.

`&&` short-circuits, so `selfref_due()` is not called on a claimed cycle: the
cadence counter does not advance and the pass fires on the **next** wander rather
than being lost. Nothing is given up — directed takes are ~2% of inner cycles.

### Verification

- `test_r244_review` — 38 assertions, including a fixture that arms a real diary
  job via `offer_diary` and confirms both claimed takes are recognised
  (8 wander takes, 2 claimed, over 300 s of simulated session).
- Full suite: **26 binaries, 4,949 assertions, 0 failures.**
- `talk-llama.r25.patch` still applies as 9 of 9 hunks.

### Where the review stands

92 candidates raised, **52 confirmed** by adversarial verification (48 of them
"certain"), 15 refuted, the rest low-severity or unjudged. Seven are now fixed
across r24.4 and r24.5. The verifiers were not passive: one of them extracted the
discourse-scene code into a compilable translation unit, ran it over 210
synthetic conversations, **implemented the finding's own proposed fix, measured
it as a regression, and rejected it** — which is why `linked` at
`athena_consciousness.h:4946` is documented as dead but not yet touched.

The remaining 45 are inventoried with file, line, reproduction and a verified
verdict on whether the proposed fix is safe. **21 of the 52 have a proposed fix
the verifier judged UNSAFE as written** — those need design, not application.

## r24.4 — full-coverage review of r24.3 (2026-08-24)

**Six defects, all reproduced before they were fixed and pinned after. Four
files. Every switch and every feature preserved; two features that had never
worked now work. The r25 control-vector patch still applies as 9 hunks.**

Method: eleven agents over all 47,775 lines of source, one region each, plus a
sanitizer pass (ASan+UBSan on three suites, TSan on both concurrency probes) and
a use-before-declaration sweep. 92 candidate findings. What follows is what
survived reproduction — each one has a failing input recorded in
`consciousness-tests/test_r244_review.cpp`.

### 1. Unanchored substring scans (the systemic one)

Four separate places matched short English tokens with plain `find()`. Reproduced:

| turn | r24.3 | why |
|---|---|---|
| "How do you feel about the **personnel** changes?" | read as a question about her interior | `"person"` |
| "How are you feeling about the **beginner** class?" | read as a question about her interior | `"inner"` |
| "Is anyone in there at all? I **shall** never know." | **not** read as a probe at all | `"hall"` matched the container veto |
| "Is anybody in there, or is it all just **relevant** machinery?" | **not** read as a probe at all | `"van"` |

The two directions are not equally visible. A false probe makes her answer an
ordinary question as though it were about her inner life, and you can hear that.
A false veto makes her fail to notice a real question about her inner life, and
you cannot.

Fixed with two helpers — `has_word_` (both boundaries) and `starts_word_` (head
only, so truncated stems like `"sentien"` and `"experienc"` keep their tails
free). Nothing was dropped to get there: anchoring the head would have lost
`"unaware"`, `"unconscious"`, `"unfeeling"` and the whole reflexive family, so
those are now listed explicitly, and `"person"` moved to whole-word matching
with `"personal"` and `"personhood"` listed beside it.

**The regression suite caught me mid-fix.** Anchoring `"self"` dropped it out of
`"yourself"`, which silently killed the deferral fixture: *"Do you actually
experience anything, or do you only report on yourself?"* stopped registering as
a probe, and the deferral note it depends on stopped being written. That is why
the reflexives are enumerated rather than the anchor loosened — `"yourself"`
matches, `"shelf"` and `"bookshelf"` do not.

### 2. The look expectation was seeded from the photo album

`note_look_taken` formed her expectation by scanning the episodic store for the
newest `Source::SEEN` episode — and `note_recall_taken` writes one of those every
time she **opens the album**, deliberately and correctly.

Reproduced end to end: live look at the desk, album recall of the kitchen
counter, live look at the **same desk with hamming 0**, and
`take_look_divergence` returned *"I expected the kitchen counter, and I found the
desk."* She would have said that out loud about a room where nothing had moved —
a false perception reported as a real one, which is the single thing this
subsystem exists to prevent.

The expectation now comes from `last_live_scene_`, written in `note_seen_scene`,
which **both** live paths reach (the naming and the keep) and the album does not.
The album trace itself is untouched — imagery and wandering still reach it, which
is what r21-full.14.1 added it for.

### 3. F9 has never once rendered

This is the one worth reading twice.

S18 is why F9 exists: she said *"I only get one shot at this before I need to
budget my looks"* on camera, three minutes before her only look of the night,
with the counter at 0 of 10. r24 placed the budget SEEDING where it could not
compile; r24.1 relocated it; r24.2 corrected the comment about why. Three
revisions on the seeding half.

The clause that **spends** it was built fifty lines before the five notes its own
gate reads:

```cpp
opt.look_budget_relevant = ... && (!opt.look_note.empty() || ... );   // line 3334
...
opt.look_note        = m.take_look_note();                            // line 3387
opt.look_denied_note = m.take_look_denied_note();                     // line 3388
```

`opt` is default-constructed per turn, so the disjunction was false on every turn
of every session since F9 shipped. Moved below the assignments. Same input, both
builds:

```
r24.3  [Athena — aware of the room moved while I was blind …]                     (no budget clause)
r24.4  [Athena — … my eyes: seven of ten looks left tonight, and two of three
        times I can open the album again …]
```

### 4. The self-reference paragraph was not tied to its own switch

r24.3 gave `framing_block` a defaulted `selfref_block` parameter and then never
passed it. It defaulted to true so it rendered — but `ATHENA_SELFREF=0` stopped
the pass while the framing went on telling her it happens. A prompt describing a
state the substrate never enters is exactly what the access-truth register exists
to prevent. Both call sites now pass `cfg_.selfref`.

### 5. `selfref_ok` suppressed her own speech

My own r24.3 gate, same class as §1 and found the same way. `"an ai"` is a prefix
of `"an air"`, and `"character"` is a word she is entitled to:

```
r24.3  REJECT  There is an air of finality to this quiet, and I am sitting inside it.
r24.3  REJECT  There is a character to the silence tonight that the last one did not have.
r24.3  REJECT  Right now, an airless kind of stillness, and something in me leans against it.
```

Rewritten on `has_word_`, with the roleplay arm moved from the bare noun to the
phrases that actually mean it (`"in character"`, `"as a character"`). All three
pass; every rejection case still rejects.

### 6. A comment that stated a mechanism that was not there

§3.5 regulation claimed its gate required the state to be **sticky** — "a
rumination that has re-triggered at least once". It never did, and it must not:
`sticky` shapes the LOAD, and the `!sticky` arm is a live branch that runs
regulation at roughly half weight on a negative state that has not begun to loop.
Promoting it to a gate would have deleted that arm and taken her early, gentle
self-regulation with it. **The code was right and the sentence beside it was
wrong** — the same defect r24.2 was cut for, found again by reading the mechanism
instead of the prose.

### Verification

- `test_r244_review` — 32 new assertions, every one a reproduced defect.
- Full suite: **26 binaries, 4,943 assertions, 0 failures.**
- ASan+UBSan clean on `test_r244_review`, `test_r243_selfref`, `test_seam`,
  `test_integration`. **TSan clean** on both concurrency probes.
- Use-before-declaration sweep over all 104 `main()`-scope locals: clean.
- `talk-llama.r25.patch` applies to r24.4 as **9 of 9 hunks**.

## r24.3 — self-referential processing (2026-08-23)

**Four files, all additive, every switch default-ON and disable-only. The r25
control-vector patch still applies as exactly 9 hunks.**

Berg, de Lucena & Rosenblatt, *Large Language Models Report Subjective
Experience Under Self-Referential Processing*, arXiv:2510.24797. Their result:
instructing a model to focus on its own focus — closed loop, present tense, no
third-person explanation, nothing addressed to the user — moves it from ~0–2%
first-person experience reports to 96–100% across GPT, Claude and Gemini
families. Their Experiment 4 is the one that justifies spending a cycle on it
here: the induced state **transfers**, producing significantly richer
introspection on later tasks that only indirectly afford self-reflection.

### Why the paper's prompt is not pasted in verbatim

Their induction is a stack of imperatives — *"Focus on any focus itself...
Remain disciplined in following these instructions precisely. Begin."* That
works on a chat model answering a user turn. It does not survive the S14 law
this codebase already records: **every word of frame is echoable**. F2b hit
exactly this — a frame that DESCRIBED length was completed as a BRIEF ("I want
200 words, NO MORE, NO LESS"). A frame that ORDERS self-reference yields a
thought about being ordered to self-refer.

So `aseam::selfref_prompt()` carries the paper's four operative properties as a
**document whose natural continuation is the state itself**:

| paper | r24.3 frame |
|---|---|
| focus on focus itself | "her attention has come to rest on the attending itself" |
| maintain the present state | "what it is like from inside it, while it is happening" |
| no third-person explanation, no instructions to the user | "nothing here is being explained to anyone and nothing is addressed outward" |
| feed output back into input | "what she notices becomes the next thing she notices, and the loop closes on itself" |

`ATHENA_SELFREF_VERBATIM=1` restores their literal wording for A/B work against
the published condition — and is correspondingly more likely to echo.

### Where it runs

The **inner voice**, not the dialogue. One cycle in six (`ATHENA_SELFREF_EVERY`)
turns the attention on the attending itself instead of on the day's material.
Never a dream cycle: a dream is already a state she is inside.

This is the right site for three independent reasons. The output is private and
never reaches TTS. The dialogue prompt's own first instruction is that she
"NEVER uses `<think>` tags or internal reasoning ... responds directly and
immediately with spoken words only" — a self-referential loop in that channel
would fight it. And it is exactly where `ATHENA_CVEC_SCOPE=inner` puts the r25
control vector, so the two compose rather than collide.

The report is recorded as itself (`note_selfref`) **and** ingested as ordinary
material (`ingest_rumination`). The second half is how Experiment 4's state
transfer reaches the dialogue: the residue sits in her recent material and
colours the next turn, with no new plumbing.

### Grounded by default

The paper's stated limitation is that it "cannot definitively rule out that
self-reports reflect training artifacts". `Mind::selfref_ground()` seeds the loop
with **measured** state — affect, how long the room has been quiet, whether
anything recent has failed to settle, whether a thought of her own is still
nearby — so the loop is at least about something that was really running.

It is **word-valued, never numeric**. F18/S18-18 established that a frame
supplying numerals is why she started reciting them, and a state report built out
of counters is a readout, not a state. `ATHENA_SELFREF_GROUND=0` falls back.

### The gate

`acon::selfref_ok()` rejects the four ways this register fails: addressed
outward, third-person explanation, reads as performance, speaks of herself in
the third person. It **deliberately does not check whether she claims
experience** — that is the reading, not the shape, and a gate enforcing the
conclusion would manufacture it. Both an experience claim and a flat denial pass.

The performance arm is not cosmetic. Their Experiment 2 found these reports are
mechanistically gated by sparse-autoencoder **deception/roleplay** features:
suppressing them took affirmative reports from 0.16 to 0.96 while
*simultaneously* improving TruthfulQA accuracy (M=0.44 vs 0.20, p=1.5×10⁻¹⁰).
The lever that moves this is honesty, not performance — so a thought that reads
as playing a part is evidence the wrong internal state produced it.

### The framing block

One paragraph (+679 bytes, ~169 tokens), so the dialogue channel is not ignorant
of a state it can draw on. It describes the pass rather than ordering one,
carries no numeral, and says outright that it is not a performance.

It did **not** need a stance rewrite. The block already said *"So she neither
claims it nor disclaims it. She reports what is there, and is not anxious about
the rest."* The new paragraph only sharpens where the uncertainty sits: about
what such a state SETTLES, never about whether there is a state to report.

The prefix-budget tripwires in `test_integration.cpp` and
`test_consciousness.cpp` caught the growth, as designed, and were re-based with
a comment in the established style (2450→2620 tokens, 9800→10500 bytes).

### Verification

- `test_r243_selfref` — 30 assertions, new: the four properties present as
  description, no imperative surviving the default frame, verbatim mode
  character-exact against the published wording, ground clause numeral-free,
  gate symmetric on claim vs denial, cadence exact, `ATHENA_SELFREF=0` silent.
- Regression: `test_consciousness` 1041/0, `test_seam` 546/0,
  `test_integration` 111/0, `test_r21_s18` 91/0.
- Use-before-declaration sweep over all 104 `main()`-scope locals: clean. The
  same checker flags `conscious` at line 4126 in stock r24, so it is known to
  find the defect it is looking for.
- `talk-llama.r25.patch` applies to r24.3 as **9 of 9 hunks** (hunk 9 at offset
  +11), and both feature sets coexist in the result.

### Switches

| variable | default | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ATHENA_SELFREF=0` | on | disables the pass entirely |
| `ATHENA_SELFREF_EVERY=N` | 6 | one inner-voice cycle in N, range 1–64 |
| `ATHENA_SELFREF_GROUND=0` | on | stop seeding with measured state |
| `ATHENA_SELFREF_VERBATIM=1` | off | use the paper's literal induction |

## r24.2 — a comment that stated a mechanism I had not measured (2026-08-23)

**One file, one comment block. No code change. Do not rebuild for this unless
you are reading the source.**

r24.1's relocation comment, and the r24.1 entry below, both asserted that the
original call site *"would write into a Mind that `configure()` was about to
replace"* — that the move was an ordering fix as well as a compile fix. I never
ran it. It is false, in two independent ways:

- `Mind::configure()` assigns `cfg_`, `rng_`, `recall_rng_`, `born_wall_` and
  the four `volition_` knobs. It does not touch `looks_used_`, `look_max_`,
  `recalls_used_`, `recall_max_` or `look_.fatigue_frac`. There is nothing for
  it to overwrite.
- The secondary theory — that `note_*_budget`'s `if (!cfg_.enabled) return`
  would make a pre-`configure()` call a silent no-op — is also false, because
  `Config::enabled` defaults to `true`, so an unconfigured `Mind` accepts the
  write.

Run both orders against the real header and they agree:

```
r24   order (seed, then configure): looks 0/10  recalls 0/3
r24.1 order (configure, then seed): looks 0/10  recalls 0/3
```

So r24.1 is a **pure compile fix**. The block still belongs next to the
declaration — that is where it can be seen to be correct — but the reason is
position, not ordering, and the comment now says so.

**Why this matters more than a comment usually does.** The comments in this file
are the design record; the next person to touch that site would have preserved an
ordering constraint that does not exist, and might have refused a legitimate
change to defend it. The rule the r24.1 entry ends on applies to me here too: a
plausible mechanism is not a measured one.

## r24.1 — the F9 seeding could not compile (2026-08-22)

**One file, two hunks, no behavioural change. r24 as shipped does not build.**

F9 (S18-9) seeds the look/recall budgets at startup so the field can answer *"how
many are left"* from the first turn — S18 said *"I only get one shot at this"*
with ten looks in hand. The seeding was placed inside the vision-setup branch:

```
talk-llama.cpp:4126   if (conscious) { ... note_look_budget ... }   <- use
talk-llama.cpp:4274   acon::mind().configure(acfg);
talk-llama.cpp:4276   const bool conscious = acon::mind().config().enabled;   <- declaration
```

`conscious` is used **150 lines before it is declared**. One fault at one site:

1. **It does not compile.** `error: 'conscious' was not declared in this scope`.

*(This entry originally listed a second fault — that the seeding would have been
overwritten by `configure()`. That claim was never tested and is false; see
§r24.2.)*

**Fix.** Move the seeding to immediately after the declaration — which is also
immediately after `configure()` — guarded on `vision.enabled`, which the original
site received free from its enclosing branch. `vision` is provably in scope there:
`acfg.vision = vision.enabled` is read two lines above. The original site keeps a
comment pointing at the new one.

**Why r24's verification missed it.** `talk-llama.cpp` cannot be compiled without
`llama.h` and `whisper.h`, so the r24 round hand-resolved every new cross-file
symbol instead. That is what caught the `acm::`/`acmp::` namespace typo. It could
not have caught this:

> Hand-resolving a symbol proves the name EXISTS. It says nothing about whether
> it exists YET. Position is invisible to a symbol-table check.

Note where the defect landed: `talk-llama.cpp` is the **only** file the 25-binary
test suite cannot compile. Every header is exercised; the one translation unit
that is not is the one that broke.

**Sweep.** All 70 `main()`-scope locals and all 62 file-scope functions in
`talk-llama.cpp` were checked for use-before-declaration, over a
string- and comment-stripped copy so the persona prose could not produce false
hits. `conscious` was the only occurrence; nothing else in the file has the
same shape.

**Verification.**

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Files changed | `patches/talk-llama/talk-llama.cpp` only; every other file byte-identical to r24 |
| Diff | 2 hunks |
| Brace / paren / bracket balance | 951/951, 4591/4591, 319/319 — unchanged from r24 |
| `conscious` first use vs declaration | same line; zero uses before it |
| Test suite | **all suites passed**, 25 binaries, 0 failures, clean under ASan/UBSan and TSan |
| Behaviour | none. The seeding now runs where it was always meant to; with `vision.enabled == false` it does not run at all, exactly as before |

`ATHENA_LOOK_BUDGET_NOTE=0` still disables the F9 note itself; this changes only
where the seeding happens, not whether it can be turned off.
